metadata.note: AI-generated drafts (Ollama) refined for key bills (Claude). Display with an 'AI summary' label and a link to the official bill.

HB 1.summary: The bill would make it illegal to leave a firearm accessible to a child and would require certain firearm dealers to provide notice about this law. It also establishes exceptions and defenses against the offense.

HB 10.summary: The bill would strengthen protections for individuals who have not been convicted of crimes by prohibiting the disclosure of arrest booking photographs. It also provides procedures for removing these photos from pay-for-removal publications and websites.

HB 100.summary: This bill would require health insurers to pass along at least 80% of prescription drug rebates they receive from third parties to their enrollees.

HB 1000.summary: The bill would provide a one-time tax credit for individual taxpayers who filed income tax returns for the 2024 and 2025 taxable years.

HB 1001.summary: The bill would reduce the rate of income tax. It affects all taxpayers.

HB 1002.summary: The bill would change Medicaid coverage for foster children from managed care to fee-for-service.

HB 1003.summary: The bill would revise the provisions related to daily expense accounts for members of the General Assembly and provide them with an additional security expense allowance.

HB 1004.summary: The bill would allow the commissioner of public safety to provide security guards to the leaders of the Georgia Senate and House of Representatives and their families, as well as any member of the General Assembly who faces a credible threat to their safety.

HB 1005.summary: The bill would provide for a city manager in the City of Austell and revise the powers and duties of city council committees, the mayor, and department directors to reflect this change.

HB 1006.summary: This bill would require certain establishments to include an opioid antagonist in their first aid kits. It also allows individuals to possess these drugs on certain premises and trained personnel to administer them, providing immunity for those who do so.

HB 1008.summary: This bill would change how members of the General Assembly who live within 50 miles of the state capitol receive their allowances, making it so these allowances are paid through the legislative payroll system.

HB 1009.summary: This bill would require Georgia public schools to ban student access to personal electronic devices, such as phones and smartwatches, from the first bell to the last bell. Current law covers kindergarten through grade eight; the bill adds grades nine through twelve, starting no later than July 1, 2027. Schools must set storage, communication, and discipline rules. Students whose IEP, Section 504 Plan, or medical plan requires a device may use it.

HB 101.summary: This bill would require the state to publish an annual report detailing the amount of prescription drug rebates and other price reductions that are used to lower health insurance premiums for state employees.

HB 1010.summary: This bill would require annual reports on the value of securities sold or offered for sale. It also sets fees and makes controlling private funds jointly and severally liable for the liabilities of target firms they acquire.

HB 1011.summary: The bill would require law enforcement agencies to adopt written policies for vehicular pursuits in residential areas, establish pursuit review committees, and mandate annual reporting and training.

HB 1012.summary: This bill would stop local governments from building or developing new data centers for a certain period of time. It also includes an exception and defines a term related to data centers.

HB 1013.summary: This bill would designate lemon pepper as the official Georgia state chicken wing flavor.

HB 1014.summary: This bill would stop private and public primary and secondary schools from serving or selling food or drinks that contain certain synthetic dyes. It also stops third parties from doing so on school property.

HB 1015.summary: The bill would revise certain funded levels of the Self-insurers Guaranty Trust Fund related to workers' compensation.

HB 1016.summary: The bill would expand the remedies available in magistrate courts for cases involving unauthorized possession of real property. It affects people who are subject to removal or arrest for unauthorized possession of property.

HB 1017.summary: The bill would stop certain business types from buying or getting an interest in single-family homes. It also sets rules for how these properties are taxed.

HB 1018.summary: The bill would exempt sales of clothing and school-related supplies from sales and use taxes during the month of August each year.

HB 1019.summary: This bill would set limits on rent increases for certain senior citizens. It affects landlords and tenants.

HB 102.summary: The bill would establish the Georgia Quality Reporting Project within the Department of Community Health. It would define the project's purposes, create a working group, and set rules for submitting and processing clinical data with claims data. It also includes penalties for violations.

HB 1440.summary: This bill would create a homestead tax exemption for residents of Bryan County, Georgia, based on the difference between the current year's assessed value and the base year's assessed value of their home for school district taxes.

HR 1048.summary: This resolution urges the General Assembly to consider and adopt the Georgia Bereaved Parents and Family Support Act of 2026, which would provide job-protected bereavement leave for parents who lose a child.

HR 118.summary: This resolution compensates Mr. Michael Woolfolk.

HR 119.summary: This resolution directs the Department of Administrative Services to pay Mario Stinchcomb $975,000 for his wrongful murder conviction, for which he was exonerated in 2021. He would get an initial $321,750, with the rest paid in monthly installments over ten years starting in 2026. The state would get a credit for any damages he wins in a related lawsuit, and the payment would be excluded from his state taxable income.

HR 128.summary: This resolution compensates Mr. Joseph Samuel Watkins.

HR 129.summary: This resolution compensates Mr. Daryl Lee Clark.

HR 130.summary: This resolution would compensate Mr. Sedrick Moore.

HR 1427.summary: This resolution urges Congress to pass the Thiokol Memorial Gold Medal Act.

HR 1474.summary: This resolution encourages the creation of a life sciences caucus in the Georgia House of Representatives.

HR 1791.summary: This resolution urges the federal government to create a national data protection authority.

HR 1858.summary: This resolution urges Georgia's congressional delegation to pass the Essential Worker Pay Protection Act and to provide permanent protections for essential federal employees during government shutdowns.

HR 276.summary: This resolution commemorates the Equal Rights Amendment as the law of the land and ratifies a proposed amendment to the United States Constitution.

HR 67.summary: This resolution supports Georgia's goals for clean energy, workforce development, and creating green jobs by the year 2050.

HR 884.summary: This resolution urges the federal government to give states more power to create new ways to encourage people to work and to change programs that help people who are not working.

HB 1007.summary: This bill would allow residential tenants to make repairs that the landlord is supposed to make and deduct the cost from their rent under certain conditions. It also gives tenants the right to end their rental agreement under certain circumstances.

HB 1020.summary: The bill would allow district attorneys to receive monthly retirement benefits from the Georgia Judicial Retirement System at the age of 65.

HB 1021.summary: The bill would increase the amount of funds the authority is allowed to keep for administrative costs.

HB 1022.summary: The bill would ban electric tinting on vehicles and digital license plates. It also sets penalties for these violations.

HB 1023.summary: The bill requires local school boards to use weapon detection systems in certain school buildings to prevent individuals from unlawfully possessing or carrying weapons.

HB 1024.summary: The bill would revise the exemption for a debtor's interest in real or personal property used as a residence, including cooperative property and burial plots, in bankruptcy and intestate insolvent estates.

HB 1025.summary: The bill would provide funding for the child in need of services (CHINS) program through a new CHINS Support Fund, with the Department of Education overseeing the fund. It also establishes a regional coordination system for the program.

HB 1026.summary: The bill sets the compensation for members of the City of Valdosta Board of Education.

HB 1027.summary: This bill would allow certain long-term contracts for the sale of electric power in counties and municipalities.

HB 1028.summary: The bill would change how district attorneys are paid and how their salaries are calculated.

HB 1029.summary: This bill would revise the boundaries of the City of Holly Springs in Cherokee County, change the city council from five to four members, and provide new district boundaries for the city council. It also includes provisions for the current council members to continue in office and specifies effective dates.

HB 103.summary: The bill would increase the homestead exemption and raise the income cap for certain residents of Troup County's school district who are 65 years of age or older and have incomes not exceeding $22,000.

HB 1030.summary: This bill would require the State Board of Education to create content standards for advanced math courses in middle and high schools and mandate local education agencies to offer these courses.

HB 1031.summary: The bill would set limitations on how much landlords can increase rent on residential properties.

HB 1032.summary: This bill would allow students who have completed pre-kindergarten or kindergarten at a private school to enroll in public school early, even if they do not meet the usual age requirements for kindergarten or first grade. It also requires the State Board of Education to create guidelines and a model policy for early enrollment.

HB 1033.summary: This bill would require insurance coverage for diagnostic testing and treatment related to Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.

HB 1034.summary: This bill would require financial institutions to allow customers to place emergency holds on suspected fraudulent transactions. It also amends laws related to selling and trade practices, and forgery and fraud.

HB 1035.summary: This bill would stop local governments from adding unpaid service charges to the tax roll for tax execution or sale of a home that is owner-occupied.

HB 1036.summary: This bill would allow homeowners in communities governed by property owners' or homeowners' associations to vote on whether to continue or dissolve these associations. It also sets rules for transparency and nonretaliation.

HB 1037.summary: The bill would change the compensation of judges in the State Court of Cobb County.

HB 1038.summary: The bill would repeal the Georgia Promise Scholarship Act and hold a referendum to ask voters if they want to keep or repeal the act.

HB 1039.summary: The bill would create a fund to provide state investment in impoverished communities across Georgia and establish criteria for disbursements from this fund.

HB 104.summary: The bill would create the 'Equal Athletic Opportunities Act' to prevent discrimination based on sex in interscholastic athletic activities and events. It aims to ensure fair and safe competition for students.

HB 1040.summary: This bill would prohibit smoking within 25 feet of any state and local government buildings or enclosed public places. It also bans smoking in certain workplaces that were previously exempt.

HB 1041.summary: This bill would make changes to how quickly child custody and visitation modification hearings are handled in certain situations.

HB 1042.summary: The bill would allow certain buyers at judicial sales to submit a credit bid and remove restrictions on personally identifiable information after the death of a protected person. It also provides for the qualification of special masters in certain quiet title actions.

HB 1043.summary: This bill would create a unified, trauma-informed statewide system to address youth trafficking. It would establish a state-wide care coordination office and provide training in hospitals, schools, and other relevant organizations.

HB 1044.summary: The bill would provide remedies for state citizens whose constitutional rights are deprived by civil immigration enforcement officers. It would also define terms and provide a short title.

HB 1045.summary: The bill would require public schools that issue student identification badges to include information about the 9-8-8 crisis response hotline on these badges.

HB 1046.summary: The bill would restrict the powers of business corporations, nonprofit corporations, partnerships, limited partnerships, and limited liability companies to only those explicitly granted by the General Assembly.

HB 1047.summary: The bill would revise the definition of the term 'municipality' in the water and sewer projects and costs tax law.

HB 1048.summary: The bill would require the State Board of Education to create criteria for assessing and placing students who are eligible to start first grade. It also allows parents or guardians to choose to enroll their children in kindergarten instead of first grade.

HB 1049.summary: The bill would limit criminal penalties and civil damages for donors and gleaners who donate food and for organizations that accept food donations.

HB 105.summary: The bill would increase the indemnification award for certain state public school personnel in the event of death.

HB 1050.summary: The bill would amend a law to protect student data from immigration officials under certain conditions and require each school district to designate an administrator to handle interactions with immigration enforcement.

HB 1051.summary: This bill would require local school systems to have written agreements with law enforcement when employing officers in schools. It also prohibits law enforcement officers from handling school disciplinary matters unless there is criminal conduct or an immediate safety threat.

HB 1052.summary: This bill would create a financial aid program to help eligible students with off-campus housing costs. The program would provide grants to students to assist with these expenses.

HB 1053.summary: The bill would repeal laws that require local law enforcement to cooperate with federal immigration authorities and verify individuals' immigration status.

HB 1054.summary: This bill would require businesses in Georgia to warn people if they are exposed to chemicals known to cause cancer or reproductive harm. It also requires businesses to avoid discharging these chemicals into drinking water.

HB 1055.summary: This bill would stop certain entities from owning 25 or more single-family homes. It also requires these entities to file information with the Secretary of State and allows for inspections. The Attorney General and private individuals can take legal action if the rules are broken.

HB 1056.summary: The bill would change the term 'auto-injectable epinephrine' to 'epinephrine' in student health laws and combine related provisions about epinephrine in schools.

HB 1057.summary: This bill would add an eighth judge to the State Court of Gwinnett County starting January 1, 2027, and a ninth judge starting January 1, 2028.

HB 1058.summary: This bill would allow tax-exempt organizations to be beneficiaries of employee group life insurance policies.

HB 1059.summary: This bill would prohibit the construction or development of new data centers for a specified period and create the Data Center Impact Assessment Commission to evaluate the impact of data centers.

HB 106.summary: This bill would allow local school boards to offer driver education training as an elective course in public schools. Funding for the course would come from local funds, student fees, and state funding if appropriated.

HB 1060.summary: The bill would limit the authority of law enforcement officers in certain situations and restrict their use of deadly force. It also prohibits law enforcement officers from wearing face coverings.

HB 1061.summary: The bill would enact the 'Mandi Ballinger Act' and change the jurisdiction of juvenile court to include certain 17-year-olds. It also establishes an implementation committee with specific powers and composition.

HB 1062.summary: The bill would require the Georgia Department of Education to publish relevant federal guidance documents and related information. It also requires the State School Superintendent to send an annual notice to certain committees and offices.

HB 1063.summary: This bill would require electric utilities to protect residential and retail electricity customers from costs related to data center construction and operation.

HB 1064.summary: The bill would add the Classic Learning Test (CLT) as an option for standardized college admissions tests, alongside the SAT and ACT, for students in Georgia.

HB 1065.summary: This bill would provide a $100,000 homestead exemption from City of West Point ad valorem taxes for residents who are 65 years old or older and have an income of $50,000 or less.

HB 1066.summary: The bill would provide immunity from public and private nuisance claims for certain conditions and changes in historical operating schedules.

HB 1067.summary: This bill would provide a $10,000 homestead exemption from City of West Point ad valorem taxes for residents of that city.

HB 1068.summary: The bill would provide additional funding for office expenses and constituent services for members of the Georgia General Assembly. It also establishes the Office of Constituent Services, sets its duties, and outlines funding and staffing procedures.

HB 1069.summary: The bill would require the Department of Public Health to publish and maintain statistical reports about induced terminations of pregnancy, even if these reports might otherwise be confidential for physician privacy.

HB 107.summary: This bill would allow the issuance of digitally verifiable licenses for spouses of military service members, spouses of transitioning service members, and transitioning military service members.

HB 1070.summary: The bill would increase and extend an income tax credit for expenditures on maintaining railroad track owned or leased by Class III railroads.

HB 1071.summary: This bill would provide protections for employees from occupational heat exposure and allow for rules and regulations to be established by the Department of Labor.

HB 1072.summary: The bill would allow the director of the Environmental Protection Division to look into and consider an applicant's regulatory history from other states when processing certain permit applications.

HB 1073.summary: The bill would establish a specialty license plate to honor Jackson State University, with proceeds from the plates going to the general fund and the university.

HB 1074.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from ad valorem taxes for residents of the City of Suwanee.

HB 1075.summary: The bill would change the penalty for people previously convicted of trafficking persons for labor or sexual servitude if they are later convicted of a sexual offense.

HB 1076.summary: This bill would create a felony offense for obstructing a law enforcement officer with a motor vehicle.

HB 1077.summary: The bill would extend the sunset date for an exemption from sales and use taxes for tickets, fees, and admission charges to certain museums and fine arts performances or exhibitions at nonprofit facilities.

HB 1078.summary: The bill would require periodic review and automatic expiration of agency rules under the Georgia Administrative Procedure Act. It also mandates that agencies prepare reports and follow specific procedures for these reviews.

HB 1079.summary: The bill would revise the expiration and transferability of tax credits for the rehabilitation of historic structures. It also provides for reversion and reporting requirements.

HB 108.summary: The bill would provide protections for veterans and other eligible persons applying for benefits under the Fair Business Practices Act of 1975. It also includes provisions for violations and sets a short title for the act.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

HB 1080.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Public Safety Support Fund to provide support to law enforcement agencies and courts. It would also establish a board of trustees for the fund.

HB 1081.summary: The bill would amend laws to include adults with cognitive decline as disabled adults, providing definitions and related provisions.

HB 1082.summary: This bill would designate November 7 of each year as Victims of Communism Day and require public school students to receive related instruction.

HB 1083.summary: This bill would allow the Magistrate Court in Madison County to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover funds once the fee is no longer collected.

HB 1084.summary: This bill would allow the Probate Court of Madison County to charge a technology fee and specify how the money can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover funds once the fee is no longer collected.

HB 1085.summary: The bill would provide tax credits for forestry manufacturing facilities. It also includes provisions for transferring tax credits and reporting requirements.

HB 1086.summary: The bill would require certain buildings to post notices about the use of light-frame truss-type construction for firefighter safety. It also provides for rules, regulations, and enforcement.

HB 1087.summary: The bill would stop counties, cities, and other government groups from charging disabled veterans certain fees when they make home improvements to accommodate their disabilities.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

HB 1088.summary: This bill would change the term 'chiropractor' to 'chiropractic physician' in Georgia's laws. It also allows professional corporations to be jointly owned by chiropractic physicians and physicians.

HB 1089.summary: The bill would allow ivermectin to be sold as an over-the-counter medication in Georgia. It would remove ivermectin from the list of dangerous drugs and provide definitions related to this change.

HB 109.summary: The bill would create a five-year pilot program to establish emergency psychiatric assessment, treatment, and healing units (EmPATH units) in hospitals.

HB 1090.summary: This bill would change how county commissioners in Echols County are elected, making it so all commissioners are elected from the entire county instead of from specific districts.

HB 1091.summary: This bill would allow a nonbinding referendum in Brantley County to ask voters if they support a perimeter highway bypass around Waycross.

HB 1092.summary: This bill extends the life of the Chehaw Park Authority, a local authority created by a 1979 law. Under the bill, the authority would continue to exist through December 31, 2036.

HB 1093.summary: This bill would allow a nonbinding referendum in Ware County to ask voters if they support building a perimeter highway bypass around Waycross.

HB 1094.summary: The bill would revise how the State Board of Education calculates and distributes funds for student transportation programs to local school units. It also sets priorities for grants and includes legislative findings and definitions.

HB 1095.summary: This bill would allow permanent consumer fireworks sales facilities and increase the number of temporary retail fireworks sales facilities a distributor can operate. It also revises penalties for violations of fireworks regulations.

HB 1096.summary: This bill would allow certain employees of a county board of health to keep their accrued annual and sick leave if they become employees of the Department of Public Health.

HB 1097.summary: The bill would require criminal background, license status, and registry checks for owners, applicants, and employees of certain mental health facilities. It also directs the Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Disabilities to submit fingerprints to federal and state agencies for these background checks.

HB 1098.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Investment Act Pilot Fund and a Joint Legislative Oversight Commission to oversee state investment in underdeveloped communities across Georgia.

HB 1099.summary: The bill would require an evaluation of blind or visually impaired students to determine their need for Braille instruction and mandate Braille instruction in their Individualized Education Programs.

HB 11.summary: The bill would require long-term care facilities to have enough staff to provide food and nutrition services, including hiring a licensed dietitian and designating a director of food and nutrition services.

HB 110.summary: The bill would provide protections for current military members and related persons when dealing with pawnbrokers. It would also prohibit pawnbrokers from making title pawns with covered borrowers and set penalties for violations.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

HB 1100.summary: This bill would create a new special sales tax that local governments could use for healthcare purposes. It also sets rules for this tax and how it affects other taxes.

HB 1101.summary: This bill would provide a state-wide homestead tax exemption for a portion of the value of the homestead for certain senior residents.

HB 1102.summary: This bill would prevent the levy and sale of properties owned by certain senior citizens for failure to pay ad valorem taxes.

HB 1103.summary: The bill would establish the Happy Highways Grant Program to provide grants for murals and signs along the state highway system, allowing up to two murals per county.

HB 1104.summary: The bill would prohibit certain medical examinations on unconscious patients or patients under anesthesia without prior informed consent or authorization. It also states that informed consent is valid for all medical personnel under certain conditions.

HB 1105.summary: This bill would provide an exemption from ad valorem taxation for education purposes for the homesteads of individuals who are 65 years of age or older.

HB 1106.summary: The bill would create a Nursing Home Supplemental Fund and set rules for its administration, eligibility, and application process.

HB 1107.summary: The bill would require the Professional Standards Commission to develop and report annual performance measures for each educator preparation provider in the state. These measures must include certain minimum contents.

HB 1108.summary: The bill would change the state-wide system for voting equipment to require hand-marked and hand-counted paper ballots. It also moves the responsibility for certifying and selecting this system from the Secretary of State to the State Election Board.

HB 1109.summary: The bill would change the types of driver's licenses and identification cards that voters can use to prove their identity at polling places.

HB 111.summary: This bill lowers Georgia's individual income tax rate to 5.19 percent, down from 5.39 percent, for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025. The rate would then drop by 0.10 percent each year until it reaches 4.99 percent. A yearly drop is delayed a year if state revenue estimates, past revenue collections, or the Revenue Shortfall Reserve fail set tests as of December 1. The Office of Planning and Budget makes that call.

HB 1110.summary: This bill would create a tax credit for employers that offer individual coverage health reimbursement arrangements to their employees in Georgia.

HB 1111.summary: This bill would create a new local option sales tax dedicated to healthcare purposes. It would define the tax, authorize its implementation, and specify how local referenda can authorize the tax. It also prohibits taxing products ordered and delivered outside the jurisdiction.

HB 1112.summary: This bill would allow rounding the total price of goods or services when paying with legal tender. It also provides tax exemptions and definitions related to this practice.

HB 1113.summary: The bill would exclude part-time students from membership in the Georgia Defined Contribution Plan.

HB 1114.summary: This bill would allow ninth and tenth grade students to complete the financial literacy course required for high school graduation.

HB 1115.summary: This bill would prohibit institutional investors and other enterprises from owning or controlling more than 2,000 single-family residences. It also allows individuals to sue those who violate this limit.

HB 1116.summary: The bill would allow tax digests to be accepted if there is a publication error by a newspaper. It also excludes certain amounts from financing under the 'Quality Basic Education Act'.

HB 1117.summary: The bill would change how motor vehicle liability insurance policies handle claims for repairs, including rules on selecting repair facilities and making payments. It also sets guidelines for unfair claims settlement practices and requires certain disclosures and notifications.

HB 1118.summary: The bill would provide 80 hours of maternal birth leave for public officers and employees. It also includes definitions, rules, penalties, and notice requirements related to this leave.

HB 1119.summary: This bill would establish guidelines for pharmacy care and pharmacy management networks under workers' compensation. It would also set limitations for providers prescribing and dispensing certain medications and provide for reimbursement.

HB 112.summary: This bill would give a one-time refund, applied as a tax credit, to Georgia individual income taxpayers who filed returns for both 2023 and 2024. The refund equals the lesser of their 2023 Georgia income tax or a set amount: $250 for single filers and married people filing separately, $375 for heads of household, and $500 for joint filers. Nonresident aliens, estates, and trusts are excluded, as are most people claimed as dependents in 2023.

HB 1120.summary: This bill would allow the electors of Union County to vote in an advisory referendum on whether to change the county's governing authority from a sole commissioner to a five-member board of commissioners.

HB 1121.summary: The bill would change certain terms of court in the Cordele Judicial Circuit.

HB 1122.summary: Starting January 1, 2027, this bill would require health insurance plans, the state health benefit plan, and Medicaid to cover a peripheral artery disease screening test at least once every 12 months for people at higher risk, such as those 65 or older. Coverage would follow each plan's usual deductibles and copays. The state plan and Medicaid parts take effect only if funds are appropriated.

HB 1123.summary: This bill would require schools that offer after-school programs to make these programs available to pre-kindergarten students on the same basis as other students. It also allows for limited exceptions to this requirement.

HB 1124.summary: This bill would require certain state agencies to consider the definition of hinduphobia when applying laws and regulations that prohibit discrimination based on race, color, religion, or national origin. It also allows judges in criminal cases to consider hinduphobia when deciding if a defendant had a specific intent.

HB 1125.summary: The bill would add independent filmmakers to the list of entities eligible to claim tax credits for qualified production activities under the Georgia Entertainment Industry Investment Act.

HB 1126.summary: HB 1126 would create an income tax credit for production companies that spend money on certain state-certified productions. It also sets rules and an application process for this tax credit.

HB 1127.summary: The bill would create a new offense for possessing parts of a machine gun and set punishment for this crime. It also provides an exemption from this offense.

HB 1128.summary: This bill would require the State Board of Workers' Compensation to notify the legal guardian of an injured employee about their eligibility for compensation.

HB 1129.summary: The bill would change how enterprise zones are designated and would prevent them from being exempt from state sales and use tax, with some exceptions. It also sets rules for collecting fees and using revenue bonds, and limits the number of enterprise zones in urban redevelopment areas.

HB 113.summary: This bill would stop the state of Georgia and its agencies from buying goods from certain foreign countries or related entities. It would also create a list of such goods and set penalties for violations.

HB 1130.summary: The bill would amend laws about government transparency and campaign finance to set a time period for candidates or campaign committee treasurers to comply with requests to inspect accounts and to specify penalties for not complying. It also defines certain security-related expenses as campaign expenses.

HB 1131.summary: The bill would require personal service of process for notice of a warrant application hearing.

HB 1132.summary: This bill would exempt materials used in the construction, renovation, and rehabilitation of affordable housing by purely public charities from state and local sales and use taxes.

HB 1133.summary: The bill would allow the Georgia Environmental Finance Authority to finance and perform duties related to projects that help install solar panels on closed landfills.

HB 1134.summary: The bill would revise the notice requirements for repossessors of motor vehicles and provide requirements for determining when a repossession is complete.

HB 1135.summary: This bill would allow Georgia to participate in a federal tax credit program for contributions to scholarship granting organizations. It also stops state agencies from making rules or regulations about this program.

HB 1136.summary: The bill would prohibit smoking and disposing of smoking products within 25 feet of playgrounds and sandboxes, and also prohibit smoking within 250 feet of youth sports events.

HB 1137.summary: This bill would extend the expiration date for local governing bodies to collect a 1 percent retail sales and use tax for the Metropolitan Atlanta Rapid Transit Authority (MARTA).

HB 1138.summary: This bill would allow pharmacists to dispense self-administered hormonal contraceptives and administer injectable hormonal contraceptives under certain conditions. It also requires insurance to provide a minimum amount of certain contraceptives.

HB 1139.summary: The bill would rename the Spalding County Water and Sewerage Facilities Authority, change its membership and compensation, and revise its powers and enforcement procedures. It also provides for the collection of rates and charges.

HB 114.summary: The bill would update the reference date to federal regulations regarding the safe operation of motor carriers and commercial motor vehicles in Georgia's laws.

HB 1140.summary: This bill would allow the Magistrate Court of Ben Hill County to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover funds once the fee is no longer collected.

HB 1141.summary: The bill would allow a parent or legal guardian to obtain medical records when a child is taken into medical custody.

HB 1142.summary: This bill would require certain agreements for certain offenses to be eligible for a Pretrial Intervention and Diversion Program. It also provides for the creation of a registry of recidivist domestic violence offenders and for the maintenance of such registry.

HB 1143.summary: This bill would require menstrual products sold in Georgia to be free of certain restricted substances. It would also mandate ingredient labeling on packaging and set up a phased compliance schedule for manufacturers.

HB 1144.summary: This bill would eliminate state sales and use taxes on menstrual hygiene products for certain weekends. The state revenue commissioner would designate these tax-free weekends, and the Department of Revenue would publish the dates.

HB 1145.summary: This bill would provide a state-wide homestead exemption from ad valorem taxes for certain public service employees. The exemption would cover the amount by which the current year's assessed value of a homestead exceeds its base year value.

HB 1146.summary: The bill would create a pilot program to expand Georgia's Pre-K Program to include three-year-old children. It also requires annual reporting on the program.

HB 1147.summary: The bill would create a grant program to increase reimbursement rates for childcare providers who participate in the Childcare and Parent Services (CAPS) program.

HB 1148.summary: The bill would revise tax credits for donating real property for conservation purposes. It also changes required filings and the total amount of tax credits allowed, and extends the deadline for accepting new applications.

HB 1149.summary: This bill would require certain health insurers to offer a preenrollment option for anticipated newly born or adopted children. It also provides for the provision of routine well baby care in certain circumstances.

HB 115.summary: This bill would require the Department of Natural Resources to provide certain notices upon the registration of a vessel. It also allows the department to perform unattended vessel checks and to seek restitution for the cost of removing, storing, and disposing of abandoned vessels.

HB 1150.summary: The bill would expand the prescriptive authorizations for advanced practice registered nurses and physician assistants, remove certain restrictions on writing prescriptions for minors, and allow for the ordering of stimulants under certain conditions.

HB 1151.summary: The bill would expand Medicaid in Georgia by amending the medical assistance laws and allowing the Department of Community Health to submit a waiver request for a state plan amendment for Medicaid expansion.

HB 1152.summary: This bill would allow individuals to deduct certain health insurance premium payments from their income tax. It also sets income-based limits on the deduction.

HB 1153.summary: This bill would provide a tax credit for residential contractors or builders who construct new homes and sell them to taxpayers earning up to 80 percent of the area median income.

HB 1154.summary: The bill would include the offense of trafficking persons for labor or sexual servitude as a crime that can result in the death penalty.

HB 1155.summary: This bill changes how Tift County's board of commissioners handles purchasing. The board is the county's purchasing agent. Purchasing and bidding would follow a policy the board adopts, replacing the current provisions in the county's 1917 act.

HB 1156.summary: This bill would allow local governments to create grant programs to give incentives to homeowners. It also allows the establishment of local funds for these homeowner incentive grants.

HB 1157.summary: The bill would repeal certain provisions in Georgia's minimum wage law that prevent local governments from setting their own wage and employment benefit mandates.

HB 1158.summary: The bill would change how the state government refers to the western bank of the Jordan River, calling it Judea and Samaria.

HB 1159.summary: This bill would exempt from income tax all income received by individuals, corporations, and partnerships under the Farmer Bridge Assistance Program of the United States Department of Agriculture.

HB 116.summary: The bill would change the name of the Motor Carrier Compliance Division of the Department of Public Safety to Commercial Vehicle Enforcement and require law enforcement officers within this division to be trained, sworn, and certified.

HB 1160.summary: This bill would amend the rules for when the statute of limitations is paused in wrongful death lawsuits, affecting surviving relatives.

HB 1161.summary: This bill would change how drivers should behave when an emergency vehicle or a police car is approaching for a traffic stop.

HB 1162.summary: This bill would require corporations and limited liability companies, along with their subsidiaries, to provide information to the Secretary of State if they own a certain number of multifamily residences.

HB 1163.summary: This bill would exempt the primary residences of health care providers from medical malpractice lawsuits. It also provides exceptions to this exemption.

HB 1164.summary: The bill would require the State Board of Education to appoint an audit committee and set minimum responsibilities for the committee. It also revises provisions for financial audits of local school systems by the Department of Audits and Accounts.

HB 1165.summary: This bill would require the Department of Community Affairs to create a list of state-owned real property that can be used for community gardens in certain municipalities. It also sets requirements for establishing and maintaining these community gardens and allows municipalities to fund them.

HB 1166.summary: This bill would prevent zoning decisions from affecting or being required for residential dwellings that are 400 square feet or smaller.

HB 1167.summary: This bill would designate the second week in March of each year as 'Sleep Health Awareness Week' in Georgia and encourage the Department of Public Health to provide sleep hygiene education.

HB 1168.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from Heard County school district ad valorem taxes for residents who are 70 years old or older.

HB 1169.summary: This bill would allow the Probate Court of Spalding County to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used.

HB 117.summary: The bill would require food service establishments to notify customers of the country of origin for seafood items.

HB 1170.summary: The bill would allow the State Court of Spalding County to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used.

HB 1171.summary: This bill would establish minimum habitability standards for rental housing and prohibit landlords from waiving these standards. It also clarifies existing duties of landlords.

HB 1172.summary: This bill would allow the Magistrate Court of Spalding County to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used.

HB 1173.summary: The bill would provide limited bereavement leave and extended compassionate leave for certain employees under specific conditions. It also prohibits certain employer actions and provides a cause of action and remedy for violations.

HB 1174.summary: The bill would provide retraining and other support for federal employees who lose their jobs. It also requires coordination between the Georgia Department of Labor, the Technical College System of Georgia, and the University System of Georgia.

HB 1175.summary: The bill would create a new crime called theft by shoplifting of essential items and set penalties for it. It also allows for prosecution by citation and defines the offense.

HB 1176.summary: This bill would exempt from sales and use taxes the sale of tangible personal property used or consumed in the generation, transmission, distribution, sale, or furnishing of electricity.

HB 1177.summary: This bill would allow development authorities to undertake projects that include affordable housing uses of property.

HB 1178.summary: The bill would establish the Budget and Fiscal Affairs Oversight Committee of the House of Representatives, set out its duties, and provide for member allowances and audits.

HB 1179.summary: The bill would remove a revenue threshold requirement for local governments to change the designation of a private nonprofit organization that promotes tourism, conventions, and trade shows in their jurisdiction.

HB 118.summary: The bill would revise requirements for child care learning centers and family child care learning homes, including the need to have at least one portable airway clearance device and CPR-certified employees.

HB 1180.summary: The bill would eliminate the outstanding bond limit for the Georgia Housing and Finance Authority and provide that bonds issued by the authority are backed by the full faith and credit of the state.

HB 1181.summary: This bill would require an application for a certificate of title for a motor vehicle to include the last certificate of title from another state if the vehicle was previously registered in that state and the applicant is receiving the vehicle through inheritance, devise, or bequest.

HB 1182.summary: The bill would add more prohibited acts related to soil amendments in agriculture.

HB 1183.summary: This bill would exempt from Georgia state income tax the personal compensation received by individuals for full-time duty in the active military service of the United States.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

HB 1184.summary: The bill would treat retired military officers the same as warrant officers and enlisted personnel for transferring to the state retired list at the grade they earned during their service.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

HB 1185.summary: This bill would require certain shareholder claims to be heard by the Georgia State-wide Business Court. It also allows a corporation's bylaws or articles of incorporation to specify that certain claims must be heard by this court.

HB 1186.summary: The bill would repeal the Act that created the Garden City Area Convention and Visitors Bureau Authority and address the assets and liabilities of the authority.

HB 1187.summary: The bill would prohibit contracts or agreements that aim to hide details of childhood sexual abuse claims. It also aims to keep the identifying information of victims confidential.

HB 1188.summary: The bill would require landlords to disclose the total rental price of residential properties and prohibit hidden fees. It affects landlords and tenants.

HB 1189.summary: This bill would stop the prosecution of sodomy between consenting adults.

HB 119.summary: The bill would revise the standards for bringing a legal action against the government for unauthorized acts related to weapon regulation under the Brady Law.

HB 1190.summary: This bill would allow students to advise the State Board of Education and local boards of education, and would invite the Georgia Teacher of the Year to advise the State Board of Education.

HB 1191.summary: This bill would add more military medal awards that qualify for special veteran license plates and create a specialty license plate for United States Navy submarine service members.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

HB 1192.summary: The bill would change accounting practices for the Department of Human Services and the Department of Community Health related to public assistance. It also sets aside funds for specific purposes, requires annual reviews, and mandates annual reports.

HB 1193.summary: This bill creates the "Georgia Early Literacy Act of 2026." Subject to state funding, it would let the State Board of Education give grants to local school systems to pay for one school-based literacy coach in each school with any of grades kindergarten through three. Schools with 200 or fewer full-time students would get 50 percent of that amount. It would also have regional educational service agencies employ regional literacy coaches, and it would substantially revise the "Georgia Early Literacy and Dyslexia Act."

HB 1194.summary: This bill would clarify the periods of time for transportation network company services in Georgia's insurance requirements for these companies and their drivers.

HB 1195.summary: The bill would revise the rules for veterinarians and veterinary technicians to practice and provide veterinary teletriage and telemedicine.

HB 1196.summary: The bill would create a new offense called criminal trespass involving a wild animal and provide penalties for this offense.

HB 1197.summary: This bill would allow certain billiards and darts tournaments and their prizes under the Georgia Lottery for Education Act.

HB 1198.summary: This bill would allow for a limited license to offer or sell insurance for portable electronics and consumer goods. It would also revise definitions and make conforming changes.

HB 1199.summary: The bill would revise the definitions of 'Internal Revenue Code' and 'Internal Revenue Code of 1986' in Georgia law to incorporate certain provisions of federal law.

HB 12.summary: The bill would change the definition of a 'qualified local school system' for equalization grants, lowering the minimum required millage rate from 14 mills to 10 mills. It also sets a 25 percent reduction in grant awards for systems that do not meet this new rate.

HB 120.summary: The bill would amend Georgia law to define terms related to firearms, ammunition, and other weapons, and it would prohibit the enforcement of federal extreme risk protection orders in the state and the acceptance of federal funds related to these orders.

HB 1200.summary: The bill would prevent any increases in the adjusted base year assessed value of properties above the value set in tax year 2025 for a homestead exemption from Chatham County and City of Savannah School District ad valorem taxes.

HB 1201.summary: The bill would require new dwellings and dwelling units to comply with safety standards for smoke detectors and set a staggered timeline for compliance.

HB 1202.summary: The bill would correct a writing error in a reference within the law about the Georgia Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Advisory Board.

HB 1203.summary: This bill changes how Chatham County homeowners get a school district property tax exemption created by a 2025 law. Anyone who, as of December 31, 2026, has applied for and is eligible for the existing 1999 homestead exemption from Chatham County and City of Savannah school district taxes would automatically qualify for the 2025 exemption. They would not need to apply separately.

HB 1204.summary: The bill would change the age at which individuals are protected from age discrimination in employment.

HB 1205.summary: This bill would provide a new charter for the City of Yatesville, outlining its incorporation, boundaries, and powers.

HB 1206.summary: This bill would require local boards of education and other public school governing bodies to consider the total cost of ownership and related factors when purchasing school technology devices.

HB 1207.summary: The bill would create a registry of people who repeatedly commit domestic violence. It would require court clerks to give information to the Georgia Crime Information Center and charge fees for registration.

HB 1208.summary: This bill would require depositions in Georgia to be taken by certified court reporters instead of being recorded by stenographic means.

HB 1209.summary: The bill would provide a sales and use tax exemption for purchases of tangible property and construction materials used in the construction and furnishing of certain buildings.

HB 121.summary: The bill would prohibit public officers or employees from enforcing or helping to enforce federal laws or actions that infringe on the right to keep and bear arms.

HB 1210.summary: The bill would provide protections for children who adopt an identity that differs from their sex in dependency proceedings and child abuse cases.

HB 1211.summary: The bill would provide guidelines and recommendations for colorectal cancer screening, examinations, and laboratory tests through insurance.

HB 1212.summary: This bill would impose an excise tax on certain proceeds from judgments and settlements intended for the cleanup of PFAS contamination but not used for that purpose. It also provides for exceptions, notice requirements, and payment procedures.

HB 1213.summary: This bill would allow the City of Mableton to use redevelopment powers under Georgia law and to hold a referendum on the matter.

HB 1214.summary: This bill would create a new special sales tax that local governments can use for healthcare purposes. It also sets rules for how the tax is collected and how the money is used.

HB 1215.summary: The bill would add a third judge to the superior courts in the Middle Judicial Circuit. The Governor would appoint this judge, and the counties in the circuit would provide necessary facilities and support.

HB 1216.summary: This bill would require that any excise tax on rooms, lodgings, and accommodations be sent to the Department of Revenue for distribution. It also requires the submission of contracts and memoranda of understanding to help with this distribution.

HB 1217.summary: This bill would require lifeguards to be positioned on public beaches during certain periods and would allow the Department of Economic Development to create a pilot program to encourage high school students to become lifeguards.

HB 1218.summary: This bill would allow students from certain virtual schools to participate in extracurricular and interscholastic activities at their resident public school.

HB 1219.summary: This bill would require new property owners' associations to follow the Georgia Property Owners' Association Act. It also allows existing associations to vote on whether to be subject to the act and outlines procedures for terminating property owners' associations.

HB 122.summary: The bill would provide that life is valued and protected from the moment of conception, and that each life from that moment is given the same rights and protections as other persons.

HB 1220.summary: The bill would revise the rules for student eligibility and maximum scholarship amounts for student scholarship organizations. It also provides provisions for military students and students with Individualized Education Programs (IEPs), Section 504 Plans, or other designated disabilities.

HB 1221.summary: The bill would require property owners' associations to provide written notice of certain sums owed and allow a reasonable time to pay. It also requires an itemized list of attorney's fees claimed and an order finding the fees reasonable.

HB 1222.summary: The bill would require the issuance of statements of accounts for specialized land transactions and specify the information needed in these statements and how to request and provide them. It also outlines the consequences of failing to provide such statements as required.

HB 1223.summary: This bill would allow law enforcement to keep audio and video recordings that show a person's death from being disclosed to the public.

HB 1224.summary: The bill would change the rules for ending automatic renewal provisions in service contracts, giving consumers the option to have the contract end after its specified period.

HB 1225.summary: This bill would give certain consumers a pro rata refund if they cancel a service contract after a price increase.

HB 1226.summary: The bill would revise the standards for using force in self-defense or to defend others. It also provides a presumption that can be challenged and sets the timing for claiming immunity from prosecution based on justification.

HB 1227.summary: The bill would change the information required from people registering to vote who were previously registered in another state, county, or municipality. It also allows the use of comparable notices from other states to cancel voter registrations of people who were previously registered in Georgia.

HB 1228.summary: The bill would change how real property bought or acquired by certain business enterprises is taxed, requiring it to be assessed at 100% of its fair market value. It also requires that the tax revenue from this property be used to reduce the ad valorem tax bill on homesteads in the same tax jurisdiction.

HB 1229.summary: This bill would allow local governments to permit museums within their area to sell alcoholic beverages on Sundays at the same times as other retailers.

HB 123.summary: This bill would change how pretrial proceedings are handled in capital offense cases when the death penalty is sought and the accused has an intellectual disability. It includes provisions for notice of intent to claim intellectual disability, pretrial determination of intellectual disability, and capital case procedures.

HB 1230.summary: This bill would prohibit the operation of unmanned aircraft systems over places of incarceration. It would also require signs to be posted warning of this prohibition and declare such systems as contraband in these areas.

HB 1231.summary: This bill would prevent teachers from being required to supervise students during their duty-free lunch period or planning period, except in cases of extreme emergency. Teachers who do supervise during these times in other than an extreme emergency would be compensated.

HB 1232.summary: This bill would allow certain students to be excused from school to participate in officially sanctioned visits to the state capitol.

HB 1233.summary: This bill would allow local governments to waive development impact fees for projects related to affordable or workforce housing without needing to increase other impact fees to make up for the lost funds.

HB 1234.summary: This bill would allow certain group term life insurance benefits to be assigned to pay for funeral services of a deceased person who was a member of the Employees' Retirement System of Georgia, the Georgia Legislative Retirement System, or the Georgia Judicial Retirement System.

HB 1235.summary: The bill would require candidates, campaign committees, independent committees, and leadership committees that receive more than 50 percent of their funding from non-Georgia sources to include certain notices on their campaign advertisements.

HB 1236.summary: The bill would require a final determination on the medical necessity of a healthcare service to be agreed upon by a clinician when a private review agent or utilization review entity questions it.

HB 1237.summary: The bill would create the Pollution Prevention and Producer Responsibility Act of 2026, establishing a Producer Responsibility Advisory Board and requiring the development and distribution of lists of recyclable materials and approved recycling processes.

HB 1238.summary: The bill directs the Department of Community Health to ask the federal government for permission to pay certain caregivers through Medicaid for providing respite care and related services.

HB 1239.summary: This bill would require school systems and public schools to allow students up to two excused absences per school year for attending or participating in civic or political events.

HB 124.summary: This bill would require insurance policies to cover healthcare services for pediatric autoimmune neuropsychiatric disorders associated with streptococcal infection (PANDAS) and pediatric acute onset neuropsychiatric disorders (PANS).

HB 1240.summary: This bill would apply the same limit on total ad valorem tax digest to the renewal of existing tax allocation districts as it does to the creation of new ones.

HB 1241.summary: This bill changes the charter of the City of Decatur, rewriting the article on the city commission. The city commission has four commissioners and a mayor. Commissioners come from two election districts, and the mayor is elected citywide. Other parts of the article cover who can run for office, how terms are staggered, and how the mayor and the commission operate.

HB 1242.summary: This bill would remove the authority of the Department of Public Health and county boards of health to require vaccinations or other preventive measures against contagious or infectious diseases.

HB 1243.summary: This bill would allow researchers to access criminal justice data and records legally. It also requires the Attorney General to provide guidance to criminal justice agencies on sharing this information with researchers.

HB 1244.summary: The bill would amend a law about duty-free lunch periods and planning periods for educators, making sure it cannot be waived. It also sets an effective date and applies to related matters.

HB 1245.summary: The bill would change how members of the Walker County Board of Education are elected, switching from being elected by all voters in the school system to being elected by voters in their respective education districts.

HB 1246.summary: This bill would provide a new charter for the City of Clayton, including details on reincorporation, boundaries, powers, accounting, budgeting, contracting, purchasing, and other city-related matters.

HB 1247.summary: This bill would stop courts and administrative officers from considering agency interpretations when deciding cases involving laws and regulations.

HB 1248.summary: This bill would regulate, license, and tax the use of cannabis in Georgia. It also allows counties and cities to make their own ordinances about cannabis.

HB 1249.summary: This bill would require public elementary and secondary schools in Georgia to display the Bill of Rights in multiple locations. It also specifies how these displays should be made and provides for rules and regulations.

HB 125.summary: The bill would create a new offense called online menacing of a peace officer and set penalties for it.

HB 1250.summary: The bill would require certain hospitals to offer perinatal bereavement care counseling options and any available perinatal bereavement devices.

HB 1251.summary: This bill would require community associations to provide documents to unit owners upon request, maintain certain records, and create an online database. It also includes provisions for annual reports, civil actions, attorney's fees, and penalties.

HB 1252.summary: The bill would prohibit certain entities from acquiring an interest in a single-family residence under specific circumstances. It also provides definitions and a short title for the act.

HB 1253.summary: The bill would establish the Georgia Charter School Facilities Authority to help charter schools get revolving loan funds and other public financing for building, renovating, and fixing educational facilities.

HB 1254.summary: The bill would move the regulation of various professions from individual boards to the Secretary of State. It also amends laws related to cemetery and funeral services, DNA testing, and other professions and businesses.

HB 1255.summary: The bill would modify criminal procedure rules related to motions and discovery in criminal cases, modernize discovery processes, and revise provisions for serving subpoenas.

HB 1256.summary: This bill would provide for student loan repayment for public school teachers who graduated from an eligible postsecondary educational institution in Georgia and have taught for at least five years in a public school in the state.

HB 1257.summary: The bill would revise provisions for incentive grants for local boards of education to approve charter school petitions, update rules for the Office of Charter School Compliance, and change requirements for charter petitions by existing charter schools and state charter school records.

HB 1258.summary: This bill would add an additional judge to the State Court of Muscogee County. It also sets the terms of office and powers for this new judge.

HB 1259.summary: This bill would stop local school systems from offering virtual instruction to students from other systems if the local system's College and Career Ready Performance Index is below the state average. It also requires an agreement between local school systems to allow out-of-system students to attend virtual schools.

HB 126.summary: This bill would allow small businesses to sell or distribute alcoholic beverages purchased from designated retail dealers. It also sets rules for licensing and regulating these small businesses and requires them to keep records and submit reports.

HB 1260.summary: This bill would stop paying salaries, compensation, and expenses to members of county and municipal governing bodies who do not complete required training.

HB 1261.summary: The bill would provide level 1 freeport exemptions for certain goods in inventory for electric utilities and set rules for applying for such exemptions.

HB 1262.summary: This bill would increase the monetary penalties the Commissioner of Insurance can impose for violations of the Georgia Insurance Code related to mental health parity, general enforcement, surprise billing, and prepaid legal services plans.

HB 1263.summary: The bill would allow people to claim a refund of certain fees and taxes related to insurance premiums if they are paid within three years of the payment to the Commissioner.

HB 1264.summary: The bill would create a pilot program to provide Medicaid coverage for doula care for pregnant women who are Medicaid recipients. It also sets qualifications for doulas and requires a report on the program's effectiveness.

HB 1265.summary: The bill would create a new offense for fleeing or attempting to elude a pursuing vehicle or law enforcement officer from specific divisions of the Department of Public Safety. It would provide penalties based on the distance a person fled.

HB 1266.summary: The bill would repeal a provision related to the use of certain motors on vessels being operated on the Ogeechee River.

HB 1267.summary: The bill would increase penalties for certain traffic and motor vehicle offenses, including those related to license plates, revalidation decals, temporary operating permits, certificates of registration and title, and odometer alterations. It also authorizes the Department of Revenue to impose penalties for violations by licensed used motor vehicle dealers.

HB 1268.summary: This bill would revise, modernize, and correct errors or omissions in the Official Code of Georgia Annotated. It would also repeal outdated or unconstitutional portions of the code.

HB 1269.summary: The bill would require students from kindergarten to 12th grade to receive digital literacy instruction appropriate for their grade level. It also requires the Department of Education to develop and publish model programs for digital literacy.

HB 127.summary: The bill would increase the number of accumulated sick leave days that teachers and other school personnel can take each school year from three to five days.

HB 1270.summary: This bill would allow law enforcement to install and use mobile tracking devices, with court authorization, to track individuals or vehicles.

HB 1271.summary: The bill would revise the definition of 'education record' and expand provisions for parents and legal custodians to inspect and review student education records.

HB 1272.summary: This bill would provide for the licensing of payment stablecoin issuers, set rules for their advertising and business operations, and establish procedures for third-party examination and investigation. It would also outline the payment of fees and costs related to these examinations and investigations, and specify conditions for suspending or revoking a license.

HB 1273.summary: This bill would allow physician assistants to receive certain tasks from podiatric physicians. It also allows podiatric physicians to delegate certain authorities to physician assistants.

HB 1274.summary: This bill would require the Department of Insurance to collect data annually from auto insurance companies and allow the Commissioner of Insurance to order refunds for any excess profits made by these companies.

HB 1275.summary: This bill would ensure that stem cell therapies in Georgia do not use stem cells derived from aborted fetuses. It also provides definitions and requirements for the designation of physician assistants and nurse practitioners.

HB 1276.summary: The bill would allow the Department of Community Health to review information from various sources to check and confirm the eligibility of people receiving Medicaid.

HB 1277.summary: The bill would increase the project cost threshold for public roads and airports that require environmental evaluations.

HB 1278.summary: This bill would improve the process for issuing permits to dentists who want to administer conscious sedation and general anesthesia. It also requires the evaluation and certification of facilities where these procedures are performed and ensures dentists demonstrate proficiency in administering sedative techniques.

HB 1279.summary: The bill would extend the sunset date for tax-exempt organizations to use noncommercial written materials or mailings without sales and use tax.

HB 128.summary: This bill would stop vehicle rental companies from refusing to rent or lease cars to people over the age of 25 just because of their age.

HB 1280.summary: This bill would allow the General Assembly to pass a local act for the election of a county's chief appraiser. It would also set rules for the election, commission, removal, term, qualifications, vacancies, oath, duties, and compensation of such chief appraisers.

HB 1281.summary: This bill would require child care learning centers to have specific amounts of liability insurance and to show proof of this insurance. It also sets penalties for not following this rule.

HB 1282.summary: The bill would include the offense of aggravated sexual battery in the list of crimes involving victims under 16 years of age that are excluded from certain criminal procedure provisions.

HB 1283.summary: The bill would allow the creation of Family Justice Centers to address family violence issues. It affects people involved in family violence cases.

HB 1284.summary: This bill would allow local school boards to award high school diplomas to students who are at the end of their lives. It also allows for posthumous awarding of diplomas and provides for waivers and policies.

HB 1285.summary: The bill would revise the number of local sales and use taxes that counties can collect, allowing them to collect both an enhanced homestead option sales tax and a local option sales tax.

HB 1286.summary: The bill would abolish the position of director of planning for the Atlanta-region Transit Link Authority.

HB 1287.summary: The bill would change how the commissioner of the Department of Transportation is chosen.

HB 1288.summary: The bill would require law enforcement to get consent or a court order before withdrawing blood from people who are going to be put in jail or let out of jail for DNA testing.

HB 1289.summary: The bill would modify the provisions for the offense of rape and provide for penalties and limitations on defense.

HB 129.summary: The bill would remove a limitation on leased property for certain entities regarding preferential assessment for conservation use property and residential transitional property.

HB 1290.summary: The bill would revise the definition of sexual abuse for elder persons and provide for dangerous sexual offenses occurring after June 30, 2026.

HB 1291.summary: This bill would allow an income tax credit for certain costs related to providing transportation benefits to employees.

HB 1292.summary: This bill would exempt certain nursing homes for war veterans from certificate of need requirements.

HB 1293.summary: This bill would update the eligibility requirements for the Dual Achievement Program in Georgia's education system. It also ensures that students already enrolled in the program can continue their participation.

HB 1294.summary: This bill would allow transfer students up to 180 days to be evaluated for and receive medical and education services based on medical forms completed by out-of-state doctors.

HB 1295.summary: The bill would allow Georgia to join an interstate compact for physician assistant licensure, which would affect how physician assistants are licensed and regulated in the state.

HB 1296.summary: The bill would create a pilot program to support clinical research and provide certain eligible treatments to veterans and first responders suffering from specific conditions.

HB 1297.summary: This bill would allow the Magistrate Court of Pierce County to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover money after the fee is no longer collected.

HB 1298.summary: This bill would exempt the retail sale of electricity and natural gas for use by residential properties from sales and use taxes.

HB 1299.summary: This bill would allow hospital authorities to acquire, develop, operate, or equip outpatient healthcare facilities.

HB 13.summary: The bill would set the compensation for the Echols County Board of Education.

HB 130.summary: This bill would create the Pay As You Earn Education Program, which would establish and administer loans for education. It would also set rules for calculating and repaying these loans.

HB 1300.summary: The bill would increase the maximum amount of contributions allowed per beneficiary for savings trust accounts under the Georgia Higher Education Savings Plan Act.

HB 1301.summary: The bill would amend Georgia law to clarify requirements for data reported by consumer reporting agencies when providing consumer reports for employment purposes.

HB 1302.summary: The bill would change the name of the Office of Student Achievement to the Office of Education and Workforce Strategy, combine the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act Plan and Perkins State Plan, and create registered apprenticeship programs.

HB 1303.summary: The bill would create a new offense for possessing a controlled substance in the presence of a child. It would also provide definitions, penalties, and limitations on merging other offenses from the same conduct.

HB 1304.summary: This bill would allow portable solar generation devices under 1,200 watts to be exempt from certain requirements for interconnection and operation by electric service providers.

HB 1305.summary: This bill would create a licensing system for home inspectors in Georgia, including requirements for education, insurance, and continuing education. It also allows for reciprocity of licenses and company licensing.

HB 1306.summary: This bill would allow gold and silver to be used as legal tender and establish guidelines for a bullion depository and an electronic payment system. It also prohibits social credit scoring systems and requires annual reports.

HB 1307.summary: This bill would increase the homestead exemption for senior citizens and disabled persons in the City of Brookhaven to $200,000.

HB 1308.summary: This bill would allow local and state charter schools and charter school petitioners to lease, utilize, or buy unused facilities owned by a local board of education, subject to certain conditions.

HB 1309.summary: The bill would clarify that anyone who dispenses drugs is considered to be practicing pharmacy and must follow all record-keeping and other requirements set by the Georgia State Board of Pharmacy.

HB 131.summary: The bill would change the requirements for self-service storage facilities to advertise before they can enforce a lien on a tenant's property.

HB 1310.summary: This bill would designate cotton as the official state fabric of Georgia.

HB 1311.summary: This bill would stop courts from giving attorney's fees to people found guilty or who admit guilt in sexual offenses when the person who brought the case is the victim.

HB 1312.summary: This bill would prohibit people under a protective order for family or dating violence from having firearms or ammunition. It also requires courts to report such prohibitions and mandates the surrender or transfer of firearms or ammunition.

HB 1313.summary: The bill would provide legal protections for healthcare professionals who administer medical treatment to pregnant women.

HB 1314.summary: This bill would require licensees to disclose whether a transaction is reportable to a credit reporting agency.

HB 1315.summary: The bill would limit the time local governments can enforce certain moratoriums and prevent them from reimposing similar moratoriums within a certain period. It also waives sovereign immunity for claims related to damages from moratoriums that exceed these limitations and sets out recoverable damages and attorney's fees.

HB 1316.summary: This bill would remove the five-year residency requirement for a homestead exemption from Walker County school district ad valorem taxes for residents who are 75 years old or older.

HB 1317.summary: This bill would allow the City of Fort Oglethorpe to levy an excise tax according to the specified code section.

HB 1318.summary: The bill would require an actuarial study on a state-based paid family and medical leave insurance program.

HB 1319.summary: This bill would allow insurance companies to offer premium discounts for motor vehicles that have certain antitheft devices, affecting private passenger automobile insurance and commercial motor vehicle insurance with comprehensive coverage.

HB 132.summary: The bill would create the office of senior municipal court judge, setting qualifications, application and approval procedures, and amenities and privileges for such judges. It also preserves local actions that have already established senior judges for particular municipal courts.

HB 1320.summary: This bill would amend the law to include nuclear energy generation facilities in the integrated resource plan for public utilities.

HB 1321.summary: This bill would provide a $100,000 homestead exemption from City of Cartersville ad valorem taxes for residents of that city.

HB 1322.summary: The bill would change the penalty for rioting from a misdemeanor to a felony.

HB 1323.summary: The bill would require new data centers to operate as hybrid power data centers and would be certified by the Public Service Commission. It also provides for enforcement and rules and regulations.

HB 1324.summary: This bill would repeal the prohibition on possessing a silencer in Georgia.

HB 1325.summary: The bill would require local school boards to provide opportunities for parents and teachers to be involved in creating and updating student codes of conduct.

HB 1326.summary: The bill would create a tax credit for businesses that provide living wage jobs. It sets conditions and limitations for the tax credit and defines related terms.

HB 1327.summary: The bill would require each public and private elementary and secondary school in Georgia to install key boxes at their buildings in locations agreed upon with local law enforcement and emergency management agencies.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

HB 1328.summary: This bill would allow the selection committee for University of North Georgia military scholarships to choose more scholarship recipients and set a limit on the number of scholarships awarded. It also provides criteria for selecting scholarship recipients.

HB 1329.summary: The bill would amend laws related to controlled substances, specifically those classified as Schedule I, and also provide provisions related to dangerous drugs.

HB 133.summary: This bill would allow public school students to attend religious moral instruction courses provided by outside organizations, under certain conditions. Students could receive academic credit for these courses.
