HB 1330.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Public School Excellence and Stability (GPSES) grant program and set eligibility requirements for it. It also clarifies student residency qualifications for promise scholarship accounts.

HB 1331.summary: This bill would amend Georgia's minimum wage law to address how workers who receive tips as part of their compensation are paid.

HB 1332.summary: The bill would require certain hospitals to give preference to American-made pharmaceuticals and set rules for documentation and exceptions.

HB 1333.summary: This bill would allow taxpayers in municipalities to choose not to pay for certain governmental affairs activities. It would also define related terms and repeal conflicting laws.

HB 1334.summary: The bill would create the Georgia-Africa and Caribbean Trade Commission to promote trade between Georgia and African and Caribbean countries. The commission would report annually and have a fund for expenses.

HB 1335.summary: The bill would classify certain longshoremen and related maritime, port, warehouse, and logistics workers as essential workers during emergencies.

HB 1336.summary: This bill would require that at least 50 percent of the ad valorem tax revenue collected from aircraft by local tax jurisdictions be used for maintaining and operating airports within those jurisdictions.

HB 1337.summary: This bill would allow clerks of superior courts and probate court judges to keep and spend fees from passport applications and processing. It also sets rules for how these fees can be used and requires certain disclosures in written reports.

HB 1338.summary: This bill would change a 1999 homestead exemption from City of Savannah property taxes for city purposes. It would cap the "adjusted base year assessed value" of a homestead at its tax year 2025 level for later years. It would take effect only if Savannah voters approve it in the November 2026 election and the General Assembly passes it by a two-thirds vote.

HB 1339.summary: The bill would revise the provisions for filling vacancies in the office of mayor or councilor in the city of Columbus, Georgia.

HB 134.summary: The bill would revise and expand the sales tax exemption for manufactured homes. It also sets a sunset date and includes legislative findings.

HB 1340.summary: This bill would raise the income limit for a homestead exemption from school district ad valorem taxes for senior citizens in Hall County. It also introduces a new exemption for residents aged 66 and older.

HB 1341.summary: This bill would provide a $10,000 homestead exemption from Hall County ad valorem taxes for county purposes to residents of Hall County.

HB 1342.summary: This bill would provide procedures and remedies when a highway improvement project is delayed because of the removal, relocation, or adjustment of utility facilities. It also sets rules for damages in such cases and removes provisions about mediation boards.

HB 1343.summary: This bill would revise the definition of legal father and require hospitals and birthing centers to provide a video about legitimating a child to parents or guardians of newborns.

HB 1344.summary: The bill would strengthen the enforcement authority of the Commissioner of Insurance and clarify regulations related to insurance, insurance fraud, uninsured motorists, and claims processing.

HB 1345.summary: This bill would allow the State Workforce Development Board to approve certain workforce training programs for implementing the federal Workforce Pell Grant program.

HB 1346.summary: This bill would require insurance coverage for comprehensive maternal mental health screening and care during and after pregnancy, as determined by a healthcare provider.

HB 1347.summary: This bill would allow certain retirement systems to invest in real estate and increase the allowable alternative investments for these systems.

HB 1348.summary: The bill would provide for compensation for receivers in civil practice and set a cap on that compensation.

HB 1349.summary: The bill would revise the membership of the pension board for teachers and employees of the Board of Education of Fulton County.

HB 135.summary: The bill would prohibit housing discrimination based on hairstyles associated with race, color, or national origin.

HB 1350.summary: This bill would protect individuals' rights to make their own decisions about medical interventions and prevent discrimination based on these decisions. It also stops the Department of Public Health and county boards of health from requiring vaccinations or other preventive measures against contagious or infectious diseases.

HB 1351.summary: This bill would require state agencies to give employees a notice when artificial intelligence is used in personnel matters. It also requires agencies to issue a disclaimer about the use of AI.

HB 1352.summary: This bill would allow public school students to attend religious or moral instruction courses provided by individuals or organizations outside of school, under certain conditions. Students could receive academic credit for these courses.

HB 1353.summary: The bill would exclude usufructs from assessments for the excise tax on rooms, lodgings, and accommodations.

HB 1354.summary: The bill would require health insurers providing a network plan to approve credentialing applications within a certain time frame and would have the Department of Insurance establish a standardized credentialing application.

HB 1355.summary: This bill would update Georgia's workers' compensation law by changing rules on experience modification factors, procedures for refusing suitable employment, and certain benefits. It also allows for petitions, notices, teleconferences, and signed sworn statements, and permits an interlocutory order. The bill would increase weekly benefits for total disability.

HB 1356.summary: This bill would revise the compensation for the chairperson and members of the Macon County Board of Commissioners.

HB 1357.summary: This bill changes the law that created the Bulloch County Public Facilities Authority. It revises what counts as a "project" the authority can fund with revenue bonds, including county buildings, facilities, and equipment. It bars the authority from issuing bonds for projects of the school district or other local governments in the county, and says no bond may have a maturity over 40 years.

HB 1358.summary: The bill would allow the Magistrate Court of Brooks County to charge a technology fee and specify how the money from this fee can be used. It also sets rules for ending the fee and handling leftover funds.

HB 1359.summary: This bill would increase the number of members on the board of elections and registration for Brooks County from the current number to five members. It also changes how the members are appointed and how vacancies are filled.

HB 136.summary: This bill would expand the tax credit for contributions to foster child support organizations to include wraparound and mentorship services for justice-involved youth. It also allows certain insurance companies to use these tax credits against their insurance premium tax liability.

HB 1360.summary: This bill would prohibit class action lawsuits for refunds of taxes and license fees by counties and municipalities.

HB 1361.summary: The bill would allow pharmacies to compound certain active pharmaceutical ingredients and set conditions for the sale, transfer, or distribution of compounded drugs. It also requires manufacturers and wholesalers to provide specific documentation and mandates record maintenance.

HB 1362.summary: The bill would make it illegal for people with certain financial interests to hold specific public offices. It also adds rules to prevent conflicts of interest for state public officials.

HB 1363.summary: This bill would allow public schools and postsecondary educational institutions to treat antisemitism the same way they treat religious discrimination. It also requires the Department of Education to create a state-wide K-12 Title VI Coordinator.

HB 1364.summary: This bill would repeal provisions for nonjudicial foreclosures on time-share estates, with some exceptions for time-share estates created during certain periods.

HB 1365.summary: The bill would add a twenty-first judge to the superior courts in the Atlanta Judicial Circuit. The Governor would appoint the initial judge, and future judges would be elected. The bill also outlines the powers of this additional judge.

HB 1366.summary: This bill would create a scholarship program for children of public school teachers who have taught for at least ten years. The scholarships would cover tuition at eligible postsecondary institutions.

HB 1367.summary: The bill would change how board members are appointed to fill vacancies on the board of one or more community improvement districts in unincorporated Fulton County. It also provides for special elections for certain vacancies and notice requirements.

HB 1368.summary: The bill would amend laws related to mental health to re-establish community service boards and change how their governing boards are made up. It also makes other related changes.

HB 1369.summary: The bill would stop courts, arbitration panels, administrative agencies, and other tribunals from enforcing foreign laws that violate rights protected by the U.S. or Georgia Constitution.

HB 137.summary: The bill would increase the dollar value of certain public works contracts that are exempt from provisions related to the retention of contractual payments. It affects contracts for public works and those made by public schools.

HB 1370.summary: The bill would exclude a portion of overtime pay and cash tips from state income tax. It also requires employers to report this information.

HB 1371.summary: The bill would create income tax credits for businesses that meet certain job and investment requirements in Georgia. It also sets up a process for certifying qualified projects and provides incentives for wage, capital enhancement, and location-based tax credits.

HB 1372.summary: This bill would stop foreign persons and entities from buying land near critical infrastructure without getting approval from the Attorney General.

HB 1373.summary: This bill would revise exceptions to criminal prohibitions on gambling for coin-operated amusement machines, allowing them to be used for games like poker, blackjack, card games, and keno.

HB 1374.summary: The bill would provide requirements for insurance methods of payment to healthcare providers, including definitions, notification, and prohibitions on certain contractual waivers.

HB 1375.summary: This bill would restate the provisions related to the number, qualifications, and compensation of judges in the State Court of Hall County. It also provides for an additional judge for the court starting January 1, 2028.

HB 1376.summary: The bill would create the Commission for the Blind and Visually Impaired, set its composition, duties, and require the Georgia Vocational Rehabilitation Agency to consult with the commission.

HB 1377.summary: The bill would set time limits for recalling an election for a special sales and use tax for transit purposes if the tax is not approved. It affects elections for transit SPLOST.

HB 1378.summary: The bill would clarify the residency requirements for students to qualify for the Georgia Promise Scholarship.

HB 1379.summary: This bill would require institutions of the University System of Georgia, units of the Technical College System of Georgia, and local school systems to report semiannually on funding received from foreign sources. These reports would be made publicly available.

HB 138.summary: This bill would require the Georgia Peace Officer Standards and Training Council to establish basic and in-service training courses on de-escalation techniques and methods for peace officers.

HB 1380.summary: This bill would allow current and former members of the General Assembly to get special license plates with the International Symbol of Access if they qualify.

HB 1381.summary: This bill would require public utilities to include grid modernization assessments in their integrated resource plans. It also requires justification for new transmission construction instead of using certain new technologies and allows for the recovery of costs and savings related to new technologies.

HB 1382.summary: The bill would encourage the University System of Georgia and the Technical College System of Georgia to maintain policies that allow active duty military and veteran students to receive academic credit based on their military service. It also encourages the use of joint service transcripts.

HB 1383.summary: This bill would set daily emission limits for toluene from stationary sources in the Tallapoosa River Basin.

HB 1384.summary: This bill would require municipalities to share a portion of the revenue they get from certain franchise agreements with the county where the agreements are located.

HB 1385.summary: The bill would update provisions related to the office of the Safety Fire Commissioner to improve government efficiency. It also sets procedures for rule-making, hearings, and appeals, and allows for the appointment of a deputy commissioner of safety fire. Additionally, it provides certain powers in suspected arson investigations.

HB 1386.summary: This bill would prevent county development authorities in certain counties from operating within certain municipalities.

HB 1387.summary: This bill would create a statewide homestead exemption from ad valorem property taxes for homeowners, with the amount of the exemption determined from the proceeds of property taxes collected on data centers.

HB 1388.summary: This bill would require that any traffic impact analysis needed to get a building permit must be completed within 36 months after the project is substantially finished.

HB 1389.summary: The bill would extend the notice period for tenants to vacate or pay rent from the current period to seven days in dispossessory proceedings.

HB 139.summary: The bill would stop drug manufacturers and wholesalers from preventing pharmacies from buying drugs from entities that participate in a specific federal drug discount program.

HB 1390.summary: The bill would declare motor vehicles used in reckless stunt driving offenses as contraband and allow for their forfeiture.

HB 1391.summary: The bill would create a specialty license plate to honor public safety officers. Proceeds from the plate would be disbursed to the general fund and the agency supporting public safety officers.

HB 1392.summary: The bill would change the requirement for funeral establishments to maintain at least eight caskets at each location.

HB 1393.summary: This bill would allow rural hospitals to join together to increase their purchasing power with third-party payors while keeping their independence.

HB 1394.summary: The bill would ensure that Rosenwald Schools are treated as historic properties for the purpose of the historic preservation grant program and fund.

HB 1395.summary: The bill would require the intervention component of DUI Alcohol or Drug Use Risk Reduction Programs to be conducted in person.

HB 1396.summary: This bill would require privately funded organizations that operate shelters or provide outreach services to homeless individuals within 1,000 feet of schools, public parks, public playgrounds, or certain child care facilities to participate in the Georgia Homeless Management Information System (HMIS).

HB 1397.summary: This bill would allow unconscious victims of alleged sexual assault to give implied consent for a drug-facilitated sexual assault examination.

HB 1398.summary: The bill would revise arrest procedures for pregnant women, requiring pregnancy testing within a certain time after detention and setting limitations on the use and disclosure of this information. It also sets bond requirements and limitations.

HB 1399.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Likeness, Expression, Generative AI, and Commercial Yield (LEGACY) Act, which would give individuals property rights in their likeness and require consent for using their likeness commercially.

HB 14.summary: This bill would designate cornbread as the official state bread of Georgia.

HB 140.summary: This bill would limit the amount of money local governments can use from court fines and forfeitures in their yearly budgets. Any extra funds collected would go to the state.

HB 1400.summary: This bill would require written disclosures about fees and performance terms for certain artist-promoter agreements. It also includes provisions for itemized receipts, notices, rescinding fees, prohibiting retaliation, and providing exemptions and a safe harbor.

HB 1401.summary: This bill would require third-party audits of detention facilities that house federal immigration detainees. It sets criteria for the audits, outlines the selection process for auditors, and mandates the reporting and publishing of annual audit results.

HB 1402.summary: The bill would require vision and hearing screening for all public school students from pre-kindergarten through third grade.

HB 1403.summary: The bill would allow judges, justices, court officers, and other individuals to serve as judge advocates in certain capacities.

HB 1404.summary: This bill would allow the City of Pooler to levy an excise tax according to specific state law.

HB 1405.summary: The bill would require the Department of Juvenile Justice to provide cognitive behavioral therapy for certain children in restrictive custody. It sets criteria for participation and a minimum number of therapy hours. DJJ must also produce an annual report.

HB 1406.summary: This bill would require the publication of election calls in newspapers and on government websites.

HB 1407.summary: The bill would amend the Civil Practice Act to provide for scheduling of civil trials and trial calendars for certain civil actions.

HB 1408.summary: This bill would allow licensed veterinary technicians to give antirabies vaccinations to animals under the direct supervision of a licensed veterinarian.

HB 1409.summary: The bill would revise the mandated reporting requirements for child abuse in domestic relations cases. It also provides for the use of a secure web-based reporting platform.

HB 141.summary: This bill would allow businesses and practitioners to submit affidavits from certified public accountants instead of tax returns when they have locations or offices in more than one jurisdiction.

HB 1410.summary: This bill would update vision screening and literacy readiness requirements for elementary and secondary school students in Georgia.

HB 1411.summary: The bill would include domestic violence prevention in the existing program for teen dating violence prevention for students in grades eight through twelve.

HB 1412.summary: The bill would provide for the payment of certain money from traffic fines generated by members of the Uniform Division of the Department of Public Safety.

HB 1413.summary: The bill would establish a needs-based scholarship program for students attending eligible public and private postsecondary institutions in Georgia.

HB 1414.summary: This bill would allow limited liability companies to create protected series and registered series, setting procedures for their creation, records, assets, consolidation, and merger.

HB 1415.summary: The bill would require the Stone Mountain Memorial Association to hold in trust all real property obtained before January 1, 1971, and prohibit the association from selling this property, with an exception.

HB 1416.summary: This bill would exclude tips from state income tax. Employers would be required to report tips to the state. The bill also provides a definition and sets an effective date.

HB 1417.summary: This bill would include advanced placement, international baccalaureate, and Cambridge fine arts courses in the calculation of grade point averages for determining student eligibility for HOPE scholarships and other scholarships.

HB 1418.summary: This bill would allow local governments to create programs to reduce hunger and food waste by using digital platforms to share resources. It also sets requirements for these digital platforms and limits the liability of participants.

HB 1419.summary: The bill would require motor vehicle liability insurance policies to process supplemental estimates for repairs in a timely manner and provide for written explanations when claims are denied or delayed.

HB 142.summary: The bill would extend preferential assessment periods for certain historic properties for ad valorem tax purposes.

HB 1420.summary: The bill would require motor vehicle liability insurance policies to use original equipment manufacturer repair procedures for repairs. It also provides for unfair claims settlement practices and definitions related to these procedures.

HB 1421.summary: The bill would prohibit insurance companies from improperly directing car accident victims to specific repair facilities. It also sets rules for selecting repair facilities and making payments for repairs.

HB 1422.summary: This bill would add stillbirth as a qualifying event for parental leave for eligible state employees.

HB 1423.summary: The bill would revise the effective date of an existing law about elections and primaries.

HB 1424.summary: The bill would revise the compensation for the Sumter County board of education and school superintendent.

HB 1425.summary: The bill would create the Worker Tariff Relief Program Act, which would provide types of assistance to individuals and set requirements for receiving this assistance. The Department of Labor would be responsible for administering the program and creating rules and regulations.

HB 1426.summary: This bill would require peace officers to receive training on how to evacuate people with disabilities during emergencies. It also updates emergency management procedures to include evacuation plans for people with disabilities, subject to funding.

HB 1428.summary: The bill would allow the Georgia Professional Engineers and Land Surveyors Board to keep certain funds from fees it collects.

HB 1429.summary: The bill would require juvenile court clerks to collect and submit data about monetary sanctions given to juvenile offenders to the Administrative Office of the Courts.

HB 143.summary: The bill would revise provisions regarding water-measuring devices for farm use of surface and ground water.

HB 1430.summary: The bill would allow the Department of Community Health to license supportive senior housing communities and set requirements for them, including COVID-19 rules, employer-based programs, and influenza education.

HB 1431.summary: The bill would create a presumption of joint physical custody in divorce proceedings involving children. It also provides for exceptions to this presumption.

HB 1432.summary: This bill would provide rules for handling vacancies on the legislative oversight committee of the Georgia Public Defender Council and set a penalty for the council if it does not cooperate with the committee.

HB 1433.summary: The bill would make certain acts of unauthorized practice of law felonies and set penalties for these actions.

HB 1434.summary: The bill would require local governments to identify areas affected by airports, hold public hearings, and create regulations for land use in those areas.

HB 1435.summary: This bill would allow the Municipal Court of the Town of Mount Airy to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used.

HB 1436.summary: The bill would prohibit local government agencies from distributing funds to programs that substantially limit cash bail for certain offenses.

HB 1437.summary: This bill would allow notaries public to perform notarial acts using electronic means when certain requirements are met.

HB 1438.summary: The bill would create regional tariff transition advisory councils to provide guidance and report on tariff-related issues. It outlines the councils' membership, duties, and reporting requirements, and specifies funding sources and administrative support.

HB 1439.summary: This bill would prohibit the use of surveillance pricing in retail food stores, set limits on the use of electronic shelf labels, and provide for enforcement and penalties.

HB 144.summary: The bill would revise a tax credit for medical preceptor rotations, add dentistry to the program, increase the value of the tax credit, and set an annual cap. It also extends the sunset provision for the tax credit.

HB 1441.summary: The bill would create a reporting framework for trade impact transparency and accountability, requiring public reports and hearings. It also establishes an advisory panel and sets rules for confidentiality of taxpayer and business information.

HB 1442.summary: This bill would prevent local moratoria from applying to certain properties under specific circumstances.

HB 1443.summary: This bill would allow a designee of a member of the General Assembly to intervene in certain cases before the Public Service Commission.

HB 1444.summary: This bill would require sales tax returns to include specific information about the location where the tax was collected, the identity of the entity collecting the tax, and the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the entity, if applicable.

HB 1445.summary: This bill would allow sharing of GPS monitoring data with law enforcement and school districts in juvenile proceedings.

HB 1446.summary: The bill would transfer the responsibility for overseeing emergency medical services from the Department of Public Health to the Georgia Emergency Medical Services and Trauma Council.

HB 1447.summary: The bill would require a comprehensive efficiency review of local taxing bodies and mandate a report. It also allows for the use of certain grant funds and sets penalties.

HB 1448.summary: This bill would provide comprehensive regulation for financing local government assets and establish a short title for the Georgia Local Government Finance Authority Act.

HB 1449.summary: The bill would create a grant program for small businesses, small-scale farmers, and small nonprofit organizations in Georgia.

HB 145.summary: This bill would change the state floral emblem of Georgia to the sweetbay magnolia.

HB 1450.summary: The bill would require the Georgia General Assembly to approve certain deployments of the National Guard by the Governor. It also sets notification, briefing, and reporting requirements for National Guard deployments.

HB 1451.summary: The bill would allow local governments and nonprofit organizations to offer incentives to households moving from other states to Georgia. It also establishes a grant program for the Department of Community Affairs to support this relocation effort.

HB 1452.summary: This bill would allow the Municipal Court of the City of Mableton to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used.

HB 1453.summary: This bill would allow the governing authority of Jeff Davis County to levy an excise tax.

HB 1454.summary: The bill would revise laws related to firearms and the carrying and possession of firearms and other weapons. It also changes the database prohibition and provides for preemption for the discharge of firearms under certain circumstances.

HB 1455.summary: The bill would create a commission to review and validate the employment status of 1099 tax returns filed by employers on behalf of employees. The commission would also provide remedies for employees affected by incorrect 1099 filings.

HB 1456.summary: The bill would allow victims of sexual assault to get protective orders or consent agreements against the person who committed the assault. It also sets procedures and penalties for these orders.

HB 1457.summary: This bill would provide preferential tax assessment for affordable home use property. It sets procedures, conditions, and limitations for this preferential assessment and outlines the responsibilities of county tax commissioners and the Department of Community Affairs.

HB 1458.summary: The bill would allow clergy members to be charged with certain improper sexual contact offenses.

HB 1459.summary: This bill would allow the governing authority of any county or city to hold meetings by teleconference, making these meetings viewable to the public and allowing public commentary without being physically present.

HB 1460.summary: This bill changes how salaries are set for prosecutors in Muscogee County's State Court. The solicitor-general's pay would be at least 90 percent of a junior judge's salary in that court. The chief assistant solicitor-general would earn at least 80 percent of the solicitor-general's pay. Other assistant solicitors-general would have pay set by the solicitor-general, in line with other county or state attorneys.

HB 1461.summary: The bill would change the salary provisions for the clerk of the Superior Court of Muscogee County and the chief deputy clerk.

HB 1462.summary: This bill would create the Columbus Music Commission in Georgia. It sets out the commission's membership, duties, and powers, and provides for tax exemptions for the commission.

HB 1463.summary: The bill would add damage to the owner's vehicle to the liability of a peer-to-peer car-sharing program.

HB 1464.summary: The bill would create a commission to review and validate the employment status of 1099 tax returns filed by employers on behalf of employees. The commission would also provide remedies to employees affected by invalid 1099 filings.

HB 1465.summary: This bill would remove the requirement for drivers to display a revalidation decal on their vehicles as proof of annual motor vehicle registration renewal.

HB 1466.summary: This bill would allow brewers to operate satellite tasting rooms, with certain limitations. It also provides exceptions to transfer limitations and rules for regulatory authority.

HB 1467.summary: The bill would change motor-voter applications to be opt-in instead of opt-out.

HB 1468.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Property Tax Fairness Fund and provide rules for it. It would also give constitutional authorization for the fund and set limits on tax credits.

HB 1469.summary: This bill would restrict and seal certain records for people sentenced to a first conditional discharge for possession of controlled substances and certain nonviolent property crimes, unless the status is revoked.

HB 147.summary: The bill would require state agencies to conduct an annual inventory of their use of artificial intelligence and to provide annual reports to the Georgia Technology Authority.

HB 1470.summary: This bill would create a cause of action for abusive litigation based on alleged website access violations under federal and state law. It also provides factors for evaluating such claims and a rebuttable presumption when corrective action is taken after receiving notice.

HB 1471.summary: This bill would require local school systems to allow students to take up to five excused absences per school year for mental health reasons.

HB 1472.summary: The bill would revise the definition of the term 'small business' for state income tax purposes.

HB 1473.summary: This bill would stop elected officials in counties, cities, and combined county-city governments from signing nondisclosure agreements with private companies about economic development projects.

HB 1474.summary: This bill would require the annual publication of a map showing areas where the demand for child care for children aged zero to five exceeds available licensed slots by a ratio of at least three to one.

HB 1475.summary: The bill would amend laws related to benefits from governmental programs or civil or military service, duties and responsibilities of health care agents, and contested cases. It aims to provide limited authority for the appointment of an authorized representative for certain purposes.

HB 1476.summary: The bill would revise the amount of tax credits for postproduction expenditures and make additional postproduction expenditures eligible for tax credits.

HB 1477.summary: This bill would create a registration process for special education advocates and establish qualifications for them. It also requires the Department of Education to maintain a list of registered special education advocates and mandates that parents be notified of this list.

HB 1478.summary: The bill would allow courts to collect a technology fee under certain conditions and impose additional civil filing fees. It also establishes a technology fund and plans for technology use.

HB 1479.summary: The bill would extend the statute of limitations for certain alleged acts by clergy members and provide for liability for certain entities. It also extends the period for certain claims and provides definitions.

HB 148.summary: The bill would change the education and experience requirements for becoming a certified public accountant, update the rules for firms practicing public accountancy, and adjust reciprocity rules for accountants.

HB 1480.summary: This bill would repeal provisions that prohibit Medicaid expansion and amend laws related to public assistance and social services.

HB 1481.summary: The bill would designate March 14 of each year as National Black Midwives Day in Georgia.

HB 1482.summary: The bill would require certain cities to make their jails available for use by the sheriff under specific conditions and set fees for this arrangement.

HB 1483.summary: This bill would stop taxpayers from filing class action lawsuits to get refunds for property taxes.

HB 1484.summary: This bill would allow the City of Bowman to levy an excise tax according to a specific section of the Georgia Code.

HB 1485.summary: This bill would allow the Probate Court of Union County to charge a technology fee and specify how the money collected can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover funds once the fee is no longer needed.

HB 1486.summary: The bill would revise the definition of 'education record' and include additional cross-references related to access to student education records by parents and legal custodians. It also removes a specific time limit for parents or legal custodians to request education records.

HB 1487.summary: The bill would remove the millage rate cap for the City of Cornelia.

HB 1488.summary: The bill would establish the Hinesville Conference Center and Tourism Authority, define its purpose, and outline its membership, procedures, and powers.

HB 1489.summary: This bill would require candidates running for election in a district in Douglasville to live in that district for a certain period before the election.

HB 149.summary: The bill would create a three-year pilot program for a mobile health clinic to provide postpartum care in certain counties.

HB 1490.summary: The bill would transfer the responsibility for operating the Georgia Capitol Museum from the Board of Regents of the University System of Georgia to the Georgia Building Authority. It also provides for the transfer of agreements, property, employees, and funds to the Georgia Building Authority.

HB 1491.summary: The bill would increase the homestead exemption from ad valorem taxes for county purposes in Bartow County from $5,000 to $30,000 for certain residents.

HB 1492.summary: This bill would create a homestead exemption from City of Hampton ad valorem taxes for residents who have lived in the city for at least five years. The exemption would cover the full assessed value of the homestead.

HB 1493.summary: The bill would amend labor and industrial relations laws, repeal certain sections related to collective bargaining and firefighter working conditions, and modify state employee payroll deductions.

HB 1494.summary: The bill would require ride share network services to provide ride share drivers with certain information on a monthly basis and set notice and process requirements when a ride share network service deactivates or terminates a ride share driver.

HB 1495.summary: This bill would set limits on rent increases for certain senior citizens and senior housing.

HB 1496.summary: This bill would amend the charter of the City of Acworth to adopt by reference a certain map.

HB 1497.summary: The bill would provide a statement form regarding the effect of quitclaim deeds and give the act a short title.

HB 1498.summary: The bill would allow for the automatic granting of homestead exemptions by providing procedures for the transmission of relevant information following a real estate closing.

HB 1499.summary: The bill would increase the amount of the tax credit for qualified caregiving expenses. It affects people who claim this tax credit.

HB 15.summary: This bill would update terminology and revise procedures and requirements for credit unions, money transmissions, mortgage lenders and brokers, foreign banking institutions, and installment loans in Georgia.

HB 150.summary: The bill would require universities to report quarterly about funding they receive from individuals or entities related to China.

HB 1500.summary: This bill changes the city limits of Suwanee in Gwinnett County. It adds about 93 acres to the city, including parcels and the unincorporated parts of McGinnis Ferry Road. It also removes about 8 acres, including a parcel and the nearby right-of-way along McGinnis Ferry Road and I-85.

HB 1501.summary: The bill would require the Environmental Protection Division to maintain a public website to monitor levels of certain contaminants in public water systems. It also requires annual reports and recommendations to the General Assembly.

HB 1502.summary: The bill would establish requirements for the Department of Community Health to contract with care management organizations for providing healthcare services to Medicaid and PeachCare for Kids recipients.

HB 1503.summary: The bill would provide a homestead exemption from City of Covington ad valorem taxes for residents of the city. The exemption would cover the total amount of the assessed value of the homestead.

HB 1504.summary: This bill would allow the State Court of Dekalb County to charge and collect technology fees. It also provides for a court administrator and revises compensation provisions.

HB 1505.summary: The bill would require that sex education and HIV prevention instruction in schools be age-appropriate and medically accurate, and promote sexual abstinence. It also includes the subject of personal responsibility in the course of study.

HB 1506.summary: The bill would amend laws related to prompt payment to provide payment terms for business-to-business transactions. It would also define certain terms and repeal conflicting laws.

HB 1507.summary: The bill would revise the salary of the judge and solicitor for the State Court of Wayne County.

HB 1508.summary: The bill would revise the election and term provisions for the mayor and city council members of Pembroke.

HB 1509.summary: This bill would require local governments with zoning ordinances to obtain special use permits for operating immigration detention centers.

HB 151.summary: This bill would allow a deduction from Georgia taxable income for the loss of timber due to a casualty event, based on the decrease in value of the timber.

HB 1510.summary: This bill would restrict voting rights for people who are declared judicially incompetent.

HB 1511.summary: The bill would allow courts to collect a technology fee under certain conditions and impose additional civil filing fees. It also provides for the creation of a technology fund and technology plans.

HB 1512.summary: The bill would increase penalties for certain crimes committed against public safety officers or code enforcement officers. It also makes it an offense to throw objects at these individuals or at their vehicles.

HB 1513.summary: The bill would change the compensation of the judge and solicitor in the State Court of Fayette County.

HB 1514.summary: The bill would change the election date for the president of the Board of Education of Fulton County.

HB 1515.summary: This bill would create a homestead exemption from Madison County school district ad valorem taxes for residents who are 70 years old or older, up to $75,000 of the assessed value of their home.

HB 1516.summary: This bill would revise the real estate transfer tax for sales to the United States Department of Homeland Security or United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement. It also revises an exemption related to the tax.

HB 1517.summary: This bill would create a presumption that a nuisance exists based on certain residential local ordinance violations. It affects property tax, medical assistance, and corporate laws.

HB 1518.summary: This bill would require notice to be given if the date, time, or location for a required court appearance listed on a uniform traffic citation changes.

HB 1519.summary: The bill would change the terms of office for certain members of the Peachtree City Public Facilities Authority and prohibit the transfer of membership in the authority. It also specifies that members do not receive any benefit, right, or interest in the authority's assets.

HB 152.summary: The bill would revise the procedures for counties and municipalities to acquire professional services related to transportation and public works.

HB 1520.summary: This bill would prohibit landlords and coordinators from using nonpublic competitor data to set rental prices or occupancy decisions. It also requires annual certification and record retention for compliance.

HB 1521.summary: The bill would remove an exemption from securities regulation for certain financial institutions and provide for notes as securities, while also exempting certain notes from being considered securities. It would also establish a rebuttable presumption.

HB 1522.summary: The bill would allow the board of the Clayton County Water Authority to set the pay and expense reimbursement for its members.

HB 1523.summary: The bill would create the Sumter County Public Facilities Authority and give it the power to issue revenue bonds. It also sets rules for the bonds and protects bondholders.

HB 1524.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from Gwinnett County school district property taxes for residents aged 65 to 69, exempting 50% of the assessed value of their home. For residents aged 70 and older, the exemption would cover the full assessed value of their home.

HB 1525.summary: This bill would revise and readopt the charter of the City of Auburn, including provisions on incorporation, name, powers, boundaries, audits, contracting and purchasing procedures, and the sale of city property.

HB 1526.summary: The bill would repeal a former local constitutional amendment that provided a five-year exemption from local property taxes for people who built, equipped, established, completed, or enlarged a manufacturing or processing plant in Early County.

HB 1527.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from City of Franklin Springs ad valorem taxes for residents who are 65 years old or older.

HB 1528.summary: This bill would allow the Municipal Court of the City of Franklin Springs to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to the fee if it is no longer needed.

HB 1529.summary: This bill would allow the Municipal Court of the City of Canon to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover funds once the fee is no longer collected.

HB 153.summary: The bill would extend the sunset date for an exemption from sales and use tax for maintenance and replacement parts for machinery used to mix or transport concrete.

HB 1530.summary: This bill would change the term length for future mayors of the City of Fairmount to four years.

HB 1531.summary: This bill would revise the election provisions for the City of Ball Ground to ensure that primaries and elections are held and conducted according to the Georgia Election Code.

HB 1532.summary: The bill would remove a limit on the increased millage rate for the Dalton Independent School System and set a new maximum millage rate. It also provides for a referendum, effective dates, and judicial remedies if the referendum is not held.

HB 1533.summary: The bill would remove a limit on the increased millage rate for the Dalton Independent School System and set a new maximum millage rate. It also provides for a referendum, effective dates, and judicial remedies.

HB 1534.summary: This bill would add an additional judge to the State Court of Chatham County and set out the judge's election, powers, duties, jurisdiction, privileges, immunities, and compensation.

HB 1535.summary: This bill would allow the City of Sandy Springs to use redevelopment powers provided by state law and to hold a referendum on the issue.

HB 1536.summary: This bill would provide a new charter for the City of Eatonton.

HB 1537.summary: This bill would give Bibb County school district homeowners age 65 and older a homestead exemption from school district property taxes. Ages 65 to 74 would get $17,000 off the assessed value, ages 75 to 84 would get $32,000, and those 85 and older would be fully exempt. Residents must apply to the county tax commissioner. It takes effect only if Bibb County school district voters approve it in the November 2026 election.

HB 1538.summary: This bill would provide a homestead tax exemption for residents of Macon-Bibb County. Those aged 65 to 74 would get a $17,000 exemption, and those aged 75 to 84 would get a $32,000 exemption.

HB 1539.summary: This bill would allow the Probate Court of Ware County to charge a technology fee and specify how the money from this fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover funds once the fee is no longer collected.

HB 154.summary: The bill would designate ambulance services as an essential service in Georgia.

HB 1540.summary: This bill would allow the State Court of Ware County to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover money after the fee is no longer collected.

HB 1541.summary: This bill would allow the Magistrate Court of Ware County to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to the fee if it is no longer needed.

HB 1542.summary: This bill would allow the Magistrate Court of Worth County to charge a technology fee and specify how the money from this fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover money after the fee is no longer collected.

HB 1543.summary: The bill would increase the income cap for a homestead exemption from certain property taxes in Chattooga County for residents aged 70 or older. It also raises the value of the exemption over two years.

HB 1544.summary: This bill would create a homestead exemption from Chattooga County ad valorem taxes for county purposes. The exemption would apply to residents aged 70 or older with an income not exceeding $38,000.

HB 1545.summary: This bill would allow current Putnam County board of commissioners to continue their terms of office. It also requires board members to live in their districts and sets rules for filling vacancies.

HB 1546.summary: This bill would set requirements for local authorities to hire legal services on a contingent fee basis and require the Attorney General to review and approve such contracts. It also places restrictions on these contracts.

HB 1547.summary: This bill would provide staggered terms of office for certain future appointees to the board of elections and registration for Liberty County.

HB 1548.summary: This bill would allow the Municipal Court of the City of Clarkesville to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used.

HB 1549.summary: The bill would allow the Municipal Court of the City of Cornelia to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used.

HB 155.summary: The bill changes how arbitrators are chosen and objected to in annexation disputes, how arbitration panels report their findings, and how arbitrators are paid.

HB 1550.summary: This bill adds an area to the City of Byron's corporate limits. The added area runs along Housers Mill Road, near the Georgia Highway 247 connector. It takes effect June 1, 2026 only if a separate act removes the same right of way from the City of Fort Valley. Otherwise, it does not take effect and is repealed that day.

HB 1551.summary: The bill would increase the income cap for a homestead exemption from Pickens County School District ad valorem taxes for educational purposes.

HB 1552.summary: This bill would create a homestead exemption from City of Bremen independent school district property taxes for residents aged 65 or older who have lived in and paid taxes to the district for at least five years. The exemption would be for $90,000 of the assessed value of their home.

HB 1553.summary: This bill would allow the Municipal Court of the City of Forest Park to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used.

HB 1554.summary: The bill would provide for collateral protection insurance and amend insurance laws.

HB 1555.summary: The bill would remove certain territory from the city limits of Fort Valley and require the city to transfer ownership of any property related to the utility system if requested by the utility commission.

HB 1556.summary: The bill would provide a new charter for the City of Nicholls, outlining its incorporation, boundaries, powers, and various administrative procedures.

HB 1557.summary: The bill would revise the composition of the board of elections for Fayette County and the appointment of board members. It also specifies initial terms and allows current board members to serve out their appointed terms.

HB 1558.summary: This bill would provide a full homestead exemption from City of Palmetto ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes to residents who are 65 years of age or older.

HB 1559.summary: The bill would revise the qualifications, terms, powers, and duties of the mayor, councilmembers, and city manager in the City of Palmetto, and also revise provisions for departments and employees of the city government.

HB 156.summary: The bill would give the Department of Transportation authority over vertiports and provide definitions related to vertiports.

HB 1560.summary: The bill would allow the City of Springfield, Georgia, to use redevelopment powers under the state's constitution and laws. It also provides for a referendum.

HB 1561.summary: This bill would require secondary schools and public colleges to recognize certain rights for student journalists and provide protections for student media advisers. It also sets limitations and requires written policies.

HB 1562.summary: This bill would raise the homestead exemption from Pike County property taxes for totally disabled residents, from the county's 2002 law. The base exemption would be $15,000 of assessed value. Higher amounts, up to $30,000, would apply to those age 70 or older who have lived in the county for set lengths of time. It would take effect only if Pike County voters approve it in November 2026.

HB 1563.summary: This bill would increase the homestead exemption from ad valorem taxes for senior citizens in Pike County. It also provides for increased exemptions for certain residents who have lived in the county for a specific period of time.

HB 1564.summary: This bill would provide a full homestead exemption from Lee County school district ad valorem taxes for residents aged 67 or older, specifically for taxes used to pay interest on and retire bonded indebtedness.

HB 1565.summary: This bill would provide a full homestead exemption from Lee County school district ad valorem taxes for residents who are 80 years or older and have an income of $40,000 or less.

HB 1566.summary: This bill would provide a full homestead exemption from Ware County school district ad valorem taxes for residents who are 75 years of age or older.

HB 1567.summary: This bill would repeal an existing Act about the City of Quitman in Brooks County and transfer all legal rights, privileges, and assets of the city to Brooks County. It also provides for the transfer of duties and obligations to the county.

HB 1568.summary: The bill would change the corporate limits of the City of Woodstock.

HB 1569.summary: This bill would allow the Municipal Court of the City of McDonough to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used.

HB 157.summary: This bill would add certain properties in Jackson County to the Town of Braselton. The land is described by survey and plat records, with two tax parcels excluded. The change amends the town's 2003 charter so those properties fall within the town limits. It takes effect when the Governor approves it or it becomes law without approval.

HB 1570.summary: The bill would revise the membership of the board of the Cochran/Bleckley Airport Authority.

HB 1571.summary: This bill changes when the State Court of Bryan County, formerly the City Court of Pembroke, holds its terms. Criminal trials would be held in four regular terms a year, starting January 2 and the first day of April, July, and October. Civil trials would be held monthly, starting on the first of each month. It takes effect July 1, 2026.

HB 1572.summary: The bill would require food service establishments to take certain actions related to food allergy awareness and to post specific information in staff areas, as approved by the Department of Public Health.

HB 1573.summary: This bill would provide a $20,000 homestead exemption from City of Statham ad valorem taxes for residents aged 62 or older and an additional $10,000 exemption for those aged 67 or older.

HB 1574.summary: This bill would require people convicted of homicide by vehicle while driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs to pay restitution.

HB 1575.summary: The bill would change an existing law to apply a homestead exemption from City of Kingsland ad valorem taxes to residents who are 62 years old or older.

HB 1576.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from City of Kingsland ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes. The exemption would be for an amount equal to the difference between the current year's assessed value and the base year's assessed value of a homestead.

HB 1577.summary: The bill would revise the powers of the mayor of the City of Woodbine, allowing the mayor to vote on all matters before the city council and to select and supervise the city administrator. It also provides for the suspension of the city administrator in certain circumstances and revises contracting procedures.

HB 1578.summary: This bill updates the charter of the Town of Arcade. It changes the municipality's name to the "City of Arcade" throughout the charter and sets the council's organizational meeting for the second Monday of January after an election. It also revises rules for emergency ordinances and gives the mayor the power to veto council actions, which the council can override by a vote of four members.

HB 1579.summary: This bill would change the boundaries of the City of Savannah.

HB 158.summary: The bill would require businesses using trade names to file registration statements with the office of the Secretary of State.

HB 1580.summary: The bill would repeal and replace all current provisions related to the Henry County Airport Authority and authorize the issuance of refunding bonds, securities, or other obligations.

HB 1581.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from City of Fayetteville ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes, based on the increase in property tax collections over the value collected in tax year 2025.

HB 1582.summary: The bill would provide a homestead exemption from Fayette County school district property taxes for educational purposes, based on any increased property tax collections beyond the 2025 tax year.

HB 1583.summary: This bill would provide a new homestead exemption in Fayette County for residents based on a floating proportional amount from increased property tax collections. The exemption would apply to both county and school district ad valorem taxes.

HB 1584.summary: The bill would provide for a council-manager form of government for the City of Augusta and Richmond County, and it would require a referendum for this change to take effect. It also includes provisions for mandatory execution of election and judicial remedies if there is a failure to comply.

HB 1585.summary: This bill would allow Georgia taxpayers to get a tax credit for donations to nonprofit organizations that provide housing for people receiving cancer treatment.

HB 1586.summary: This bill would provide a new charter for the Town of Bogart.

HB 1587.summary: This bill would abolish the elected position of county surveyor in Cobb County and replace it with an appointed position starting January 1, 2029. The governing authority of Cobb County would be responsible for appointing the county surveyor and setting qualifications for the position.

HB 1588.summary: The bill would allow the sheriff of Cobb County to determine the salaries of the chief deputy sheriff, assistant chief deputy sheriff, and executive assistant to the sheriff.

HB 1589.summary: The bill would repeal term limit provisions for members of the Board of Commissioners of Telfair County.

HB 159.summary: The bill would increase the amount of bonds that the Georgia Housing and Finance Authority can have outstanding at any time.

HB 1590.summary: This bill would repeal a constitutional amendment that made county officers in Telfair County ineligible to hold office under certain conditions.

HB 1591.summary: The bill would establish protocols for recruiting, vetting, and appointing the superintendent of the DeKalb County School System, as well as for contracting with the superintendent.

HB 1592.summary: This bill would require certain schools and public institutions of higher education to recognize certain rights for student journalists and provide protections for student media advisers. It also sets limitations and requires written policies.

HB 1593.summary: The bill would repeal the ban on selling alcoholic beverages within 250 feet of any polling place on election days.

HB 1594.summary: This bill would add about 809 acres to the City of Riceboro by revising its corporate limits. The new area is described by boundary measurements that begin at the intersection of U.S. Highway 17 (South Coastal Highway) and Retreat Road. It amends the city's 1992 charter.

HB 1595.summary: The bill would revise how the income cap is calculated for a $10,000 homestead exemption from certain ad valorem taxes in Clarke County, Georgia, for residents and the Clarke County School District.

HB 1596.summary: The bill would require the Georgia Bureau of Investigation to provide local prosecutorial agencies with information about forensic database evidence. It also requires local prosecutorial agencies to make certain determinations and take specific actions.

HB 1597.summary: The bill would change loan amounts, structure, and forgiveness terms for home buying assistance programs. It also sets qualifications for eligibility and minimum fund allocation.

HB 1598.summary: This bill would provide a full homestead exemption from Laurens County school district ad valorem taxes for residents who are 80 years old or older.

HB 1599.summary: The bill would revise the qualifications for members of the Sandersville School Building Authority.

HB 16.summary: The bill would require employers in warehouse distribution centers to give workers written information about quotas and workplace surveillance, prohibit certain types of quotas, provide paid rest breaks, and set limits on the collection and use of work speed data.

HB 160.summary: The bill would add an additional judge to the city court in Carrollton, Carroll County, and provide for the appointment and election of this judge. It also establishes a chief judge for the court.

HB 1600.summary: This bill would create the City of McDonough Public Facilities Authority, allowing it to acquire, construct, equip, maintain, and operate buildings and facilities for the city's use.

HB 1601.summary: This bill would provide a $10,000 homestead exemption from City of Gainesville ad valorem taxes for residents of that city.

HB 1602.summary: This bill would provide a $10,000 homestead exemption from City of Gainesville independent school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes for residents of that district.

HB 1603.summary: This bill would require performers to give consent before their likeness can be used to create a digital replica. It also allows performers to take legal action if their consent is not obtained.

HB 1604.summary: The bill would require a task force to review the effectiveness of existing program weights under the Quality Basic Education Act every two years instead of every three years. It also requires the task force to prepare and submit a report.

HB 1605.summary: The bill would stop the Department of Community Health from claiming Medicaid estate recovery from ABLE accounts, unless federal law requires it.

HB 1606.summary: The bill would create a new law making it an offense to disrupt a worship service. It would define the offense and set penalties.

HB 1607.summary: This bill would create first-time homebuyer savings accounts, allowing contributions and transfers of beneficiaries. It also provides for tax deductions for account holders.

HB 1608.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Youth Advisory Council, set criteria for its membership, and establish its purpose and activities.

HB 161.summary: This bill would allow the Georgia Bureau of Investigation to issue subpoenas for electronic communication records when investigating crimes involving cyber-enabled threats to life and property.

HB 162.summary: The bill would restrict and seal sentences for people under the First Offender Act until their status is revoked.

HB 163.summary: The bill would require food service establishments to disclose if certain food products contain cell-cultured meat or plant-based meat alternatives.

HB 164.summary: The bill would repeal automatic repeal provisions for allowable weight variances for vehicles or loads carrying certain commodities in specific areas of the state. It also allows local law enforcement to enforce these provisions.

HB 165.summary: The bill would repeal an income tax credit for business enterprises that lease motor vehicles. It also exempts nonprofit organizations from sales and use taxes for property used in constructing, renovating, or rehabilitating affordable housing. Additionally, it repeals certain sales and use tax exemptions for film or video admissions and machinery sales.

HB 166.summary: This bill would designate the fourth Friday in November as 'National Sugarcane Syrup Day' in Georgia.

HB 167.summary: This bill would allow hunters to wear fluorescent pink outer garments while hunting.

HB 168.summary: The bill would require local governments to pass a new local act to reimpose the County Special Purpose Local Option Sales Tax (SPLOST).

HB 169.summary: This bill would limit exceptions to the breach of covenants for conservation use related to solar energy generation to existing contracts. It also sets a time when the provisions will no longer be in effect.

HB 17.summary: The bill would allow the Department of Public Health to carry out projects to educate people about valvular heart disease, raise awareness, and help with early diagnosis. It also aims to reduce sudden cardiac deaths caused by this disease.

HB 170.summary: The bill would require insurance benefit providers to disclose certain payments to treating healthcare providers. It also provides definitions and related matters.

HB 171.summary: The bill would repeal and replace a section of Georgia law about obscene material and its distribution, and it would prohibit the distribution of computer-generated obscene material depicting a child. It also sets a standard for what is considered obscene and provides penalties and probation for violations.

HB 172.summary: The bill would amend the state veterinary education laws to set limits on a student loan forgiveness program.

HB 173.summary: The bill would require the Department of Education to provide parents and guardians of students entering sixth grade with information about recommended adolescent vaccinations in print or electronic form.

HB 174.summary: This bill would allow the Municipal Court of the City of Centerville to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used.

HB 175.summary: The bill would revise background check requirements for employees of early care and education programs and Head Start programs. It also provides for the revocation and nonissuance of licenses and commissions for these programs.

HB 176.summary: The bill would change the laws about which judgments can be appealed directly and the procedures for certain types of post-judgment relief in criminal cases.

HB 177.summary: This bill would allow protective orders for family and dating violence to include protection for household pets.

HB 178.summary: The bill would require the Department of Community Health to request federal approval for a demonstration project to provide Medicaid treatment services to people living with HIV in Georgia.

HB 179.summary: The bill would require the digital recording of certain trial proceedings for appellate purposes and for persons under sentence of the state court of record. It affects the appellate practice and criminal procedure.

HB 18.summary: The bill would add a residency requirement for students eligible to participate in the Dual Enrollment Act, which allows high school students to take college courses.

HB 180.summary: The bill would modify requirements for probate judges in Georgia.

HB 181.summary: This bill would allow the state registrar to issue a 'Certificate of Foreign Birth' without a judicial order if certain criteria are met.

HB 182.summary: This bill would stop group life insurance policies from excluding or limiting coverage for deaths that happen while a person is on active duty as a service member.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

HB 183.summary: This bill would allow innkeepers to remove and hold a guest's property after the guest leaves, as part of the innkeeper's lien rights. It also provides procedures for innkeepers to remove guests and for law enforcement to assist in such removals.

HB 184.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Consumer Protection Towing Act, setting rules for towing vehicles in emergencies, at the request of the vehicle owner, and from private property. It covers requirements for estimates and invoices, notice to vehicle owners, and the release of towed vehicles.

HB 185.summary: The bill would repeal and reenact Chapter 11A of the Dietetics Practice Act in the state's laws about professions and businesses.

HB 186.summary: This bill would remove the requirement for a title ad valorem tax fee for certain inherited vehicles.

HB 187.summary: The bill would change certain provisions related to professions practicing in Georgia, including electrical contractors, plumbers, and others involved in building and housing work.

HB 188.summary: The bill would extend protections for victims of family violence and stalking when it comes to residential leases.

HB 189.summary: The bill would amend laws related to notaries public, setting limitations on certain notarial acts.

HB 19.summary: The bill would require the Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Disabilities to create and maintain an electronic registry for inpatient psychiatric beds.

HB 190.summary: This bill would stop condominium and property owners' associations from punishing property owners who take certain actions. It also outlines what actions are not considered retaliation and provides definitions, remedies, and a defense.

HB 191.summary: The bill would allow for substitute service when a respondent is avoiding service to delay a hearing in family violence cases.

HB 192.summary: The bill would include specific references to programs on the High-demand Career List in the State Board of Education's minimum course of study for career education for students in grades six through 12. It also provides for evaluation methodology related to the State Workforce Development Board.

HB 193.summary: This bill would require businesses in Georgia to warn people if they are exposed to chemicals known to cause cancer or reproductive harm. It also would prevent the discharge of such chemicals into drinking water.

HB 194.summary: The bill would revise the standards for using force in self-defense or to defend others. It also provides a presumption that a person claiming self-defense is immune from prosecution and sets standards for proof in such cases.

HB 195.summary: The bill would require law enforcement to have probable cause before issuing summonses or boarding vessels related to watercraft rules and regulations.

HB 196.summary: The bill would require that drugs dispensed to state employees for self-administration under their health insurance plan be reimbursed using a transparent, index-based price plus a dispensing fee.

HB 197.summary: The bill would require health care providers to make a reasonable effort to respond to attempts by private review agents or utility review entities to discuss a patient's care.

HB 198.summary: The bill would allow certain youth groups to use school facilities. It also provides a definition and related matters.

HB 199.summary: The bill would modify provisions related to protecting the personally identifiable information of judges and their spouses. It also abolishes the requirement for the Administrative Office of the Courts to maintain a database of protected persons and information.

HB 2.summary: This bill would create a tax credit for people who buy devices to safely store firearms. It sets an annual limit on the total tax credit that can be claimed.

HB 20.summary: The bill would require the State Board of Education to create rules that all certified public school staff must complete annual training on depression and suicide awareness and prevention.

HB 200.summary: The bill would allow the State Board of Education to start a three-year pilot program for an immersive writing program in eligible public elementary schools for students in grades two through five.

HB 201.summary: The bill would prohibit selling, offering for sale, trading, or distributing lab-grown meat in Georgia.

HB 202.summary: The bill would create a program to encourage local boards of education to approve new charter school petitions and provide grants to those boards that do so.

HB 203.summary: The bill would require the Board of Regents to include members who are graduates of historically black colleges or universities that are part of the University System of Georgia.

HB 204.summary: This bill would remove the Department of Public Safety's authority to set reasonable rates, fares, and charges for motor carriers transporting household goods.

HB 205.summary: The bill would require the Board of Homeland Security to develop a list of approved unmanned aircraft systems for use in Georgia.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

HB 206.summary: The bill would repeal the Drug-free Postsecondary Education Act of 1990, which makes students convicted of certain drug offenses ineligible for loans, scholarships, and grants. It also ensures that students will not lose HOPE scholarships or grants based solely on such convictions.

HB 207.summary: This bill would provide rules for storing firearms in motor vehicles or vessels. It also sets penalties and exceptions for carrying weapons in certain school-related areas.

HB 208.summary: The bill would create special license plates that support the state parks and historic sites division of the Department of Natural Resources. It also aims to establish a specialty license plate promoting conservation, but the caption is cut off before fully explaining this part.

HB 209.summary: The bill would designate emergency medical services, including ambulance service, as essential services in Georgia.

HB 21.summary: This bill would create a tax credit for businesses that construct, renovate, purchase, or lease property to sell or offer healthy foods in less developed areas.

HB 210.summary: The bill would revise rules for retail dealers of alcoholic beverages, including allowing the issuance or holding of a beneficial interest in additional retail dealer licenses and requiring the new location of such licenses to be in the same county as the previous location.

HB 211.summary: The bill would provide immunity from certain lawsuits related to specific chemicals for entities involved in the chemicals' handling or disposal.

HB 212.summary: The bill would create a tax credit for the production of clean energy. It would also set rules for calculating the credit amount and allow the credit to be transferred.

HB 213.summary: This bill would create a tax credit for investments in clean energy. It specifies how to calculate the credit amount and sets terms and conditions for the credit. The credit can be transferred.

HB 214.summary: The bill would make creative and artistic expression evidence inadmissible in court trials.

HB 215.summary: The bill would remove the Secretary of State's authorization to be part of a nongovernmental group that shares and exchanges information to improve voter registration accuracy and efficiency. It also maintains an exemption for certain document disclosures and prohibits the Secretary of State from engaging in certain activities.

HB 216.summary: The bill would create a new commission called the Georgia CHIPS and Advanced Technology Commission within the Department of Economic Development. It would also abolish the Georgia CHIPS and Advanced Technology Consortium and replace its advisory panel and executive committee.

HB 217.summary: The bill would make the Dual Achievement Program a permanent state-wide program in Georgia.

HB 218.summary: This bill would change the law to require hospitals to offer influenza vaccinations to patients aged 18 and older before they are discharged.

HB 219.summary: This bill would allow the Georgia Composite Board of Professional Counselors, Social Workers, and Marriage and Family Therapists, as well as the Georgia Board of Nursing, to create programs to monitor and help healthcare professionals who are impaired.

HB 22.summary: The bill would require employers to give veteran employees paid leave on Veterans Day and provide a tax credit to employers for the paid leave they give.

HB 220.summary: The bill would allow an insurer under a liability policy to pay a third party and a senior lienholder under certain circumstances.

HB 221.summary: The bill would provide for equal athletic opportunities for public school students in Georgia.

HB 222.summary: The bill would require the inclusion of certain contact information on bonds and recognizances in criminal proceedings.

HB 223.summary: This bill would exclude certain disaster relief or assistance grant payments for agricultural losses caused by Hurricane Helene from being counted as taxable income. It also provides refundable income tax credits for timber producers based on casualty losses related to Hurricane Helene.

HB 224.summary: This bill would allow the Department of Transportation to build or maintain roads on military bases or installations if the U.S. Department of Defense or another federal entity pays for it.

HB 225.summary: This bill would repeal laws that allow the use of automated traffic enforcement safety devices to enforce speeding violations in school zones. It also prohibits local governing bodies or law enforcement agencies from entering into or renewing contracts for such enforcement.

HB 226.summary: This bill adds a stretch of road to the City of Cochran's corporate limits. The added area is the right of way of State Route 23 (also U.S. Highway 87), running north from the current city limits to where it meets Jac Arts Road.

HB 227.summary: The bill would rename low THC oil as medical cannabis and clarify and revise criminal penalties related to offenses against public health and morals, regulation of controlled substances, and general provisions relative to the Department of Public Health.

HB 228.summary: This bill would allow and set rules for the production of farmstead products for human consumption, providing relief from regulatory burdens for small dairy farmers and producers. It also sets standards for safety, cleanliness, and health for these products.

HB 229.summary: The bill would exempt materials used in constructing capital outlay projects for educational purposes from local sales and use taxes if the projects were approved and funded through a constitutionally authorized education special purpose local option sales tax.

HB 23.summary: The bill would require schools to provide progress reports to parents or legal guardians of students in the early intervention program. It also requires the Department of Education to work with the Professional Standards Commission to improve and update professional development opportunities for teachers.

HB 230.summary: This bill would create a tax credit for certain expenses incurred by taxpayers who sell new construction homes to individuals or related individuals for up to a certain price.

HB 231.summary: The bill would allow insurance coverage for complementary and alternative therapies when provided by certain licensed professionals, and would offer optional coverage for therapies provided by qualified herbalists, homeopaths, and others.

HB 232.summary: This bill would allow Georgia to join the Interstate Massage Compact, which is a cooperative agreement between states for regulating massage therapy practice. The Georgia Board of Massage Therapy would be responsible for administering the compact in Georgia.

HB 233.summary: The bill would designate Brunswick stew as the official state stew of Georgia.

HB 234.summary: The bill would exempt from income tax certain sign-on and retention bonuses received by commercial pilots, aircraft mechanics, and aircraft service technicians.

HB 235.summary: The bill would require employers of school employees to provide leaves of absence for donating bone marrow and organs. It also sets standards and conditions for granting such leaves and includes a penalty for noncompliance.

HB 236.summary: This bill would abolish the elected position of county surveyor in Bartow County and instead provide for the appointment of a county surveyor by the county's governing authority. The current elected surveyor would complete their term, and qualifications for future appointees would be established.

HB 237.summary: The bill would allow creative or artistic expression to be used as evidence in trials. It also sets a presumption that such evidence is not admissible unless certain conditions are met.

HB 238.summary: The bill requires the Georgia Peace Officer Standards and Training Council to create and maintain a training course for police officers on how to respond to individuals with Alzheimer's disease or dementia.
