HB 243.summary: The bill would revise the purpose of the Stone Mountain Memorial Association. It affects the association and related matters.

HB 255.summary: The bill would establish a specialty license plate honoring Southern University Alumni. Proceeds from the plate would be disbursed to the general fund and the alumni organization.

HB 257.summary: This bill would allow certain owners to get metal fleet motor vehicle license plates before their vehicles are registered.

HB 262.summary: The bill would create a grant program for the Department of Community Health to help acquire and install backup generators. The Department would consult with the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency to establish grant criteria.

HB 263.summary: This bill would create a pilot program to provide Medicaid coverage for doula care for pregnant women who are Medicaid recipients.

HB 264.summary: This bill would exempt residents who are 100 years old or older from paying income tax.

subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

HB 27.summary: The bill would provide grants from the State Board of Education to local school units to support students living in poverty. It also requires the State Board of Education to develop rules and regulations for these grants.

HB 270.summary: This bill would allow for the continuance and stay of eviction proceedings for tenants at certain airports. It also changes how eviction notices are served to tenants.

HB 272.summary: The bill would change certain provisions regarding definitions in Georgia's revenue and taxation laws.

HB 273.summary: The bill would change certain definitions related to title ad valorem tax on motor vehicles.

HB 274.summary: The bill would change certain definitions related to the alternative ad valorem tax on motor vehicles.

HB 275.summary: The bill would change certain definitions related to income taxes.

HB 276.summary: This bill creates a state income tax credit for buying, installing, and preparing a power generator that runs on woody biomass (such as land-clearing residue and wood pellets) and has at least 50 megawatts of capacity. It also changes a sales tax exemption on computer equipment for high-technology companies and data centers, adding companies that use such generators on site to those eligible from 2029 through 2034.

HB 277.summary: The bill would change certain definitions related to the excise tax on rooms, lodgings, and accommodations.

HB 278.summary: The bill would change certain definitions related to the excise tax on rooms, lodgings, and accommodations.

HB 279.summary: The bill would change certain definitions related to sales and use taxes.

HB 28.summary: This bill would provide a $10,000 homestead exemption from Colquitt County ad valorem taxes for county purposes to residents of the county.

HB 280.summary: The bill would change certain definitions related to sales and use taxes.

HB 281.summary: The bill would change certain definitions related to ad valorem taxation of property.

HB 282.summary: The bill would change certain definitions related to ad valorem taxation of property.

HB 283.summary: This bill would allow for the issuance of a refusal to sign citation for drivers who fail to sign a citation, and it would provide a penalty for this refusal.

HB 285.summary: The bill would create a judicial procedure for removing a person's involuntary hospitalization information from law enforcement databases.

HB 286.summary: The bill would create a subfund within the Seed-Capital Fund to provide startup capital to small businesses that are majority owned by students or graduates of a small business program at the Technical College System of Georgia.

HB 287.summary: This bill updates the reference date for standards, rules, and regulations related to the Environmental Protection Division and the Environmental Advisory Council, as well as for rules related to game and fish.

HB 288.summary: This bill would allow for declaratory judgments when a prosecuting attorney makes accusations about the credibility of a peace officer.

HB 289.summary: The bill would allow remote online notarizations and set requirements for electronic journaling. It affects notaries public and those using their services.

HB 29.summary: This bill would create a homestead exemption of $10,000 from Colquitt County school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes for residents of that district.

HB 290.summary: The bill would revise the terms 'Internal Revenue Code' and 'Internal Revenue Code of 1986' in Georgia law to incorporate certain provisions of federal law.

HB 291.summary: The bill would create a certification process for community health workers in Georgia. It would establish a committee to oversee the certification and approve training programs.

HB 292.summary: This bill would allow certain employers to be certified as living wage employers and provide a tax credit for those employers who hire individuals in new living wage jobs for at least one year.

HB 293.summary: The bill would repeal parts of the 'Protect Students First Act' that deal with divisive concepts and other related provisions in Georgia's education laws.

HB 294.summary: The bill would require the State Board of Education to review and update policies, guidelines, and processes for awarding high school credit based on a student's demonstration of subject area competency.

HB 295.summary: This bill lets Georgia owners of real property submit a written claim to their city or county for money if a local government's policy or a public nuisance it maintains cuts the property's value or causes the owner expenses. If the claim is rejected or ignored for 30 days, the owner may sue.

HB 296.summary: This bill would allow people to show a driver's license in an electronic format when driving, instead of needing a physical license. It also says that law enforcement cannot force someone to show their license on a wireless device.

HB 297.summary: This bill would revise the definition of 'multipurpose off-highway vehicle' and create a subclassification for ad valorem taxation of such vehicles.

HB 298.summary: The bill would require hospitals to have written nurse staffing plans and establish nurse staffing committees. It also mandates annual reports on staffing information.

HB 299.summary: This bill would repeal a section of Georgia law that restricts local governments from regulating rent.

HB 3.summary: The bill would require background checks for all firearm transfers in Georgia.

HB 30.summary: The bill would provide a homestead exemption from Catoosa County school district ad valorem taxes for residents who are 67 years old or older, up to $100,000 of the assessed value of their home.

HB 300.summary: The bill would change laws about pawnbrokers to exclude motor vehicle certificates of title from pawn transactions. It also removes provisions that say pawnbrokers possessing these certificates are considered to possess the vehicles.

HB 301.summary: This bill would automatically restrict criminal history records for certain misdemeanor and felony convictions five years after the completion of the sentence.

HB 302.summary: This bill would provide free meals to public school students enrolled in after-school or summer school programs.

HB 303.summary: The bill would provide for the placement of a monument to honor the Original 33.

HB 304.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Municipal Court Clerks' Council, define its membership, powers, and duties, and provide for its funding. It would also specify the status of the council and its members.

HB 305.summary: The bill would prohibit certain entities from acquiring an interest in a single-family dwelling. It also provides definitions and a short title for the act.

HB 306.summary: The bill would create a cause of action for workplace harassment and retaliation, allowing employees to sue for such issues.

HB 307.summary: The bill would add provisions for students who are at risk of not achieving grade-level reading proficiency or who show signs of dyslexia under the Quality Basic Education Act.

HB 308.summary: This bill would allow miniature on-road vehicles to be operated on certain highways, set standards for registering these vehicles, and require an annual licensing fee and license plates for them.

HB 309.summary: This bill would require local governments to hold a public vote before they can abolish a police force that was created by a resolution or ordinance.

HB 31.summary: The bill would require the Catoosa County Board of Education to adopt a balanced budget. If the Quality Basic Education Formula is fully funded by state appropriations, the budget must be balanced without using fiscal reserves.

HB 310.summary: The bill would create a program to provide grant funds to public schools to pay student teachers during their required student teaching component of their teacher education programs.

HB 311.summary: The bill would change the age at which individuals are protected from age discrimination in employment.

HB 312.summary: This bill would allow people applying for unemployment benefits to get their personnel files if their former employers contest their claims. It also requires the Department of Labor to modify the separation notice and penalizes employers who do not deliver personnel files on time.

HB 313.summary: The bill would require all public elementary and secondary schools in Georgia to display the Ten Commandments in multiple locations.

HB 314.summary: The bill would revise and update definitions and certification requirements for athletic trainers and require athletic training students to be supervised by a physician or licensed athletic trainer.

HB 315.summary: The bill would define what a law enforcement officer is and provide for the use of deadly force by these officers. It also affects the authorization of arrests with and without warrants.

HB 316.summary: The bill would create an income tax credit in Georgia equal to 20 percent of the federal earned income tax credit.

HB 317.summary: This bill would create a new type of community development district in Georgia to support workforce and residential infrastructure projects.

HB 318.summary: This bill would allow people to appeal superior court decisions on zoning decisions made by counties and cities.

HB 319.summary: The bill would provide penalties for state and local officials and employees who do not comply with laws related to illegal aliens.

HB 32.summary: This bill would allow the Probate Court of Cook County to charge a technology fee and specify how the money collected can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover funds once the fee is no longer needed.

HB 320.summary: The bill would require solar panels to be recycled instead of discarded or disposed of in any other way. It would mandate that solar panels be delivered to a collection or processing facility that accepts them for recycling.

HB 321.summary: The bill would increase the state minimum wage to a living wage, as defined by the legislation.

HB 322.summary: The bill would revise the rules for the Georgia Board of Dentistry to issue licenses for teaching or instructing in accredited dental, dental hygiene schools, or academic medical centers.

HB 323.summary: This bill would allow Medicare supplement insurance policies to be issued and renewed for individuals under 65 years old who are eligible for Medicare due to disability or end-stage renal disease. It also sets open enrollment periods and limits how much insurers can charge these individuals for the policies.

HB 324.summary: This bill would give certain voters preferential treatment during advance voting and on election day. The preferential treatment applies to voters who are blind, deaf, an amputee, pregnant, or accompanied by young children or children with special needs.

HB 325.summary: The bill would revise certain definitions related to protective orders and military judges' processes for issuing protective orders involving members of the state militia.

HB 326.summary: This bill would require the state health benefit plan to provide the same level of coverage for nonopioid pain management drugs as it does for opioid pain management drugs, including similar annual deductibles, coinsurance, copayments, exclusions, and reductions.

HB 327.summary: The bill would amend laws related to financial institutions, power of attorney, court jurisdiction, domestic relations, and the disclosure of AIDS confidential information.

HB 328.summary: The bill would increase the annual limit for tax credits available for contributions to student scholarship organizations and extend the time allowed after preapproval to make these contributions.

HB 329.summary: The bill would allow certified nurse practitioners and physician assistants to perform artificial insemination.

HB 33.summary: This bill would allow the Magistrate Court of Cook County to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover money after the fee is no longer collected.

HB 330.summary: The bill would revise the income tax credits for contributions to law enforcement foundations.

HB 331.summary: The bill would prohibit the transfer of certain domestic animals at specific locations and provide exceptions, enforcement, and penalties. It also includes definitions.

HB 334.summary: The bill would require the Department of Community Health to review medications and treatments for sickle cell disease for Medicaid recipients each year and to provide for public input and an annual report.

HB 335.summary: The bill would amend the Quality Basic Education Act to address mental health risks for student athletes by providing guidelines and materials to educate athletes, their parents or guardians, school personnel, and coaches about mental health risks and raise awareness of mental health resources.

HB 336.summary: This bill would require local school systems to provide information about sickle cell disease to parents and guardians of students in grades six through twelve when other health information is given.

HB 337.summary: The bill would create the State Law Enforcement Officer Plan to offer enhanced retirement benefits for electing state law enforcement officers. It also sets conditions and limitations for the plan and establishes a deferred retirement option program.

HB 338.summary: The bill would create the State Law Enforcement Officer Plan to provide enhanced retirement benefits for certain state law enforcement officers. It also sets conditions and limitations for the plan and includes provisions for deferred retirement option program accounts.

HB 339.summary: This bill would exempt ride share drivers and ride share network services from being defined as motor carriers under Georgia law.

HB 34.summary: The bill would establish a system for professional licensing boards to track continuing education requirements for licensees.

HB 340.summary: This bill would require local school systems and public schools to create policies and procedures for the use of personal electronic devices by students in kindergarten through eighth grade during school and school-sponsored events.

HB 341.summary: The bill would create a tax credit for certain employers that offer individual coverage health reimbursement arrangements to their employees.

HB 342.summary: The bill would repeal certain advertising restrictions for licensees related to access to medical cannabis.

HB 344.summary: The bill would change the penalty amount for traffic violations captured by cameras on school buses.

HB 345.summary: The bill would stop insurance companies from raising liability insurance rates for five years.

HB 346.summary: This bill would stop municipalities and counties from using public, educational, and governmental programming (PEG) channels for political purposes.

HB 347.summary: The bill would provide compensation for pregnant women who are compelled to carry a pregnancy to term due to a fetal heartbeat law, instead of being able to choose to terminate the pregnancy.

HB 348.summary: The bill would allow limited purpose subsidiaries and captive insurance companies to offer more types of insurance and reinsurance. It affects these specific insurance companies.

HB 349.summary: The bill would change the provisions for filling vacancies on the Board of Commissioners of Douglas County.

HB 350.summary: The bill would revise provisions for safe places for newborns, allowing ambulance services to take physical custody of newborns and setting specifications for newborn safety devices.

HB 352.summary: This bill would revise coverage criteria to include Medicaid recipients with gestational diabetes for continuous glucose monitors.

HB 353.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Music Office and set out its duties. It would also provide for the adoption and promulgation of rules and regulations by the office.

HB 354.summary: The bill would exclude from evidence certain communications between an attorney and a client when the client is in a penal institution.

HB 355.summary: The bill would provide a process for filling vacancies in the offices of councilmember or mayor in the City of Doraville.

HB 356.summary: This bill would create the City of Doraville Building and Public Facilities Authority.

HB 357.summary: The bill would allow tax credits for certain contributions made by taxpayers to mortgage loan originators. It sets an annual limit and outlines terms and conditions for these credits.

HB 358.summary: The bill would amend a law to add a definition related to prohibiting foreign persons and entities from acquiring certain land in Georgia.

HB 359.summary: The bill would allow the City of Cedartown to hold a referendum to exercise redevelopment and other powers under the Georgia Constitution and Chapter 44 of Title 36 of the O.C.G.A., the 'Redevelopment Powers Law'.

HB 362.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from Bryan County school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes. The exemption would be for the amount by which the current year's assessed value of a homestead exceeds its adjusted base year assessed value.

HB 363.summary: This bill would include gatherings for religious worship, observance, or acknowledging the death of an individual as protected activities under the criminal trespass law.

HB 365.summary: The bill would create a temporary income tax credit for certain expenses related to projects that enhance industrial infrastructure and connectivity. The Department of Community Affairs would approve eligibility for this tax credit.

HB 366.summary: The bill would designate April 29 of each year as 'Heritage and Freedom Flag of the Former Republic of Vietnam Day' in Georgia.

HB 367.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Equity and Fairness Commission, set its members and officers, and outline its duties and powers. It also requires the commission to report on its activities.

HB 368.summary: The bill would require a law enforcement officer to tell a driver the reason for a traffic stop after the driver shows their driver's license, if the driver asks.

HB 369.summary: The bill would set equipment standards for motor vehicles used to sell food or beverages on roadways.

HB 37.summary: This bill would require local school systems to inform their employees about social security withholdings and eligibility for certain benefits, pension, or retirement plans.

HB 370.summary: This bill would require school districts that do not use the state-wide base year homestead exemption to include information about their reserve funds on property tax bills. HB 372.summary: The bill would remove a requirement for certain Teachers Retirement System beneficiaries to be hired to work in designated areas of highest need. It also extends provisions to the year 2030.

HB 373.summary: This bill would require major medical insurance coverage to include annual prostate cancer screenings for certain men. It also applies this requirement to the state employees' health insurance plan.

HB 374.summary: The bill would allow local governments to create databases for managing residential rental properties. HB 375.summary: This bill would exclude overtime pay from state income tax. Employers would need to report this change.

HB 376.summary: The bill would increase the amount of tax credits available for the rehabilitation of certified structures.

HB 379.summary: This bill would provide certain lien protections in divorce actions and require notice of standing orders in domestic relations actions.

HB 38.summary: The bill would revise the definition of an 'eligible student' for the needs based financial aid program in Georgia.

HB 380.summary: The bill would repeal the law that created the Lower Chattahoochee Regional Airport Authority and address the authority's assets and liabilities.

HB 381.summary: The bill would add Clay, Marion, and Webster counties to the Lower Chattahoochee Regional Transportation Authority and revise the appointment of members.

HB 382.summary: The bill would revise a provision in Georgia law related to Schedule I controlled substances, specifically regarding psilocybin.

HB 383.summary: This bill would allow high school student athletes and prospective student athletes to receive compensation for the use of their name, image, or likeness. It also sets a rule that contracts for such compensation automatically expire when the student athlete graduates or is no longer enrolled.

HB 384.summary: This bill would require all peace officers to swear a uniform oath, including aspirational language, and limit the legal effect of any aspirational parts of the oath. It also restricts the crime of violating an oath of a public officer to only codified oaths.

HB 385.summary: The bill would allow academically successful students who are pursuing both a baccalaureate degree and a first professional degree to use the full number of hours of HOPE scholarship eligibility.

HB 386.summary: The bill would exempt sales of clothing and school-related supplies from sales and use taxes during the last weekend of July each year.

HB 387.summary: This bill would require service delivery agreements to include a growth boundary agreement component, with some exceptions. It affects local government service delivery agreements.

HB 389.summary: This bill would stop condominium, property, and homeowners' associations from preventing owners from putting solar energy devices on common roofs or roof structures. It also sets rules for who pays for removing and reinstalling these devices and allows for repairing common roofs or roof structures.

HB 39.summary: This bill would allow the Magistrate Court of Habersham County to charge a technology fee, specify how the fee can be used, and outline how the funds should be managed and eventually terminated.

HB 390.summary: The bill would create a new crime called interference with a first responder and set penalties for it. It would also add this offense to the list of bail restricted offenses.

HB 391.summary: The bill would change certain provisions related to boxing, wrestling, and martial art associations and federations in Georgia.

HB 392.summary: The bill changes the dates for certain events related to the Georgia Tax Court, including when the chief court judge starts their duties and when the court begins accepting cases. It also deals with the transfer and handling of cases currently pending before the Georgia Tax Tribunal.

HB 393.summary: The bill would change traffic laws for bicycles, requiring cyclists to signal their intention to turn unless certain exceptions apply. It also sets standards for cyclists approaching intersections with stop signs.

HB 394.summary: The bill would increase the minimum wage for certain employees and eligible full-time state employees.

HB 395.summary: The bill would increase the minimum wage and provide a credit for employers of tipped workers. It also eliminates certain eligibility exemptions from the minimum wage.

HB 396.summary: This bill would amend the charter of the City of Acworth to adopt a certain map by reference.

HB 397.summary: This bill would allow municipalities to choose to provide advance voting on Saturdays for municipal elections.

HB 398.summary: The bill would allow the production and sale of certain food items from home kitchens, with specific exemptions, requirements, and disclosures. It also includes provisions for inspections and civil penalties.

HB 399.summary: The bill would require certain residential landlords to have in-state staff to manage communications with tenants.

HB 4.summary: This bill would require a three-day waiting period for the purchase or transfer of certain firearms. It also provides for exceptions and criminal penalties.

HB 400.summary: The bill would allow certain local governments to seek certifications from the Department of Community Affairs if they enact specific policies. These certifications could help these local governments get priority in grant and loan applications submitted to state agencies.

HB 401.summary: This bill would stop insurance companies from including advertising costs when setting or using insurance rates.

HB 402.summary: The bill would establish goals for renewable energy sources and a renewable energy portfolio standard for electric service providers, as set by the Public Service Commission. HB 403.summary: The bill aims to enhance protections for homeowners and tenants by revising or removing certain provisions that hinder housing stability.

HB 404.summary: This bill changes the boundaries of the City of Conyers. It adds nine listed properties, mostly along Milstead Avenue (Highway 20) and one on Old Covington Highway, in Rockdale County, to the city limits. Each parcel is described by its address and legal land description.

HB 405.summary: This bill would require insurance adjusters to also be licensed as contractors. It limits the type of adjuster license based on the contractor's license type and allows licensed contractors to become licensed adjusters.

HB 406.summary: The bill would increase the retirement age for superior court judges who start their positions on or after July 1, 2026.

HB 407.summary: The bill would create a tax credit for businesses that do business with Georgia-grown hemp owners and suppliers.

HB 408.summary: The bill would repeal prelicensing education requirements for certain insurance licenses and set a three-day limit on the reexamination waiting period for applicants.

HB 411.summary: The bill would change the description of the commissioner districts for Banks County. It also provides for the continuation in office of current members and sets effective dates.

HB 413.summary: This bill would stop local governments from making rules that ban mobile sawmills on agricultural land.

HB 414.summary: The bill would revise the definition of 'person' to include certain nonresidents of the state in election and campaign finance laws. It also gives the State Ethics Commission more power to investigate nonresidents and documents outside the state.

HB 415.summary: The bill would enact the Homeowners Protection Act and require a rental intention affidavit in dispossessory proceedings.

HB 416.summary: The bill would change which retailers can be charged fees in enterprise zones. It also updates the duration of enterprise zones.

HB 417.summary: The bill would revise the definition of an approved school for tuition equalization grants at private colleges and universities.

HB 418.summary: This bill would require the establishment of blocked trust accounts for minors who perform artistic or creative services in Georgia. It also gives the Commissioner of Labor the authority to investigate and determine the conditions of employment for child performers before they start working.

HB 419.summary: This bill would require institutions within the University System of Georgia and units within the Technical College System of Georgia to possess opioid antagonists.

HB 42.summary: The bill would revise how the State Board of Education calculates and distributes funds to local school districts for student transportation programs.

HB 420.summary: This bill would require certain health insurance policies to cover genetic testing for inherited mutations and cancer imaging under specific conditions. It also ensures that such coverage is not subject to cost-sharing requirements and protects the eligibility of health savings accounts.

HB 421.summary: The bill would establish a new crime for traveling to meet a minor for indecent purposes and set penalties for this offense.

HB 422.summary: The bill would require the state employees' health insurance plan to include high deductible health plans.

HB 423.summary: The bill would update laws related to emergency communications and the 9-1-1 system to include Next Generation 9-1-1 systems and services.

HB 608.summary: The bill would revise how vacancies on the Muscogee County School District board of education are filled.

HB 609.summary: The bill would revise rules about local government employees not being allowed to have an interest in redevelopment activities. It would limit this rule to employees whose job duties are related to such activities or areas.

HB 61.summary: The bill would allow separate license plates for hearses and ambulances.

HB 610.summary: This bill would allow municipal elected and appointed officials and employees to acquire property interests in redevelopment areas under certain conditions.

HB 611.summary: This bill would require publicly owned treatment works to ask industrial users about the manufacture or use of PFAS (forever chemicals).

HB 612.summary: The bill would add a member to the Behavioral Health Coordinating Council and establish a parity compliance review panel.

HB 613.summary: The bill would give preferences in certain public works construction contracts to contractors or subcontractors who participate in a registered apprenticeship program.

HB 614.summary: This bill would allow local governments to prohibit the use or ignition of consumer fireworks near facilities that house equines. It also provides for special event permits.

HB 615.summary: The bill would abolish the current membership structure of the Chatham County Recreation Authority and establish new board membership rules, including terms of office and quorum requirements.

HB 616.summary: The bill would revise a deduction related to depreciation for single-family residential rental property for income tax purposes.

HB 617.summary: This bill would reestablish a consumer utility counsel to represent consumers in matters before the Public Service Commission or other agencies concerning public utilities.

HB 618.summary: This bill would require sellers of real property in Georgia to disclose any flood damage to the property.

HB 619.summary: The bill would revise the election schedule for the mayor and councilmembers of the City of Donalsonville to better stagger their elections and provide for an interim term of office.

HB 62.summary: The bill would change rules for condominium and property owners' associations, including requirements for board members, voting, proxies, quorums, residency, and board size.

HB 620.summary: This bill would designate Blood Plasma Donation Awareness Day in Georgia.

HB 621.summary: This bill would allow members of the Georgia General Assembly to request assistance from the Georgia Bureau of Investigation.

HB 622.summary: This bill changes how much the mayor and city council members of Hoboken, Georgia are paid. The mayor would receive $475 per month, and each councilmember would receive $175 per month. They would also be repaid for actual and necessary expenses they have while doing their jobs.

HB 623.summary: This bill would allow the Probate Court of Carroll County to charge a technology fee and specify how the money can be used. It also sets rules for ending the fee and handling leftover funds.

HB 624.summary: The bill would allow the State Court of Carroll County to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover money after the fee is no longer collected.

HB 625.summary: The bill would provide an additional judge for the State Court of Fulton County.

HB 626.summary: The bill would extend the time period for retaining evidence in sexual assault cases when the victim does not report the assault immediately.

HB 627.summary: The bill would revise a provision related to the use of deadly weapons in juvenile proceedings and expand the types of offenses where the superior court has exclusive jurisdiction in juvenile cases.

HB 628.summary: The bill would revise an income tax credit for contributions to law enforcement foundations, increasing the annual contribution limit and extending the sunset date.

HB 629.summary: This bill would remove the requirement for a licensed physician in automated external defibrillator (AED) programs in educational settings.

HB 63.summary: The bill would establish a new offense for failing to adequately secure a loaded or unloaded firearm. It affects anyone who possesses a firearm in Georgia.

HB 630.summary: The bill would remove the used car division and the used parts division from the State Board of Registration of Used Motor Vehicle Dealers and Used Motor Vehicle Parts Dealers. It would also transfer the powers and duties of these divisions to the board and revise the board's membership and responsibilities.

HB 631.summary: This bill would require that the minimum base salary for certified professional personnel with bachelor's degrees in elementary and secondary education be based on the national average living wage, as determined by the State Board of Education.

HB 632.summary: This bill would clarify the eligibility of certain veterans for exemption from paying occupation taxes, administrative fees, and regulatory fees when engaging in peddling, operating businesses, or practicing professions.

HB 633.summary: This bill would allow caregivers to make absentee ballot applications for certain voters.

HB 634.summary: The bill would revise provisions for the expedited completion of a student's first Individualized Education Program under the Georgia Special Needs Scholarship Act. It also provides for calculating scholarship amounts, electronic deposits, and a compliance form.

HB 635.summary: The bill would revise and clarify the qualifications for becoming a licensed residential or commercial general contractor in Georgia, and it would also change how the State Licensing Board for Residential and Commercial General Contractors operates.

HB 636.summary: The bill would revise penalties for certain sexual offenses and provide for fines collected from these violations to be used for the Safe Harbor for Sexually Exploited Children Fund Commission.

HB 637.summary: The bill would change the requirement for public hearings before the Cobb County Board of Commissioners can spend over $100,000 to hire an independent consultant or conduct an independent study.

HB 638.summary: This bill would prohibit stopping or parking a motor vehicle other than a transit vehicle in a designated transit vehicle lane in the City of Atlanta.

HB 639.summary: The bill would expedite and prioritize processes for terminating parental rights in cases involving parental incapacity and child maltreatment.

HB 64.summary: The bill would require owners of assault weapons to have liability insurance to cover legal costs if something happens because of the weapon.

HB 640.summary: This bill would change how city offices in Alpharetta are elected, requiring a majority vote for candidates to win.

HB 641.summary: This bill would require electric suppliers to delay the discontinuation of electrical service to residential customers who have a serious illness for a certain period of time. It also sets notice requirements and allows for the renewal of the delay period.

HB 642.summary: The bill would stop public primary and secondary schools from serving or selling food or drinks that contain synthetic dye. It also requires certification of compliance with this rule.

HB 643.summary: This bill would require each public and private elementary and secondary school in Georgia to install key boxes at their buildings in locations agreed upon with local law enforcement and emergency management agencies.

HB 644.summary: This bill would allow the director of the Environmental Protection Division to look into and consider the regulatory history of a company in other states when reviewing permit applications.

HB 645.summary: This bill would repeal certain requirements for COVID-19 testing of staff members in long-term care facilities.

HB 646.summary: The bill would set minimum salaries for coroners and revise compensation for deputy coroners. It also removes certain death investigation fees.

HB 647.summary: The bill would change the corporate limits of the City of Mulberry.

HB 648.summary: The bill removes the income cap for a homestead exemption from City of College Park ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes for disabled residents and those 65 years of age or older.

HB 649.summary: This bill would require insurance coverage for comprehensive maternal mental health screening and care during and after pregnancy, as determined by a healthcare provider.

HB 65.summary: This bill would designate collard greens as the official state greens and potlikka as the official state dipping sauce of the official state bread in Georgia.

HB 650.summary: The bill would restore certain rights to individuals with criminal histories. It affects people with criminal records and amends laws related to courts, professions and businesses, property, and public officers and employees.

HB 651.summary: The bill would revise the rules for using automated traffic enforcement devices in school zones and allow district attorneys, solicitors-general, and prosecuting attorneys to enforce civil monetary penalties for speeding in school zones based on recorded evidence.

HB 652.summary: The bill would create an exception for collecting motor fuel taxes on electricity delivered by certain electric vehicle charging stations.

HB 653.summary: This bill would rename the Georgia Public Service Commission as the Georgia Public Utilities Commission. It also provides for the continuation of all rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and administrative orders of the current commission under the new name.

HB 654.summary: This bill would stop insurers from requiring prior authorization for medical tests, procedures, and prescription drugs before they pay for them.

HB 655.summary: The bill would renew a tax credit for postproduction expenditures and increase the annual limit. It also provides an additional credit for certain expenditures in rural counties.

HB 656.summary: This bill would allow local governments to charge development impact fees for public facilities that are created through agreements between developers and the government.

HB 657.summary: The bill would set qualifications for recovery community organizations dealing with substance use and provide for the certification of peer specialists in mental health.

HB 658.summary: The bill would provide certain consumer protections for insurance policies in Georgia if the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act is repealed. It includes provisions for preventive services at no additional cost and coverage for dependents up to age 26.

HB 659.summary: The bill would expand medical education funding and the service cancelable loan program to include optometrists.

HB 66.summary: The bill would expand the definition of a rental motor vehicle for ad valorem tax purposes.

HB 660.summary: This bill would stop the state health benefit plan and state funds from covering expenses for any transition-related interventions.

HB 661.summary: The bill aims to enhance penalties related to voter qualifications and registration.

HB 662.summary: The bill would revise the definition of 'rural hospital organization' in Georgia's tax credit eligibility rules.

HB 663.summary: The bill would revise the fee for motor vehicle emissions inspections.

HB 664.summary: This bill would allow property owners' associations to submit to certain provisions after their creation and set voting procedures for this submission. It also outlines how votes are recorded and notice is given.

HB 665.summary: The bill would transfer all environmental health responsibilities from county boards of health to the Department of Public Health.

HB 666.summary: This bill would add a sixth judge to the superior courts in the Clayton Judicial Circuit. It also specifies how the Governor should appoint this additional judge and how jurors should be selected for this circuit. Additionally, it allows for an extra court reporter in the Clayton Judicial Circuit.

HB 667.summary: The bill would set standards for when an employer or insurance provider is liable for actions related to a commercial vehicle driver. It affects commercial drivers and their employers or insurance providers.

HB 668.summary: The bill changes references to assistance and guide dogs to service dogs in laws about crimes and offenses, rights of persons with disabilities, and rules of the road. It also adds a criminal penalty for anyone who harms or kills a service dog.

HB 669.summary: This bill would provide low-wealth capital outlay grants to certain local school systems that award contracts for roofing improvements to suppliers meeting specific criteria.

HB 67.summary: This bill would amend the General Appropriations Act for the State Fiscal Year starting July 1, 2024, and ending June 30, 2025, to make changes to the state's budget for various government departments, boards, commissions, institutions, and other agencies, as well as for the university system, common schools, counties, municipalities, and other entities.

HB 670.summary: This bill would create comprehensive state civil rights laws to protect individuals from discrimination in housing, public accommodations, and employment based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, and age.

HB 671.summary: This bill would allow people to sue anyone who knowingly or negligently engages in sexually explicit conduct in the presence of a minor, or who knowingly or negligently allows a minor to be present while another person engages in such conduct.

HB 672.summary: The bill would require perinatal facilities in Georgia to implement evidence-based implicit bias programs for their healthcare professionals. These programs would include specific components and require initial and refresher training.

HB 673.summary: This bill would limit bars to first offender treatment for certain minor offenders who are adjudicated as adults. It also provides for retroactive first offender treatment under certain circumstances.

HB 674.summary: The bill would require the State Board of Education to create content standards for teaching financial literacy and money management in grades four and five. Local school boards would then have to provide this instruction.

HB 675.summary: The bill would create criminal offenses related to providing material support for terrorism and set penalties for these offenses. It would also establish guidelines for law enforcement investigations.

HB 676.summary: The bill would impose a fine for filing a frivolous mechanic's lien. It affects property law.

HB 677.summary: This bill would provide for certain placement procedures for children upon discharge from a hospital or psychiatric residential treatment facility in certain circumstances. It also amends provisions related to patient protection to provide for per diem payments to hospitals or psychiatric residential treatment facilities.

HB 678.summary: The bill would give authorities with limited jurisdiction the same legal protections from lawsuits as counties have.

HB 679.summary: The bill would prohibit agreements that fix rental prices for residential properties as unenforceable contracts that restrain trade. It also provides a criminal penalty for violating this prohibition.

HB 68.summary: This is Georgia's general budget bill for the state fiscal year running July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2026. It provides appropriations for state government and its departments, boards, commissions, and other agencies. It also covers the university system, common schools, counties, municipalities, and political subdivisions.

HB 680.summary: This bill would stop employers that do not provide affordable health insurance from asking employees to give a doctor's note when they are absent from work.

HB 681.summary: This bill would allow people to request that their name change petitions be sealed.

HB 682.summary: This bill would prevent the death penalty from being imposed if the only evidence of the defendant's guilt is the testimony of a single eyewitness.

HB 683.summary: This bill would allow local fire ordinances to require fire sprinklers in one- and two-family dwellings, even though the state residential and fire building code does not require them.

HB 684.summary: This bill would allow schools of barbering, cosmetology, and hair design to teach trichology training courses. It also requires certain teachers and instructors to complete 50 hours of trichology training.

HB 685.summary: This bill would allow for the creation of one or more community improvement districts in Bartow County. It would also provide for the purposes of these districts and define general obligation bonds, notes, and other obligations of the districts.

HB 686.summary: This bill would allow and regulate sports betting in Georgia, including setting up rules for sports betting licensees and excluding certain payments from being considered illegal gambling.

HB 687.summary: This bill would require landlords to give tenants a detailed list of existing damage to the rental property and an itemization of all fees before the tenant pays a security deposit.

HB 688.summary: This bill would allow service of legal process by certified mail and statutory overnight delivery with return receipt requested.

HB 689.summary: The bill would establish a homelessness prevention program and set up an application process and minimum standards for it. It would also specify how certain funds can be used and how disbursements should be made.

HB 69.summary: This bill would amend the General Appropriations Act for the State Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2024, and ending June 30, 2025, to make, provide, and change certain appropriations for the operation of the state government and its departments, boards, bureaus, commissions, institutions, and other agencies, as well as for the university system, common schools, counties, municipalities, and political subdivisions.

HB 690.summary: The bill would add a duty of care for pharmacy benefits managers to insured individuals, health plans, and providers. It also provides for definitions, rules and regulations, a priority of duties, and a private right of action.

HB 691.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Resilience Office under the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency. It would establish a board of directors and outline their duties, as well as provide for hiring staff and funding.

HB 692.summary: This bill would require registered professional nurses and advanced practice registered nurses working in outpatient settings to notify their supervising or delegating physician immediately if they receive a complaint or report from the Georgia Board of Nursing.

HB 693.summary: The bill would expand the definition of 'approved school' for tuition equalization grants at private colleges and universities.

HB 694.summary: The bill would allow the State Board of Education to create a five-year pilot program aimed at increasing high school graduation rates and preparing more students for postsecondary education by providing better counseling and preparation services in secondary schools.

HB 695.summary: The bill would create a needs-based financial aid program through the Georgia Student Finance Authority to award grants to eligible students who have not yet received their financial aid awards, helping them get the materials needed to start classes.

HB 696.summary: The bill would provide for school lunch and breakfast programs for public school students in Georgia, offering these meals at no cost to students attending the lowest performing 25 percent of schools in the state.

HB 697.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from City of Chickamauga independent school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes. The exemption would be $50,000 for residents aged 70 or older, and the full assessed value for other residents.

HB 698.summary: This bill would give some Walker County school district homeowners a break on school property taxes. Residents 70 and older would get a $50,000 homestead exemption. Residents 75 and older who have lived in the district five years or more would be exempt on the full assessed value of their homestead. Voters in the district would decide in November 2026.

HB 699.summary: This bill would change the terms of the board of elections and registration for Dawson County to be staggered.

HB 7.summary: This bill would provide a tax credit for graduates who are employed in high-tech full-time jobs in rural counties.

HB 70.summary: HB 70 would amend the General Appropriations Act for the State Fiscal Year starting July 1, 2024, to make changes in funding for state government operations, departments, boards, and other agencies, as well as for the university system, common schools, counties, and municipalities.

HB 700.summary: The bill would limit the amount of surcharges that merchants can charge for purchases made with credit cards. It affects merchants and consumers.

HB 701.summary: This bill would allow the Probate Court of Terrell County and the judge serving as the Magistrate Court judge to collect a technology fee. It also specifies how the fee can be used and what happens to any leftover funds.

HB 702.summary: The bill would make sponsors of direct initiative petitions campaign committees and ban the use of public funds to advocate for or against such petitions.

HB 703.summary: This bill would increase the income cap for residents of Peachtree City to qualify for a homestead exemption from ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes from $30,000 to $60,000.

HB 704.summary: The bill would change the requirement for the state auditor to produce monthly reports on architectural and engineering firms doing business with the state to annual reports. It also removes certain requirements.

HB 705.summary: This bill would prohibit traffic stops based solely on the fact that a person is operating a motorcycle or wearing motorcycle-related gear.

HB 706.summary: The bill would require coursework and educational programs on the history of Black Americans and their contributions to American society in schools.

HB 707.summary: The bill would limit rent increases for seniors and veterans in Georgia. It also provides definitions and defense in dispossessory actions.

HB 708.summary: The bill would allow renters to deduct the costs of certain repairs from their rental payments. It also changes the time required for responses and the effectiveness of writs of possession.

HB 709.summary: This bill would allow the City of Demorest to use redevelopment powers under Georgia law and to hold a referendum on the matter.

HB 71.summary: HB 71 would provide appropriations for the State Fiscal Year starting July 1, 2025, and ending June 30, 2026, covering various state government operations, departments, and agencies, as well as educational and local government activities.

HB 710.summary: The bill would set limits on how much landlords can increase rental amounts for residential properties. It would also make charging rental amounts above these limits an unlawful, unfair, and deceptive trade practice.

HB 711.summary: The bill would prohibit the possession of devices that attach to firearms to produce rapid fire, and it would revise and add definitions related to this prohibition. It also provides for exceptions and punishment.

HB 712.summary: This bill would stop property tax bills from including any fees or assessments that are not related to taxes.

HB 713.summary: This bill would prevent the General Assembly from making rules or policies that limit the number of bills or resolutions a member can file or introduce during a legislative session. It also aims to ensure that no rules, policies, or procedures are put in place that would limit or obstruct members' abilities to fulfill their duties.

HB 714.summary: The bill would revise provisions related to the designation of electors and the appointment and election of board members for community improvement districts in the City of Rincon.

HB 715.summary: The bill would prohibit the use of artificial intelligence or automated decision tools without human oversight in making certain housing determinations and would also restrict certain defenses in actions for discriminatory housing practices.

HB 716.summary: The bill would establish a needs-based grant program to help postsecondary students who are facing food insecurity. The program would be run by the Georgia Student Finance Authority.

HB 717.summary: This bill would regulate the administration of psychedelic-assisted treatment and therapy, including setting standards and requirements and licensing clinics.

HB 718.summary: The bill would establish the first week of April each year as 'Women's Golf Week' in Georgia.

HB 719.summary: This bill changes how much Worth County board of education members are paid. The chairperson would receive $300 per day and each other member $200 per day for attending board meetings or committee meetings and travel on official board business approved in advance by a majority of the board. Actual expenses would also be reimbursed. It takes effect on the first day of the month after it becomes law.

HB 72.summary: The bill would provide funding for the operation of state government and its departments, boards, bureaus, commissions, institutions, and other agencies, as well as for the university system, common schools, counties, municipalities, and political subdivisions for the State Fiscal Year beginning July 1, 2025, and ending June 30, 2026.

HB 720.summary: The bill would revise the compensation of members of the Board of Education of Lee County.

HB 721.summary: The bill would add new requirements for transportation referral service providers and ride share network services regarding driver safety, hiring practices, and the privacy of personal information for drivers and passengers.

HB 722.summary: This bill would provide for a chief judge and an associate judge in the State Court of Bryan County. It also specifies that the associate judge would be initially appointed by the Governor.

HB 723.summary: This bill would allow taxpayers to get a tax credit for expenses they incur when providing a warming center to unsheltered individuals during days of inclement weather.

HB 724.summary: This bill would change the terms of the mayor and city council members in Pembroke to four years.

HB 725.summary: The bill would amend Georgia law to add new duties for landlords regarding certain rental agreements.

HB 726.summary: The bill would limit the amount of surcharges that merchants can charge for customers using credit cards. It affects merchants and credit card users.

HB 727.summary: The bill would add a post-employment restriction for state employees involved in state purchasing.

HB 728.summary: The bill would limit the effective date of rules or regulations adopted by the State Election Board before a primary, election, or runoff.

HB 729.summary: The bill would establish programs to provide obstetric care in areas with low access to maternity care and maternity care deserts. It would also create a student loan repayment program for certain obstetric providers and a grant program for perinatal facilities.

HB 73.summary: This bill would change future elections for members of the Seminole County Board of Education to be nonpartisan.

HB 730.summary: The bill would amend the Chatham-Savannah Authority for the Homeless Act to provide for membership, meetings, purposes, and definitions. It also includes legislative findings.

HB 731.summary: This bill would create an alternative homestead option sales tax and specify how the tax proceeds are distributed. It also allows certain counties to levy a special purpose local option sales and use tax, subject to a referendum.

HB 732.summary: This bill would allow the Glynn County governing authority to levy an excise tax as permitted by a specific section of the O.C.G.A. It also sets procedures, conditions, and limitations for this tax.

HB 733.summary: The bill would increase transparency and accountability in the insurance industry and at the office of the Commissioner of Insurance. It would also allow an advocate to review and investigate complaints and request a hearing.

HB 734.summary: This bill would allow the City of Vidalia to use redevelopment powers under Georgia law and hold a referendum on the matter.

HB 735.summary: This bill would allow the City of Lyons, Georgia, to use redevelopment powers under the Georgia Constitution and the 'Redevelopment Powers Law'. It also provides for a referendum.

HB 736.summary: The bill would add and revise definitions for policies prohibiting bullying and cyberbullying in schools. It also requires the provision of certain information related to these policies.

HB 737.summary: This bill would allow the governing authority of Haralson County to levy an excise tax according to a specific section of Georgia law.

HB 738.summary: This bill would abolish the elected position of county surveyor in Butts County and instead provide for the appointment of a county surveyor by the county's governing authority. It also sets qualifications for the position and provides for successors.

HB 739.summary: The bill would allow the City of Lawrenceville to annex certain territory into its boundaries and provide for a referendum on the annexation.

HB 74.summary: The bill would correct a reference in the Georgia Lottery for Education Act and apply certain provisions of the Georgia Administrative Procedure Act to bona fide coin-operated amusement machines.

HB 740.summary: The bill would create standards for first grade readiness and policies for placement and promotion in kindergarten and grades one and two. It also sets a timetable for these policies to be implemented.

HB 741.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from Bryan County school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes for homeowners whose current year's assessed value of their homestead exceeds the base year's assessed value.

HB 742.summary: The bill would increase the compensation of the mayor and councilmembers in the City of Broxton, Georgia.

HB 743.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from City of Social Circle ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes for homeowners whose current year's assessed value of their homestead exceeds the adjusted base year's assessed value.

HB 744.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from City of Walnut Grove ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes for certain property owners.

HB 745.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from City of Loganville ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes. The exemption would be for the amount by which the current year's assessed value of a homestead exceeds the adjusted base year's assessed value.

HB 746.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from City of Monroe ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes for homeowners whose current year's assessed value of their homestead exceeds the adjusted base year's assessed value.

HB 747.summary: The bill would change the compensation of judges in the State Court of Cobb County.

HB 748.summary: The bill would change the compensation of the coroner in Carroll County.

HB 749.summary: The bill would change the annual salary of the chairperson and members of the Board of Commissioners of Carroll County.

HB 75.summary: The bill would change how government agencies handle and care for impounded domesticated animals, requiring a court order before any such animal can be euthanized. It also addresses liability issues related to the death or loss of impounded animals.

HB 750.summary: This bill would add a judge to the State Court of Forsyth County.

HB 751.summary: The bill would allow the Department of Community Health to request a Section 1115 waiver from the federal government for Medicare and Medicaid services. It also authorizes additional qualifying activity types.

HB 752.summary: The bill would require firefighters, paramedics, cardiac technicians, and peace officers to receive training on how to handle encounters with individuals who have physical, mental, or neurological conditions that affect their ability to communicate.

HB 753.summary: The bill would create the Better Georgia Without Blight Fund to provide financing and technical assistance for fixing up old or run-down buildings.

HB 754.summary: The bill would require the Board of Education of Catoosa County to have an internal audit function and establish the position of internal auditor. It also outlines the selection, powers, and duties of the internal auditor.

HB 755.summary: This bill would allow Cherokee County to levy an excise tax as permitted by state law.

HB 756.summary: The bill would abolish the current memberships of the Chatham Area Transit Authority and establish a new board membership structure with defined terms of office.

HB 757.summary: The bill would require registration of kratom products and sworn certification of compliance. It also provides for the publication of registration information and revises penalties.

HB 758.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from Spalding County school district ad valorem taxes for residents aged 65 or older, with the exemption amount based on their income, excluding certain retirement income.

HB 759.summary: The bill would update the terms of board members, revise meeting procedures, rename the elections supervisor as the elections director, and allow the board to hire its own legal counsel for Spalding County's board of elections.

HB 76.summary: This bill would require the Department of Transportation to hold public hearings for local transportation projects that have a significant impact.

HB 760.summary: The bill would change the annual salary of the chairperson and members of the Glynn County Board of Commissioners. It also provides for withholding compensation for certain meeting absences.

HB 761.summary: The bill would increase the homestead exemption from ad valorem taxes for certain residents of the City of Lilburn. It would raise the exemption amount for residents aged 65 or older or those who are disabled.

HB 762.summary: The bill would create the Savannah Music Commission, define its membership and duties, and provide for tax exemptions for the commission.

HB 763.summary: The bill would create the Richmond Hill-Bryan County Airport Authority, a new entity for the County of Bryan and the City of Richmond Hill. It would also ensure that the city or county does not incur liability or debt through the authority's actions and would make the authority's bonds tax-exempt.

HB 764.summary: This bill would change how vacancies in the offices of mayor or city council member in the City of Nelson are filled. It also provides for special elections.

HB 765.summary: This bill would amend the Fair Business Practices Act to provide rules for medical debt collection, including information on medical assistance, interest and fees, payment plans, and restrictions on collection during health insurance appeals.

HB 766.summary: The bill would create and establish the Sumter-Americus County Unification Commission. It would also provide for the membership of the commission and the certification of election results.

HB 767.summary: The bill would revise the provisions regarding the compensation of members of the Gwinnett County Board of Education. It also includes a provision to suspend these revised compensation provisions if the board approves a buyout of the superintendent's contract.

HB 768.summary: The bill would provide a supplement for the chief judge of the State Court of Gwinnett County.

HB 769.summary: The bill would change the provisions related to salary supplements for judges in the Gwinnett Judicial Circuit.

HB 77.summary: The bill would revise the responsibilities of drivers when they encounter a funeral procession on a two-lane highway.

HB 770.summary: The bill would provide an additional supplement for the chief judge of the Gwinnett Judicial Circuit.

HB 771.summary: This bill would change a Cherokee County School District property tax exemption for residents who are disabled or at least 62 and meet an income limit. It would waive the five-year homestead requirement for the surviving spouse of someone who got the exemption. It would take effect only if Cherokee County school district voters approve it in an election no later than November 2026.

HB 772.summary: The bill would increase the homestead exemption from city ad valorem taxes for residents of Norcross who own and occupy their residences, and for those who are 62 years old or older and own and occupy their residences.

HB 773.summary: This bill would allow certain people who are required to join the Public School Employees Retirement System to instead join the Teachers Retirement System of Georgia. The bill also sets conditions and prevents the transfer of creditable service.

HB 774.summary: This bill would allow the Probate Court of DeKalb County to charge a technology fee and specify how the money from this fee can be used. It also sets rules for ending the fee and handling any leftover money.

HB 775.summary: This bill would increase the homestead exemption from Butts County School District ad valorem taxes for residents aged 62 or older from $15,000 to $50,000.

HB 776.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from Fulton County school district property taxes for residents who are 70 years old or older. The exemption would cover 50 percent of the assessed value of their home.

HB 777.summary: This bill would provide a 25 percent homestead exemption from Fulton County school district ad valorem taxes for residents who are 65 years of age or older.

HB 778.summary: This bill would allow the Magistrate Court of Upson County to charge a technology fee and specify how the money from this fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover funds once the fee is no longer collected.

HB 779.summary: This bill would require landlords and managers of apartment buildings or complexes to provide local police and fire departments with certain information. It also sets a penalty for not following this requirement.

HB 78.summary: The bill would increase the limit on the total percentage of funds that the Employees' Retirement System of Georgia can invest in alternative investments.

HB 780.summary: The bill would provide a homestead exemption from City of Greensboro ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes. The exemption would be for an amount equal to the difference between the current year's assessed value and the adjusted base year's assessed value of a homestead.

HR 753.summary: This resolution creates a House Study Committee to examine ways to improve access to internal medicine in rural areas.

HR 754.summary: Creates a House Study Committee to examine street lighting along state routes.

HR 755.summary: This resolution creates a House Study Committee to examine electric franchise fees for unincorporated areas.

HR 756.summary: This resolution encourages the General Assembly to protect immigrant survivors of gender-based violence and human trafficking by ensuring they can safely report crimes to law enforcement without fear of abuse of information.

HR 757.summary: This resolution creates a House Study Committee to examine civil rights protections.

HR 8.summary: The resolution supports creating a State Workgroup to Increase Chronic Disease Information and Screenings in Communities of Color.

HR 815.summary: This resolution creates a House Study Committee to explore the potential use of humanoids and robotics in Georgia's workforce development.

HR 816.summary: This resolution creates a House Study Committee to examine an At-Risk Populations Abuse Registry.

HR 817.summary: This resolution creates a House Study Committee to examine the use of drones and unmanned aircraft from foreign adversaries by the government.

HR 847.summary: This resolution creates a House Study Committee to evaluate funding for public health.

HR 859.summary: Creates a House Study Committee to examine inclusive educational settings for students with disabilities.

HR 882.summary: This resolution proposes a constitutional amendment allowing local school systems to collect a sales and use tax for their maintenance and operation expenses. It also requires these systems to reduce their millage rates by an amount equal to the tax proceeds collected.

HR 883.summary: This resolution creates a House Study Committee to examine ways to make Georgia the top state for tourism.

HR 885.summary: This resolution creates a House Study Committee to examine election procedures.

HR 887.summary: This resolution creates a House Study Committee to look into ways to reduce and prioritize mandates for public school administration.

HR 905.summary: The bill encourages the Department of Education to create a public awareness campaign for students in grades K-12 about blockchain, cryptocurrency, and Web3.

HR 947.summary: This resolution creates a House Study Committee to examine the permit issuance process for the Five Points MARTA station.

HR 948.summary: This resolution creates a House Study Committee to examine Pharmacy Benefits Managers and their impact on consumer access to prescription medications.

HR 952.summary: This resolution creates a House Study Committee to examine the risks associated with hair straightening products.

HR 97.summary: This resolution authorizes the state to convey, lease, or exchange certain properties located in various counties.

HR 98.summary: This resolution would allow the granting of non-exclusive easements for the construction, installation, operation, and maintenance of facilities, utilities, roads, and access points on state-owned property in specified counties.

HR 99.summary: This resolution proposes a constitutional amendment to allow the General Assembly to use public funds for baby bond savings programs without requiring a benefit in return. It also authorizes the creation of the Baby Bond Savings Plan Trust Fund.

HR 995.summary: This resolution notifies the Senate that the House of Representatives has convened.

HR 996.summary: This resolution notifies the Governor that the Georgia General Assembly has convened.

HR 997.summary: This resolution calls for a joint session of the Georgia House of Representatives and the Senate to hear a message from the Governor and invites the Justices of the Supreme Court and the Judges of the Court of Appeals to attend.

HR 998.summary: This resolution addresses meetings and adjournments of the General Assembly.

SB 1.summary: The bill would provide rules for fair and safe participation in middle school, high school, and college sports. It aims to ensure equal athletic opportunities and safety for students.

SB 10.summary: The bill would add an additional judge to the superior courts of the Alapaha Judicial Circuit.

SB 100.summary: This bill would allow certain adopted adults to receive a copy of their original birth certificate. It also sets a fee for this service and standardizes the terminology used for birth certificates.

SB 101.summary: The bill would require testing for Duchenne muscular dystrophy as part of the newborn screening system.

SB 102.summary: The bill would revise laws related to dogfighting and prohibit the fighting of dogs and game cocks. It would also prohibit the possession or sale of objects related to dogfighting and provide for punishment.

SB 103.summary: The bill would stop companies owned or operated by Iran from bidding on or proposing for state contracts in Georgia.

SB 104.summary: This bill would stop the use or installation of any artificial intelligence system on state equipment if the company that developed or deployed the system is linked to the People's Republic of China.

SB 105.summary: The bill would allow licensed veterinarians and veterinary technicians to provide veterinary advice and triage over the phone or internet. It also allows licensed veterinarians to provide telemedicine services under certain conditions.

SB 106.summary: The bill would repeal a section of Georgia law that restricts local governments from regulating rent.

SB 107.summary: The bill would provide protections for homeowners in community associations, monitor elections for boards of directors in these associations, and require annual registration of community associations with related fees.

SB 108.summary: This bill would require property owners' associations to provide certificates of good standing for members who have paid their annual assessments. It also requires associations to offer alternative dispute resolution before placing a lien on a property for unpaid assessments and states that such a lien would be inferior to liens for unpaid medical bills.

SB 109.summary: This bill would stop group life insurance policies from excluding or limiting coverage for deaths that happen while a person is serving active duty in the military.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 11.summary: The bill would provide for creditable service for certain military service towards retirement benefits. It also specifies how to apply and receive payment for this service.

SB 110.summary: The bill would revise the definition of neglect in the juvenile code and add new definitions. It also provides an exception to certain offenses of reckless conduct.

SB 111.summary: The bill would enact the Georgia Consumer Privacy Protection Act to protect the privacy of consumer personal data in the state. It would define terms, set applicability, and provide exemptions. It would also establish responsibilities for processors and controllers of consumer data and require notice and disclosure.

SB 112.summary: The bill would extend certain protections for consumers related to warranties of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems and their components. It also requires specific information on warranty and product registration cards and forms.

SB 113.summary: This bill would allow the Georgia Composite Board of Professional Counselors, Social Workers, and Marriage and Family Therapists to create a professional health program to monitor and help impaired healthcare professionals.

SB 114.summary: This bill would establish procedures for redistricting the General Assembly and congressional districts in Georgia, including hearings, information availability, and notifications.

SB 115.summary: This bill would exempt sales of clothing and school-related supplies from sales and use taxes during the second week of August each year.

SB 116.summary: This bill would require Georgia detention facilities, including county jails and state penal institutions, to collect a DNA sample by oral swab or other noninvasive method from a person charged with a misdemeanor or felony who is subject to an immigration detainer notice. The sample is collected only if federal immigration authorities do not take the person into custody within 48 hours, not counting weekends and holidays. The facility sends the sample to the Division of Forensic Sciences.

SB 117.summary: The bill would make it a misdemeanor offense for violations related to complaints by public employees.

SB 118.summary: The bill would require the state's payroll system to allow deductions for credit unions.

SB 119.summary: The bill would provide exceptions to when a manufactured home becomes real property and would preserve the rights and remedies of prior lien or security interest holders in certain manufactured homes.

SB 12.summary: The bill would revise provisions related to public records inspection, including documents and records held by private persons or entities. It also updates definitions and judicial enforcement provisions.

SB 120.summary: The bill would prevent public schools, local education agencies, and public postsecondary institutions from promoting, supporting, or maintaining programs or activities that advocate for diversity, equity, and inclusion. It also provides for sanctions.

SB 121.summary: The bill would increase the minimum uninsured motorist coverage required under motor vehicle liability policies for individuals convicted of driving under the influence or reckless driving.

SB 122.summary: The bill would regulate the manufacture, distribution, and sale of malt beverages, including providing definitions and a short title for the regulation.

SB 123.summary: The bill updates and revises Georgia's compulsory school attendance laws. It also ensures that students cannot be expelled solely due to absenteeism and establishes reporting requirements.

SB 124.summary: The bill would require the State School Superintendent and the Department of Education to follow federal guidance documents, including those related to expanding educational freedom and opportunities for families.

SB 125.summary: The bill would change the order of experience and examination requirements for professional engineers and land surveyors.

SB 126.summary: This bill would change the age requirement for students to enroll in completion special schools from 18 to 16.

SB 127.summary: The bill would make new disclosure and notification requirements for automatic renewal provisions in service contracts with small businesses.

SB 128.summary: The bill would provide grants to local school districts for students living in poverty. It also sets rules for how the grant funds must be used.

SB 129.summary: The bill would increase the property tax exemption for totally disabled veterans and create new property tax exemptions for partially disabled veterans and first responders.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 13.summary: The bill would allow the Georgia Environmental Finance Authority to finance and perform duties related to natural gas facilities.

SB 130.summary: This bill would expand medical education funding and the service cancelable loan program for physicians in certain residency or fellowship programs.

SB 131.summary: The bill would establish the Georgia Health Care Professionals Data System to collect and display data from state licensing boards on a publicly accessible website.

SB 132.summary: This bill would require a court to hold a hearing before ordering an evaluation of a person's mental competency to stand trial. It also sets different procedures for cases involving nonviolent misdemeanor offenses.

SB 133.summary: The bill would enact the 'Blind Persons' Braille Literacy Rights and Education Act', setting license requirements for Braille for certain teachers.
