SB 134.summary: The bill would repeal Chapter 2B of Title 20, which includes the Georgia Education Savings Authority and the Georgia Promise Scholarship Act.

SB 135.summary: The bill would restrict the development of residential structures on certain coastal islands.

SB 136.summary: The bill would repeal existing laws about midwifery and create new licensing rules for community midwives. It also sets up a board to oversee the licensing process.

SB 137.summary: The bill would revise the jurisdiction of the municipal court for the City of Mulberry and make related changes.

SB 138.summary: This bill would provide for the transition of certain services related to newly incorporated municipalities in certain counties. It also revises provisions related to population data for insurance purposes.

SB 139.summary: The bill would change the boundaries of the City of Mulberry.

SB 14.summary: This bill would allow the General Assembly to provide for the nonpartisan election of district attorneys and solicitors-general of state courts, and set rules for how they qualify for office.

SB 140.summary: The bill would allow doctors of optometry to dispense and sell pharmaceutical agents to patients under certain conditions.

SB 141.summary: This bill would extend the time to appeal or protest a tax assessment from 30 days to 45 days.

SB 142.summary: The bill would provide for certain licensure for qualifying international medical graduates, including provisional, limited, and full licenses for physicians.

SB 143.summary: This bill would allow certain members of the Georgia Firefighter's Pension Fund to retire at age 50. It also provides an exception for the fund to invest in assets that might not be allowed for other public retirement systems.

SB 144.summary: This bill would prevent manufacturers from being held responsible for not warning consumers about health risks of pesticides beyond what the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency requires.

SB 145.summary: This bill would add a sixth judge to the superior courts in the Augusta Judicial Circuit and allow the Governor to appoint this additional judge.

SB 146.summary: The bill would provide regulations and protections for cemeteries and burial grounds, and revise procedures for permits related to disinterment and reinterment of human remains.

SB 147.summary: This bill would allow inmates to give consent for the release of their criminal history, vocational, and educational information upon release from correctional institutions.

SB 148.summary: The bill would create a pilot program for outdoor learning spaces in public schools. It also requires an evaluation and report on the program.

SB 149.summary: The bill would revise the definition of an approved school for tuition equalization grants at private colleges and universities.

SB 15.summary: This bill would allow the Georgia General Assembly to pass local legislation for nonpartisan elections for county governing authorities.

SB 150.summary: The bill would allow public school systems to hire certain retired teachers from the Teachers Retirement System of Georgia as full-time classroom teachers until June 30, 2034. It also reduces the number of years a retired teacher must have worked before being eligible for rehire.

SB 151.summary: The bill would create the Joint Development Authority of North Fulton Municipalities, define its powers, and establish procedures for issuing revenue bonds and other financial obligations.

SB 152.summary: The bill would allow the biological or adopted children of foster parents to qualify for Georgia Promise Scholarship accounts if they meet certain conditions.

SB 153.summary: The bill would revise, modernize, correct errors or omissions in, and reenact the statutory portion of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated. It would also repeal outdated or unconstitutional portions of the code.

SB 154.summary: The bill would revise or remove references to the United States Department of Education from the Official Code of Georgia Annotated. It also replaces a reference to student aid reports with FAFSA submission summary.

SB 155.summary: The bill would amend insurance laws to add census tracts to the list of factors insurers cannot consider when setting rates. It also addresses insurer premium rate increases.

SB 156.summary: The bill would add census tracts to the list of factors insurers cannot consider when setting rates and would address premium rate increases by insurers.

SB 157.summary: This bill would allow certain members or former members of the General Assembly to buy into the Georgia Legislative Retirement System.

SB 158.summary: The bill would create a new Commission for Blind and Visually Disabled Persons and transfer the Georgia Industries for the Blind from the Georgia Vocational Rehabilitation Agency to this new commission.

SB 159.summary: This bill would change how pretrial proceedings are handled in capital offense cases when the accused has intellectual disability. It includes provisions for notice of intent to claim intellectual disability, pretrial determination of intellectual disability, and specific verdicts and procedures for capital cases.

SB 16.summary: The bill would modify rules for public officials engaging in the bail bond business.

SB 160.summary: The bill would change the penalty for a second offense of reckless stunt driving from the forfeiture of a motor vehicle to requiring the installation of a device that limits the speed of the vehicle.

SB 161.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from Gordon County school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes. The exemption would be for the amount by which the current year's assessed value of a homestead exceeds the adjusted base year's assessed value.

SB 162.summary: The bill would require the Georgia Composite Medical Board to implement an automated system for credentialing healthcare providers in the state.

SB 163.summary: The bill would revise the standards for bringing a legal action against the government for unauthorized acts related to weapon regulations under the Brady Law.

SB 164.summary: The bill would prohibit businesses from using surveillance to set different prices for customers or to pay workers different wages based on surveillance information.

SB 165.summary: This bill would allow minors or their parents or guardians to request the termination of a minor's social media account and the deletion of the minor's personal information from the account. It also increases the amount of fines that social media platform providers may be liable for and creates a civil remedy for minors to recover damages.

SB 166.summary: The bill would revise provisions related to ordinances for governing and policing unincorporated areas of counties. It also authorizes enhanced monetary penalties for repeated violations of certain ordinances.

SB 167.summary: The bill would require private entities to take steps to prevent discrimination caused by AI systems they use. It would also regulate the use of automated decision systems for certain consequential decisions and provide exemptions and trade secret protections.

SB 168.summary: The bill would revise provisions for reducing the state income tax over time and remove certain conditions for this rate reduction.

SB 169.summary: The bill would require licensed physical therapists to complete certain education and training requirements before performing dry needling.

SB 17.summary: The bill would require local school systems to set up a mobile panic alert system to connect different emergency services technologies and ensure real-time coordination.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 170.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Interagency Council for the Homeless, outlining its purpose, membership, and duties, and requiring reporting of its activities.

SB 171.summary: The bill would require the State Board of Education to develop an advanced mathematics pathway and allow local school systems to offer this pathway to students in grades three through five.

SB 172.summary: This bill would repeal laws that allow the use of automated traffic enforcement safety devices to enforce speeding violations in school zones. It also prohibits local governing bodies or law enforcement agencies from entering into or renewing contracts for such enforcement.

SB 173.summary: The bill would allow people filing uncontested motions in superior courts and state courts to file notices of these motions. It also states that uncontested motions will be automatically granted, and it requires the chief judge to review any judge with two uncontested motions deemed granted on their docket.

SB 174.summary: The bill would amend laws related to criminal trial procedures, stating the legislative intent and rules for preserving and reviewing errors in court proceedings.

SB 175.summary: The bill would stop the use of ranked-choice voting in elections and primaries in Georgia, with some exceptions.

SB 176.summary: This bill would establish the 'Victims of Wrongful Incarceration Compensation Act' to provide compensation for people who were wrongfully incarcerated.

SB 177.summary: The bill would require agents of hostile foreign principals and foreign supported political organizations to register with the State Ethics Commission and provide registration requirements.

SB 178.summary: This bill would allow the State Depository Board to permit the state treasurer to invest in Bitcoin, set a limit on such investments, and establish requirements for safely handling and loaning these assets.

SB 179.summary: This bill would require a student's previous school to send the student's academic and disciplinary records to the new school within five days of the transfer. It also reduces the number of days a parent or guardian has to receive copies of these records.

SB 18.summary: The bill would revise provisions related to daily expense accounts for members of the General Assembly.

SB 180.summary: The bill would allow apprenticeship sponsors to enter into contracts with the State Board of the Technical College System of Georgia for the High Demand Apprenticeship Program. It also provides for completion awards for sponsors who successfully complete these contracts.

SB 181.summary: The bill would prevent public schools and public postsecondary institutions from accepting funding from or entering into contracts with foreign adversaries.

SB 182.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Music Office within the Department of Community Affairs to promote and support the music industry in Georgia.

SB 183.summary: The bill would exempt certain baby products from sales and use taxes.

SB 184.summary: The bill would require a person cited for unlawful squatting to show certain documentation. It also changes the penalty for forgery cases related to unlawful squatting.

SB 185.summary: This bill would stop the use of state funds or resources for certain treatments for state inmates.

SB 186.summary: The bill would allow assisted living communities and personal care homes to enroll as Medicaid providers. It also directs the development of a model for implementation and the submission of a state plan amendment or waiver if needed.

SB 187.summary: This bill would increase the amount of tax credits available for qualified caregiving expenses.

SB 188.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Adult and Aging Services Agency and the Georgia Adult and Aging Services Board. It also sets out the duties and powers of the board and the executive director of the agency.

SB 189.summary: This bill would have the Department of Community Affairs build and run a free-to-search public website of legal notices that the law now requires to be published in a newspaper. It would depend on funding from the General Assembly. Posting on the site would be required in addition to newspaper publication. In some cases, such as when a county's legal newspaper has no local office, a posting could replace newspaper publication.

SB 19.summary: The bill would require a ten-day waiting period for the purchase or transfer of certain firearms, with some exceptions, and set criminal penalties for violations.

SB 190.summary: The bill would provide fee waivers for active duty military members, veterans, and their family members at parks, historic areas, memorials, and recreation sites.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 191.summary: The bill would revise certain notice provisions related to benefits and appeals in employment security.

SB 192.summary: The bill would require the Department of Insurance to implement a program to help make health insurance more affordable after certain Affordable Care Act tax credits expire.

SB 193.summary: The bill would allow the State Board of the Technical College System of Georgia to create a program for adults to earn a high school diploma. It would also set rules for third-party providers who run the program and decide how to give them money.

SB 194.summary: This bill would allow people to make distilled spirits at home, set limits on how much they can make, and say they cannot sell what they make. It also allows for limited transportation and delivery of the spirits.

SB 195.summary: This bill would allow pharmacists to dispense preexposure prophylaxis and postexposure prophylaxis under certain conditions.

SB 196.summary: The bill would prohibit limited services pregnancy centers from advertising false or misleading information about the products or services they provide. It also sets out enforcement procedures, penalties, and legal actions.

SB 197.summary: The bill would repeal a grant program related to pregnancy and parenting funded by the Department of Public Health.

SB 198.summary: The bill would allow the board of trustees of the Georgia Legislative Retirement System to increase benefit multipliers for members and maintain a minimum 120 percent funded ratio. It also provides for automatic increases in employee contributions proportional to the benefit multiplier increases.

SB 199.summary: The bill would prevent the State Ethics Commission from accepting or rejecting complaints against candidates 60 days before an election. It also changes how income is reported on personal financial disclosure statements for office holders and restricts the release of home address information.

SB 2.summary: This bill would exclude tips from state income tax. Employers would need to report tips to the state. The bill defines what tips are and sets an effective date.

SB 20.summary: This bill would provide student loan repayment for veterinarians who practice shelter medicine or in nonprofit pet sterilization clinics. It also creates the State Veterinary Education Board for Shelter Medicine and Pet Sterilization.

SB 200.summary: The bill would amend Georgia law to state that life is valued and protected from the moment of conception, and that each life from that moment has the same rights and protections as other persons.

SB 201.summary: The bill would provide increased consumer protection for homeowners who enter into contracts with contractors after natural disasters. It sets certain contractual requirements and notice language.

SB 202.summary: The bill would change discovery rules for misdemeanor cases, allowing defendants to opt into reciprocal discovery similar to felony cases and requiring defendants to provide a list of witness and alibi information to the prosecuting attorney.

SB 203.summary: The bill would allow electric utility customers to aggregate demand from multiple locations and subscribe to off-site solar facilities. It also provides for nondiscriminatory interconnection of these facilities and consumer protections for customers.

SB 204.summary: The bill would allow the district attorney to charge certain felony and misdemeanor cases by accusation if they are not serious violent felonies, sexual felonies, or other specific offenses.

SB 205.summary: The bill would require insurance policies to cover healthcare services for pediatric autoimmune neuropsychiatric disorders associated with streptococcal infection (PANDAS) and pediatric acute onset neuropsychiatric disorders (PANS).

SB 206.summary: The bill would create the South Georgia Energy Authority, define its purpose, and outline its powers and responsibilities. It would also allow the authority to issue revenue bonds and set rates and charges.

SB 207.summary: The bill would create a preclearance process for licensing boards and commissions when they consider applications or investigate individuals with criminal records.

SB 208.summary: This bill would allow and regulate sports betting in Georgia, including setting rules for taxing sports betting operations.

SB 209.summary: This bill would allow certain people who are required to join the Public School Employees Retirement System to instead join the Teachers Retirement System of Georgia. It also sets conditions and prevents the transfer of creditable service.

SB 21.summary: This bill would allow local governments and their officials and employees to be sued for violating laws that prohibit sanctuary policies related to immigration.

SB 210.summary: The bill would change how vacancies on the Douglas County Board of Commissioners are filled.

SB 211.summary: The bill would create the 'Autism Missing Person Alert System Act' to help find missing people with autism. It would require certain entities to work together to develop and activate the alert system.

SB 212.summary: This bill would stop schools from sharing public student directory information with political candidates, campaign committees, political action committees, political organizations, or people or groups working for them.

SB 213.summary: The bill would ban commercial cheating services that target students and people seeking professional licenses as unfair and deceptive practices.

SB 214.summary: This bill would allow voters to cast physical absentee on-request ballots as an alternative to other in-person voting methods. It also sets procedures for the form, collection, and tabulation of these ballots, and updates reporting requirements to include these ballots.

SB 215.summary: The bill would amend the responsibilities of the administrative arm of the Supreme Court regarding the practice of law in Georgia. It also repeals provisions for the establishment of a unified self-governing bar association known as the 'State Bar of Georgia.'

SB 216.summary: This bill would allow the director of the Prosecuting Attorneys Qualifications Commission to join the Georgia Judicial Retirement System. It also provides for an election for current employees to join the system, the transfer of funds, and the payment of actuarial costs.

SB 217.summary: The bill would provide for school lunch and breakfast programs for public school students in Georgia, requiring local school systems to maximize access to federal funding and encouraging participation in the USDA's Community Eligibility Provision.

SB 218.summary: The bill would assign the Prosecuting Attorneys Qualifications Commission to the Administrative Office of the Courts for administrative purposes and fund it through the judicial branch's budget.

SB 219.summary: The bill would allow employees with disabilities to use toilet facilities in retail stores. It also provides exceptions, immunity from liability, and a criminal penalty for violations.

SB 22.summary: The bill would require the Georgia Department of Education to publish federal guidance documents and related information that are relevant and applicable. It also requires the State School Superintendent to send an annual notice to certain committees and offices.

SB 220.summary: The bill would rename low THC oil as medical cannabis and clarify and revise criminal penalties related to public health and morals, controlled substances, and the Department of Public Health.

SB 221.summary: The bill would increase the number of education hours required for licensed massage therapists.

SB 222.summary: The bill would create the Commission for the Blind and the Visually Impaired and establish a complaint process for it. It also amends the role of the Georgia Vocational Rehabilitation Agency in relation to blind persons and others.

SB 223.summary: The bill would limit the liability of landowners and occupiers for premises liability actions unless claimants can show certain facts. It also provides for affirmative defenses and rebuttable presumptions.

SB 224.summary: This bill would establish a voluntary do not sell list for firearms. It would provide procedures and conditions for registering and removing names from the list, along with penalties for violations. The bill also limits the records related to registration or removal.

SB 225.summary: This bill would prohibit educational institutions receiving state financial assistance from discriminating against students based on their race due to protective hairstyles or hair length in dress or grooming policies.

SB 226.summary: The bill would create the Peach State Saves program, a retirement savings plan for workers. It would define the program, appoint a board of trustees, and set rules for participant confidentiality and liability.

SB 227.summary: This bill would provide protections for freelance workers under labor and industrial relations laws.

SB 228.summary: This bill would allow the state treasurer to invest in bitcoin and develop policies for handling it.

SB 229.summary: This bill would stop wholesale dealers of alcoholic beverages from getting licenses to sell consumable hemp products and would also prevent them from selling or distributing such products.

SB 23.summary: The bill would increase the limit on the total percentage of funds that the Employees' Retirement System of Georgia can invest in alternative investments.

SB 230.summary: This bill would remove the limit on the maximum amount of insurance deductibles that condominium unit owners must pay.

SB 231.summary: This bill would limit the liability of firearms manufacturers, trade associations, owners or operators of sport shooting ranges, and dealers for the unlawful, intentional, or negligent acts of third parties involving the use of weapons, firearms, or ammunition.

SB 232.summary: The bill would require the destruction of a firearm that was discharged at a person under 18 years of age.

SB 233.summary: This bill changes the Behavioral Health Reform and Innovation Commission. It raises the commission from 24 to 30 members and adds seats such as people with lived experience of addiction or overdose loss and disability-related roles. It renames the subcommittees, replacing two with Addictive Diseases and Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities. It also moves the commission's end date from June 30, 2025, to December 31, 2026.

SB 234.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from City of Dalton independent school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes. The exemption amount would be the difference between the current year's assessed value and the adjusted base year's assessed value of a homestead.

SB 235.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from Whitfield County school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes. The exemption would be equal to the amount by which the current year's assessed value of a homestead exceeds the adjusted base year's assessed value.

SB 236.summary: The bill would allow students whose parents or guardians are on active duty in the U.S. armed forces to enroll in the public school of the attendance zone where they intend to live, without needing to have a lease, own a house, or secure other residency requirements.

SB 237.summary: The bill would revise provisions related to contracts and borrowing of funds for the Newton County Public Facilities Authority. It also updates rules about revenue bonds, credit not pledged, and asset distribution upon dissolution of the authority.

SB 238.summary: This bill would increase the Rockdale County Board of Commissioners from its current size to five members. It also revises the roles of the chairperson and county manager and provides for initial terms of office.

SB 239.summary: The bill would remove the requirement that funeral directors in Georgia must be licensed embalmers.

SB 24.summary: The bill would extend preferential assessment periods for certain historic properties. It affects property owners with historic properties.

SB 240.summary: The bill would designate April of each year as Georgia Native Plant Month.

SB 241.summary: The bill would allow funeral directors to use organic human reduction as a method to dispose of deceased human bodies and fetuses, requiring a disposition permit for this process.

SB 242.summary: This bill would place a monument in honor of Justice Clarence Thomas within the Nathan Deal Judicial Center and provide for the duties and responsibilities of the Capitol Art Standards Commission.

SB 243.summary: The bill would revise how money from the Back the Blue Fund can be used and how it is collected. It also states the legislative intent behind these changes.

SB 244.summary: This bill would allow a defendant in a criminal case to receive reasonable attorney's fees and costs if they successfully move to disqualify the prosecutor for misconduct.

SB 245.summary: This bill would allow grandparents to seek to revoke or amend an existing grandparent visitation order.

SB 246.summary: The bill would amend laws related to persons and their rights, the Juvenile Code, offenses against public health, domestic relations, education, and health.

SB 247.summary: The bill would increase the number of accumulated sick leave days that teachers and other school personnel can take each school year for personal or professional reasons from three to five days.

SB 248.summary: The bill would establish the Georgia Council on Library Materials Standards and require it to set standards for designating restricted materials in local school boards. It also provides definitions for terms like 'harmful to minors,' 'restricted materials,' and 'sexually explicit materials.'

SB 249.summary: Starting in the 2031-2032 school year, a computer science course will be required for high school graduation.

SB 25.summary: The bill would provide procedures for when a person is denied parole after completing certain prerequisites. It would allow for a video conference hearing for prospective parolees and require the board to submit written findings if the tentative parole month is delayed.

SB 250.summary: The bill would create the Wesley's Law Grant Program and set its purpose. It also requires the Department of Education to seek funding for the program from the Georgia Opioid Crisis Abatement Trust.

SB 251.summary: The bill would amend the Fair Business Practices Act of 1975 to encourage transparency and fairness in rent pricing for residential properties. It would prohibit landlords from not disclosing the total rental price and from charging deceptive fees.

SB 252.summary: The bill would allow independent school systems to receive municipal property interests and would require municipalities to replace any property that is conveyed to the school systems.

SB 253.summary: The bill would create a three-year pilot program for robotics in eligible public schools, with the State Board of Education setting rules and assessing the program's impact.

SB 254.summary: The bill would set milligram limits on delta-9-THC in consumable hemp products under the Georgia Hemp Farming Act.

SB 255.summary: This bill would allow certain committees of the Georgia General Assembly to have statutory investigatory powers, including the ability to issue oaths and subpoenas. It also sets rules for the confidentiality of materials related to these investigations.

SB 256.summary: This bill would require electric membership corporations to disclose certain acquisitions and other information to their members within a specific time frame.

SB 257.summary: This bill would allow local governments to create and run programs to help families find affordable housing. It also sets rules for reporting and determining the median income for households.

SB 258.summary: The bill would establish a grant program to support midwife-led birth centers and regulate midwives. It would also repeal existing provisions related to midwifery practice.

SB 259.summary: The bill would change procedures in the Juvenile Code when there is a suspicion of child abuse or neglect. It requires a physician who temporarily takes custody of a child due to suspected abuse or neglect to give certain information to the child's parent or legal guardian and to the Division of Family and Children Services.

SB 26.summary: The bill would require the state revenue commissioner to adjust the amount of military retirement income excluded from Georgia taxable net income based on a cost-of-living adjustment.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 260.summary: The bill would create the Central State Hospital Redevelopment Authority and give it powers and duties. It would also set rules for the authority's members and prohibit certain interests for employees and members.

SB 261.summary: The bill would provide for an early retirement benefit for magistrates and increase employee contributions. It also changes how the maximum monthly compensation and years of service are calculated for benefits.

SB 262.summary: The bill would require health benefit policies to cover preventive services without cost-sharing requirements and ensure the eligibility of health savings accounts. It would also be reviewed by the Commissioner of Insurance.

SB 263.summary: The bill would expand the jurisdictional authority of certain law enforcement officers to include a specified area surrounding school property.

SB 264.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Resilience Office under the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency. It would establish a board of directors, define their duties, and provide for hiring staff and funding.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 265.summary: The bill would require health benefit policies to cover medically necessary orthotic devices and prosthetic devices, including their materials and components.

SB 266.summary: The bill would increase the maximum amount of contributions allowed per beneficiary for the Georgia Higher Education Savings Plan and adjust the tax deduction for contributions to savings trust accounts.

SB 267.summary: The bill would require the State's Employee Benefit Plan Council to establish health savings accounts and provide for education or salary reductions for these accounts.

SB 268.summary: The bill would create a new crime called interference with a first responder and set penalties for it.

SB 269.summary: The bill would change procedures and notifications for involuntary outpatient commitments for people with mental illness.

SB 27.summary: The bill would create a new offense called doxxing, which involves releasing someone's personal information online with the intent to cause harm or distress. It also sets penalties for this offense and allows for protective orders and civil actions.

SB 270.summary: The bill would limit the effective date of rules or regulations adopted by the State Election Board before a general primary, general election, or runoff. It also requires notice to candidates and poll watchers for these events and revises some reporting requirements for advance voting.

SB 271.summary: The bill would create a permanent list of voters who choose to vote by absentee ballot. It would also set procedures for maintaining this list.

SB 272.summary: The bill would stop landlords from asking tenants for income information. It also lets tenants withhold rent under certain conditions and bans certain late fees. The bill covers issues like habitability and prohibits retaliation against tenants.

SB 273.summary: The bill would revise Georgia's minimum wage law, increase the minimum wage, and provide annual increases to match the rising cost of living. It also includes a credit for employers of tipped workers and removes some eligibility exemptions from the minimum wage.

SB 274.summary: The bill would allow people to register to vote and vote on the same day. It also sets procedures and notices for this process.

SB 275.summary: The bill would remove the State Board of Cosmetology and Barbers from the jurisdiction of the Secretary of State and place it under the Department of Public Health.

SB 276.summary: The bill would revise certain provisions related to recovery of medical assistance from third parties to comply with federal law. It also bars third-party payers from refusing payment solely because a healthcare item or service did not receive prior authorization.

SB 277.summary: The bill would revise the definition of drugs to include alcohol and its derivatives in drug abuse treatment and education programs.

SB 278.summary: The bill would require corn masa flour and wet corn masa products to contain a certain amount of folic acid and set labeling requirements for these products.

SB 279.summary: The bill would require the State Board of Workers' Compensation to notify the Department of Administrative Services when the board has reason to believe an injured worker is an eligible peace officer.

SB 28.summary: The bill would change procedures and processes for making laws and rules in Georgia. It affects how the General Assembly works and how health and state government operate.

SB 280.summary: The bill would set standards for when an employer or insurance provider is responsible for actions related to a commercial vehicle driver. It affects employers, insurance providers, and commercial vehicle drivers.

SB 281.summary: The bill would create the Port Wentworth Convention and Visitors Bureau Authority, setting out how the authority is run and its duties.

SB 282.summary: The bill would add requirements for earned wage access services, set fees for these services, and provide consumer protections. It also states that earned wage access payments are nonrecourse and are not considered lending activities.

SB 283.summary: This bill would remove the Department of Public Safety's authority to set reasonable rates, fares, and charges for motor carriers transporting household goods.

SB 284.summary: The bill would allow the Commissioner of Securities to order people who have violated securities rules to return money to investors, customers, or clients who paid for securities.

SB 285.summary: The bill would increase the percentage of 9-1-1 charges that are sent to the Peace Officers' Annuity and Benefit Fund.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 286.summary: The bill would provide for substance abuse and mental health treatment programs in county and municipal jails for inmates and applicants. It also establishes procedures for voluntary admission into drug court and mental health court divisions.

SB 287.summary: The bill would create and establish a purpose for the Georgia Interested Parties Advisory Group within the Department of Community Health. It would also define the group's composition and duties.

SB 288.summary: The bill would prohibit certain medical examinations on patients who are anesthetized or unconscious without prior informed consent.

SB 289.summary: The bill would define what 'formal charges' means when talking about ethical violations by members of certain boards, commissions, or authorities.

SB 29.summary: The bill would require individuals arrested for a felony to provide DNA samples when they are booked or processed by a detention facility.

SB 290.summary: This bill would create a certification program for community health workers in Georgia. It would establish the Georgia Community Health Worker Certification Committee to oversee the program.

SB 291.summary: The bill would create a new 'America First' specialty license plate in Georgia. The proceeds from the sale of these plates would go to the general fund.

SB 292.summary: This bill would change where certain Georgia-based corporations can be sued. If a corporation has its main office in Georgia, it can be sued in the county where that main office is located.

SB 293.summary: The bill would increase the number of free license plates issued to certain veterans.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 294.summary: This bill would allow retail dealers in distilled spirits to sell consumable hemp products.

SB 295.summary: This bill would require local school systems to keep and publish a list of all contracts worth more than $10,000 that use state funds.

SB 296.summary: The bill would establish new offenses for operating a school bus while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, and for endangering school bus occupants while under the influence of alcohol or drugs. It would also set penalties for these offenses.

SB 297.summary: The bill would create an exemption from sales and use taxes for certain menstrual discharge collection devices.

SB 298.summary: The bill would amend procedures for appeals when the state denies sovereign immunity or other immunities available to it.

SB 299.summary: The bill would allow members of the armed forces on active duty to use online notaries public for certain matters.

SB 3.summary: The bill would add new qualifications regarding convictions for district attorneys, assistant district attorneys, deputy district attorneys, and other attorneys employed by district attorneys.

SB 30.summary: The bill would prohibit doctors and hospitals from prescribing or administering hormone therapies and puberty-blocking medications to minors for certain purposes.

SB 300.summary: The bill would create a program to provide grant funds to public schools to pay student teachers during their required student teaching period as part of their teacher education programs.

SB 301.summary: The bill would revise provisions to protect government statues, monuments, plaques, banners, and other commemorative symbols.

SB 302.summary: This bill would create a 10 percent homestead exemption from Peach County ad valorem taxes for county purposes for residents of Peach County.

SB 303.summary: The bill would change the state-wide system for voting equipment to require hand-marked and hand-counted paper ballots. It also moves the responsibility for certifying and selecting this system from the Secretary of State to the State Election Board.

SB 304.summary: This bill would allow direct payments to property owners whose property was damaged or destroyed by a specific natural disaster.

SB 305.summary: This bill would create a special license plate honoring alumni of Alabama State University in Georgia.

SB 306.summary: This bill would require notices about the impending expiration of preferential assessment for conservation use property to be sent via certified mail. It also allows for the reinstatement of certain covenants and preferential assessments under specific circumstances and provides for appeals and refunds.

SB 307.summary: The bill would require all physicians to complete one hour of continuing education on maternal health as part of their continuing education requirements.

SB 308.summary: The bill would provide Medicaid coverage for postpartum maternal mental health care services.

SB 309.summary: The bill would repeal Chapter 2B of Title 20, which includes the Georgia Education Savings Authority and the Georgia Promise Scholarship Act.

SB 31.summary: This bill would exempt from income tax all retirement benefits received from service in the armed forces of the United States or the reserve components.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 310.summary: The bill would create the CHANGE Task Force to look at issues in urban, suburban, and rural communities and find solutions related to labor and community development.

SB 311.summary: The bill would add new requirements for ride share network services and transportation referral services to improve driver safety and protect the privacy of drivers and passengers.

SB 312.summary: The bill would establish the Georgia Peach Walk of Fame Advisory Council within the Department of Economic Development. It sets criteria for membership, outlines the election of officers, and specifies the terms and meeting frequency for the council.

SB 313.summary: The bill would allow investigations or inspections of certain residential rental properties if there is a reasonable suspicion of a code violation. It also requires the registration of certain residential rental property.

SB 314.summary: The bill would establish a program to import wholesale prescription drugs and set procedures for implementing the program.

SB 315.summary: This bill would require property owners' associations to provide certain disclosures and documents before a lot sale is finalized.

SB 316.summary: The bill would allow the Probate Court of Clinch County to charge a technology fee and specify how the money from this fee can be used.

SB 317.summary: The bill would allow the Magistrate Court of Clinch County to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used and managed.

SB 318.summary: This bill would make certain agreements involving parallel pricing coordination unenforceable contracts in general restraint of trade for residential rental properties. It also provides for a civil penalty and educational materials for residents.

SB 319.summary: The bill would establish a standard for state, county, and local law enforcement agencies to follow when deciding whether to engage in vehicular pursuits.

SB 32.summary: The bill would require a mandatory minimum sentence for people convicted of using violence against law enforcement officers while obstructing or hindering them.

SB 320.summary: The bill would create comprehensive state civil rights laws protecting individuals from discrimination in housing, public accommodations, and employment based on race, color, religion, sex, and sexual orientation.

SB 321.summary: This bill would exclude employees of employers covered by the federal Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act from Georgia's workers' compensation laws.

SB 322.summary: The bill would require the State Board of Education to include instruction on the proper use of school bus passenger restraint systems in its safety program. It also requires school buses to be equipped with passenger restraint systems.

SB 323.summary: This bill would require medically necessary tests for metal allergies and metal sensitivities before cardiovascular, dental, or orthopedic surgeries that involve inserting a metal implant. It also requires health benefit policies to cover these tests and sets cost-sharing requirements.

SB 324.summary: The bill would provide protections for life insurance policyholders and beneficiaries, including requiring an owner of a life insurance policy or annuity to be represented by a local agent when the policy or annuity is sold. It also requires the owner to be represented by a local agent even if the agent does not have a contract with the insurer. Additionally, the bill mandates an annual notice to the owner.

SB 325.summary: This bill would allow local school systems and public schools to hire or accept volunteers as school chaplains.

SB 326.summary: This bill would create a program to help blind and deaf-blind individuals find jobs and go to college by providing support service providers to assist them.

SB 327.summary: The bill would add a sixth judge to the superior courts in the Clayton Judicial Circuit.

SB 328.summary: The bill would add an additional judge to the State Court of Henry County. It also outlines how the initial additional judge will be appointed and how their successors will be elected. The terms of office for the additional judge and their successors are also provided.

SB 329.summary: The bill would provide the chief judge of the Flint Judicial Circuit with an additional annual stipend in addition to the county compensation they already receive.

SB 33.summary: The bill would set limits on the total THC concentration in consumable hemp products and revise the certificate of analysis requirements for these products.

SB 330.summary: The bill would provide a $50,000 homestead exemption from City of Atlanta independent school district property taxes for residents aged 65 or older, with a total exemption cap of $487,804,878.

SB 331.summary: This bill would repeal the existing joint airport authority for the City of Winder and the County of Barrow, established in 1958, and address the assets and liabilities of the authority.

SB 332.summary: The bill would change how members of the DeKalb County Board of Education are elected, specifying that they must be elected by electors of the DeKalb County school district.

SB 333.summary: The bill would provide a homestead exemption from City of Chickamauga independent school district property taxes for educational purposes. The exemption would be equal to the amount by which the current year's assessed value of a homestead exceeds its base year's assessed value.

SB 334.summary: The bill would provide a homestead exemption from City of Trion independent school district property taxes for educational purposes. The exemption would be for the amount by which the current year's assessed value of a homestead exceeds the base year's assessed value.

SB 335.summary: This bill would create a homestead exemption from Chattooga County school district property taxes for educational purposes. The exemption would be for the amount by which the current year's assessed value of a homestead exceeds the base year's assessed value.

SB 336.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from Dade County school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes. The exemption would be for the amount by which the current year's assessed value of a homestead exceeds the base year's assessed value.

SB 337.summary: The bill would change the electoral districts for the Macon Water Authority and set staggered terms for new members. It also provides for elections and a chairperson, and sets salaries for elected members and the chairperson.

SB 338.summary: The bill would increase term limits for the mayor of Macon, Payne City, and Bibb County, and remove term limits for commissioners in these areas.

SB 339.summary: The bill would provide for semiannual postretirement benefit adjustments for all beneficiaries of the Employees' Retirement System of Georgia.

SB 34.summary: This bill would stop electric utilities from including certain costs related to providing electricity to commercial data centers in their rates unless those rates are designed to recover costs mainly from the data centers.

SB 340.summary: The bill would provide for the selection of a mayor pro tem for the City of Tybee Island, define the duties of the mayor pro tem, and outline how to fill a vacancy in this position.

SB 341.summary: The bill would protect the exercise of constitutional rights and prohibit discrimination in the provision of essential services. It also allows for public and private enforcement.

SB 342.summary: The bill would increase the percentage of 9-1-1 charges that are remitted to the Peace Officers' Annuity and Benefit Fund.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 343.summary: The bill would stop providers of social media platforms from allowing minors aged 14 years or younger to create accounts.

SB 344.summary: The bill would allow the Probate Court of Crawford County to charge a technology fee and specify how the money from this fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover funds once the fee is no longer collected.

SB 345.summary: The bill would allow the Magistrate Court of Crawford County to charge a technology fee and specify how the fee can be used. It also outlines what happens to any leftover funds after the fee is no longer collected.

SB 346.summary: This bill changes how DeKalb County pays certain officials. It sets the salaries of the CEO, sheriff, clerk of superior court, tax commissioner, and county commissioners as percentages of a "gross salary" figure. Judges of the State, Juvenile, and Probate Courts, the chief magistrate, and the solicitor-general get the higher of $208,040 or 90 percent of that figure. It also sets associate magistrate pay and renames the Stone Mountain Judicial Circuit the DeKalb Judicial Circuit.

SB 347.summary: The bill would change the way members of the Brunswick and Glynn County Development Authority are appointed, alter the term of their office, and set new qualifications for membership.

SB 348.summary: This bill changes how Hancock County's four commissioner districts are described, using a new map named in the bill. The chairperson is still elected by the whole county. Current commissioners stay in office until their terms end, and districts 1 through 4 keep their numbers under the new descriptions. The bill takes effect July 1, 2025.

SB 349.summary: This bill would allow the governing authority of Hancock County to levy an excise tax as specified in a certain section of the O.C.G.A.

SB 35.summary: The bill would increase the number of days that homeowners' insurance policyholders must be notified before their policies are not renewed.

SB 350.summary: This bill changes how much certain DeKalb County officials and judges are paid. It sets salaries for officials such as the Chief Executive Officer, District Attorney, Sheriff, Clerk of the Superior Court, Tax Commissioner, and county commissioners as percentages of a base "gross salary." It also sets pay for several judges, the Chief Magistrate, and the Solicitor-General, and for associate magistrates. It updates references to the Stone Mountain Judicial Circuit, now called the DeKalb Judicial Circuit.

SB 351.summary: The bill would change the salary of the judge and solicitor-general for the State Court of Treutlen in Treutlen County.

SB 352.summary: The bill would provide a homestead exemption of $40,000 from Jasper County school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes for residents aged 65 or older.

SB 353.summary: This bill would allow county or joint boards of election or boards of election and registration to hold meetings via teleconference.

SB 354.summary: The bill would create a legal cause of action for individuals whose identity indicators are used without permission. It also provides for protection against the unauthorized use of identity indicators, allows for the assignment or licensing of this right, and sets out damages and other remedies. Exceptions are also provided.

SB 355.summary: This bill would create a homestead exemption from Paulding County school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes. The exemption would be for the amount by which the current year's assessed value of a homestead exceeds its adjusted base year assessed value.

SB 356.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from Polk County school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes. The exemption would be for 50 percent or $60,000 of the assessed value for residents 65 years or older, and 75 percent or $80,000 for residents 70 years or older.

SB 357.summary: The bill would allow challenges to the qualifications of people applying to register to vote or already registered. It would specify the grounds for these challenges and the required documentation.

SB 358.summary: The bill would revise the administrative procedures for verifying ethics complaints in DeKalb County.

SB 359.summary: The bill would revise and restate provisions regarding the code of ethics for the Board of Commissioners of Henry County. It also revises provisions related to the chairperson of the board and the county manager.

SB 36.summary: The bill would amend Title 50 of the Official Code of Georgia to provide for the preservation of religious freedom and the granting of relief related to religious freedom.

SB 360.summary: The bill would create a public option buy-in program to provide healthcare coverage to individuals who are not eligible for Medicaid or enrollment through a health exchange.

SB 361.summary: The bill would allow property owners' associations to place liens and use assessments. It also requires these associations to register and sets rules for administrative hearings and escrow of funds.

SB 362.summary: The bill would allow sworn law enforcement officers and the commissioner and deputy commissioner of the Department of Public Safety to retire at age 55 and receive certain disability benefits and provisions for purchasing creditable service.

SB 363.summary: The bill would restrict voting rights for people who are judicially determined to be incompetent.

SB 364.summary: The bill would add new penalties for insurance companies that knowingly provide false or misleading information to the Commissioner of Insurance if that information affects insurance premium rates.

SB 365.summary: The bill would enhance transparency in the marketing of produce and meat in Georgia.

SB 366.summary: The bill would allow ivermectin to be sold as an over-the-counter medication in Georgia. It would also remove ivermectin from the list of dangerous drugs.

SB 367.summary: The bill would exempt health care facilities, services, and equipment dedicated exclusively to treating cancer from certificate of need requirements.

SB 368.summary: The bill would create the Northeast Regional Water Authority and allow it to build or buy regional water supply reservoirs. It also sets rules for legal actions related to the authority and requires financial statements and audits.

SB 369.summary: The bill would amend the Charter Schools Act of 1998 to provide for completion charter schools, set rules and performance standards, and allow existing charter schools to convert to completion charter schools.

SB 37.summary: The bill would require all governmental entities to develop and maintain plans for using artificial intelligence systems and create the Georgia Board for Artificial Intelligence.

SB 370.summary: This bill would change election rules to require closed primaries, where only registered party members can vote in a party's primary election. It also includes provisions for checking voter affiliation before issuing absentee ballots and maintaining lists of voter affiliations.

SB 371.summary: The bill would create a grant program to establish peer support programs in hospitals and penal institutions for individuals. It also requires quarterly and annual reports on the programs.

SB 372.summary: The bill would remove references to reputational risk from guidance, rules, examination manuals, and similar documents of the Department of Banking and Finance. It also prohibits the department from considering reputational risk when regulating financial institutions.

SB 373.summary: This bill would allow notarial acts to be performed using electronic means when certain requirements are met.

SB 374.summary: This bill would allow local fire ordinances to require fire sprinklers in certain multifamily dwellings.

SB 375.summary: This bill would require certain state agencies to consider a definition of hinduphobia when applying laws and regulations that prohibit discrimination based on race, color, religion, or national origin. It also allows fact finders in criminal cases to consider hinduphobia when determining a defendant's intent.

SB 376.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Restaurant Franchise Relations Act, which would set rules for when a franchisor can terminate a franchise agreement and conditions for arbitration and renewal. It would also prohibit franchisor discrimination against franchisees.

SB 377.summary: This bill would allow curbside voting for voters who cannot enter a polling place or wait in line due to a disability or age. It also sets procedures for the form, collection, and tabulation of ballots for these voters and establishes a pilot program.

SB 378.summary: The bill would prohibit leadership committees and lobbying activities by organizations that receive public funds.

SB 379.summary: The bill would require the Department of Insurance to implement a program to make health insurance more affordable after the expiration of certain Affordable Care Act tax credits.

SB 38.summary: The bill would allow for development impact fees to be used for education purposes. It provides definitions, methods for calculating, imposing, and collecting these fees.

SB 380.summary: The bill would allow for the appropriation of funds to get federal financial help for payments to providers of Medicaid expansion.

SB 381.summary: The bill would provide grants to local school districts for students living in poverty. It also sets rules for how the grant funds must be used.

SB 382.summary: This bill would make the state-wide base year homestead exemption mandatory for all political subdivisions, and it would repeal a related tax bill requirement.

SB 383.summary: The bill would change how local child fatality review committees work, add new members to these committees, and set training requirements. It also clarifies which child deaths are reviewed and modifies the deadlines and requirements for reports related to child deaths.

SB 384.summary: This bill would allow certain motor vehicles to have a five-year registration and revalidation period instead of the usual shorter period.

SB 385.summary: The bill would abolish the office of administration floor leaders in the Georgia General Assembly.

SB 386.summary: This bill would stop paying daily expense allowances to members of the General Assembly for days when a roll call is not held. Members would need to be present for the roll call and all votes to get these allowances.

SB 387.summary: The bill would repeal the state income tax in Georgia and eliminate various income tax credits.

SB 388.summary: The bill would prevent people from being jailed for certain code violations related to buildings and housing. It also sets rules for when emergency circumstances can be considered in code enforcement.

SB 389.summary: The bill would require covered immigration officers to wear visible identification during public immigration enforcement functions and prohibit them from wearing face coverings during these functions.

SB 39.summary: The bill would stop the state health benefit plan and any state funds from covering expenses for gender-affirming care.

SB 390.summary: This bill would prohibit other states' armed military forces from deploying into Georgia without the Governor's permission, with an exception provided for.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 391.summary: The bill would prohibit activities related to immigration enforcement in certain locations without a judicial warrant. This prohibition would apply to federal, state, and local government employees.

SB 392.summary: The bill would change how the state budget is made by using zero-base budgeting, which means every program must prove its value each year. It affects how state departments and programs are funded.

SB 393.summary: This bill would stop property owners' associations from enforcing traffic laws, ordinances, or regulations. It also allows these associations to ask law enforcement agencies to enforce traffic rules within their areas.

SB 394.summary: This bill would remove a fee for operating alternative fueled vehicles and make related changes to motor vehicle registration and licensing laws.

SB 395.summary: The bill would require doctors to give the Georgia Composite Medical Board information when they certify someone as eligible for the Low THC Oil Patient Registry. It also requires annual reporting and allows the Department of Public Health to share certain information.

SB 396.summary: The bill would prohibit employers from taking retaliatory actions against employees who disclose potentially unlawful activities.

SB 397.summary: The bill would provide remedies for state citizens whose constitutional rights are deprived by civil immigration enforcement officers. It would also define terms related to this issue and give the legislation a short title.

SB 398.summary: The bill would make it a crime to use generative artificial intelligence to create images of individuals without their permission or knowledge. It also establishes new criminal offenses related to virtual peeping.

SB 399.summary: The bill would require notification to public safety answering points about the location of automated external defibrillators (AEDs) and provide for rules and regulations and training related to AEDs. It also amends provisions related to the employment and training of peace officers.

SB 4.summary: The bill would revise the roles of local boards of education and local school superintendents and set requirements for a model code of ethics for local boards of education.

SB 40.summary: The bill changes how used, detached catalytic converters are treated under the rules for secondary metals recyclers. It also sets registration requirements for these recyclers.

SB 400.summary: This bill would stop unaccredited institutions from offering degrees. It also requires certain institutions to join the Tuition Guaranty Trust Fund and explains how they can do so.

SB 401.summary: The bill would require local boards of education to teach firearm safety in grades K through 12. This instruction can be included in health and physical education classes.

SB 402.summary: The bill would create a pilot program to provide screenings, clinical evaluations, training, services, and resources for autism spectrum disorder to children in foster care.

SB 403.summary: The bill would change when property is considered abandoned and add exceptions. It also deals with the abandonment and liquidation of virtual currency and allows for delays in publishing notices on the Georgia Unclaimed Property List under certain conditions.

SB 404.summary: The bill would make joint legal and physical custody the default arrangement in child custody proceedings, with a presumption that it is in the best interests of the child. An exception to this presumption is provided.

SB 405.summary: The bill would increase the maximum amount of civil claims that can be tried in magistrate court.

SB 406.summary: This bill would require property owners' associations to register and renew their registration. It also establishes a State Board for Review of Complaints Regarding Property Owners' Associations to handle appeals and complaints.

SB 407.summary: This bill would provide a homestead exemption from Cherokee County school district ad valorem taxes for educational purposes through the tax year 2031.

SB 408.summary: This bill would extend the end date for a tax exemption on equipment used in data centers.

SB 409.summary: The bill would provide protections for homeowners regarding insurance companies' use of aerial or satellite images. It would require insurance companies to give homeowners 60 days to correct any issues found in the images.

SB 41.summary: The bill would provide equal athletic opportunities for public school students in Georgia.

SB 410.summary: This bill would repeal the sales and use tax exemption for data center equipment in Georgia. It allows certificates of exemption issued before the repeal date to still be used.

SB 411.summary: The bill would allow certain licensed professionals to perform dry needling and set education and training requirements for occupational therapists to do so. It also restricts how these professionals can represent and advertise their ability to perform dry needling.

SB 412.summary: The bill would increase the number of accumulated sick leave days that teachers and other school personnel can take each school year from three to five days for personal or professional reasons.

SB 413.summary: This bill would allow tenants or legal occupants of a residence to terminate their rental or lease agreement if they experienced residential firearm violence or reasonably fear such violence. It requires written notice.

SB 414.summary: The bill would amend the Fair Business Practices Act of 1975 to require landlords to disclose the total rental price of residential properties and prohibit hidden fees.

SB 415.summary: The bill would ban the production, sale, trade, distribution, or offering of lab-grown meat for human consumption in Georgia.

SB 416.summary: The bill would prohibit third-party hotel booking websites from falsely claiming they are affiliated with hotels. It would also consider such misrepresentation an unfair and deceptive trade practice.

SB 417.summary: This bill would allow public employees to organize and bargain collectively with the state. It also repeals certain sections related to collective bargaining and firefighter working conditions.

SB 418.summary: This bill would create a legal way for individuals to sue someone who uses their photograph or image with representations of nudity or sexually explicit conduct without permission and with the intent to harm.

SB 419.summary: This bill would require peace officers to receive training on interacting with people who have non-apparent disabilities. It also allows for a notation about such disabilities to be placed on driver's licenses and identification cards.

SB 42.summary: The bill would repeal certain penalty provisions for crimes related to prostitution, keeping a place of prostitution, pimping, and pandering.

SB 420.summary: The bill would establish fees for reef and migratory fish endorsements. It also amends rules and regulations related to the Environmental Protection Division and permit applications.

SB 421.summary: This bill would stop local governments, authorities, and political subdivisions from making agreements that prevent the disclosure of electricity and water usage data.

SB 422.summary: This bill would change the date of most municipal elections to even-numbered years and extend the terms of office for most municipal officers for one year during the transition to the new election cycle.

SB 423.summary: The bill would stop candidates, campaign committees, independent committees, political action committees, and leadership committees from getting more than 50% of their money from people who are not from Georgia.

SB 424.summary: This bill would allow gold and silver to be used as legal tender and establish guidelines for a bullion depository and an electronic payment system. It also prohibits social credit scoring systems and requires annual reports.

SB 425.summary: The bill would require all schools that receive state funding and have students in grades three through five to teach cursive handwriting to all students by the end of third grade.

SB 426.summary: The bill would require high school students seeking a diploma and individuals seeking a high school equivalency diploma to score at least 70 percent on the United States Citizenship Civics Test.

SB 427.summary: The bill would allow certain internationally trained physicians to get limited provisional licenses and provide a pathway to full licensure in Georgia.

SB 428.summary: The bill directs the Department of Community Health to request a federal waiver to allow Medicaid reimbursement for certain home and community-based services.

SB 429.summary: The bill would change the monthly income requirement for disabled veterans to qualify as tenants in Georgia.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 43.summary: The bill would increase the maximum acreage of land that can qualify for preferential assessment and taxation as a bona fide conservation use property.

SB 430.summary: The bill would allow certain military museums to qualify as destination marketing organizations and private sector nonprofit organizations for tax purposes.

SB 431.summary: This bill would require schools to enroll foster care students within two school days of a request from the student's parent or legal custodian. It also includes provisions for reporting noncompliance and corrective action plans.

SB 432.summary: This bill would extend automatic repeals of certain provisions regarding nonlapsing revenue for institutions of the University System of Georgia and units of the Technical College System of Georgia.

SB 433.summary: The bill would provide special license plates for people with autism spectrum disorder or a developmental disability and for their spouse, parent, or legal guardian.

SB 434.summary: The bill would create the Office of Homeless Youth Prevention and Protection within the Department of Community Affairs. It would also establish the office's director, purpose, responsibilities, and an advisory committee.

SB 435.summary: The bill would rename the Georgia Development Authority as the Georgia Agricultural Development Authority and make related changes.

SB 436.summary: This bill would stop local governments and political subdivisions from making agreements that prevent the disclosure of electricity or water usage information for any entity.

SB 437.summary: This bill would allow an applicant to use a private professional provider for plan review or inspection, and the review or inspection could proceed even if the local governing authority had not done its own review or inspection.

SB 438.summary: The bill would change the age at which children must attend school from six to five years old and require all children to attend a full-day kindergarten program for one year before entering first grade.

SB 439.summary: The bill would regulate referral agencies for assisted living communities and personal care homes, requiring them to make certain disclosures to prospective residents and verify the licensing of the communities and homes.

SB 44.summary: The bill would change the definition of a 'qualified local school system' by lowering the minimum required millage rate from 14 mills to 10 mills. It also proposes a 25 percent reduction in equalization grant awards for local school systems that do not meet this new millage rate requirement.

SB 440.summary: The bill would update and modernize laws related to the duties and functions of the Department of Public Health.

SB 441.summary: The bill would require certain pooled investments by local governments to be approved by the State Depository Board. It also exempts some pooled investments from this requirement.

SB 442.summary: This bill would change how commercial drivers' licenses are handled for noncitizens in Georgia. It would allow for the revocation and expiration of these licenses for noncitizens and set testing requirements for renewing them.

SB 443.summary: This bill changes Georgia's law on blocking public passages. A person who, without legal authority, purposely or recklessly blocks a highway or street so it can't be used without unreasonable inconvenience or hazard, and then refuses to clear it after an official request or a peace officer's order, would be guilty of a high and aggravated misdemeanor. The person may also be held civilly liable for damages. Blocking a sidewalk or other public passage in the same way is a misdemeanor.

SB 444.summary: This bill would prevent insurance companies from making decisions about covering healthcare services based only on artificial intelligence systems or other software tools.

SB 445.summary: The bill would exclude public schools with a statewide attendance zone and certain charter schools from a separate list of public schools reported by the Office of Student Achievement for the Georgia Promise Scholarship Act.

SB 446.summary: The bill would allow Georgia to participate in a federal tax credit program for contributions to scholarship granting organizations.

SB 447.summary: The bill would revise provisions related to the denial or nonacceptance of permits for controlling soil erosion and sedimentation. It also provides general provisions for counties and municipalities regarding the acceptance, denial, or nonacceptance of these permits.

SB 448.summary: This bill would require certain senior living facilities to have and maintain emergency and standby power systems to ensure the safety and well-being of their residents.

SB 449.summary: This bill would require certain long-term care facilities to have enough emergency and standby power systems to provide care and services for their residents during power outages.

SB 45.summary: The bill would increase the maximum acreage of land that can qualify for preferential assessment and taxation as a conservation use property.

SB 450.summary: This bill would allow public libraries to keep and use opioid antagonists, such as naloxone, and let library staff administer them and carry them on their person.

SB 451.summary: The bill would require peace officers to receive training on evacuating people with disabilities during emergencies. It also updates emergency management procedures to include evacuation plans for people with disabilities, subject to funding.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 452.summary: The bill would increase the maximum employer contribution to a 401(k) plan for certain state law enforcement officers.

SB 453.summary: The bill would exempt certain rural residents from paying taxes on their income. It also sets out ways to prove residency and penalties for not following the rules.

SB 454.summary: This bill would allow the use of temporary door locking devices in public buildings during certain emergency situations. It also provides guidelines for using such devices and rules and regulations.

SB 455.summary: The bill would create the Georgia Artificial Intelligence Commission, define its responsibilities, and assign it to the Georgia Technology Authority. It also requires the commission to produce annual reports.

SB 456.summary: The bill would amend laws related to alcoholic beverages to regulate the manufacture, distribution, and sale of certain alcoholic beverages. It would also allow manufacturers of malt beverages to sell the beverages they produce, under certain conditions.

SB 457.summary: The bill would amend the law for the City of Mulberry to allow the city to provide services and exercise powers, establish a city manager position, and set staggered terms for councilmembers.

SB 458.summary: The bill would create a licensing system for home inspectors in Georgia, including requirements for education, insurance, and continuing education. It also allows for reciprocity of licenses and company licensing.

SB 459.summary: The bill would require children to attend kindergarten before enrolling in first grade, with some exceptions. It also provides funding for literacy coaches in public schools with students in kindergarten through third grade.

SB 46.summary: The bill would create a position within the Georgia Technology Authority to improve how the state government serves the public. The State of Georgia Government Service Delivery Lead would coordinate these efforts.

SB 460.summary: The bill would allow the Department of Community Health to determine and verify eligibility for Medicaid and manage Medicaid enrollment.

SB 461.summary: This bill would change the Department of Human Services to be the main state agency in charge of administering the Medicaid program, transferring certain responsibilities from the Department of Community Health.

SB 462.summary: The bill would provide insurance coverage for out-of-network ambulance transportation services and set minimum reimbursement rates and maximum copayments, coinsurance, or deductibles for such services.

SB 463.summary: This bill would stop business enterprises or those controlled by natural-born persons from owning more than 500 single-family residential properties. It also bans foreign investment vehicles from owning any interest in single-family rental properties.

SB 464.summary: The bill would stop federal immigration authorities from using certain technologies to identify individuals for specific purposes.

SB 465.summary: The bill would prevent business enterprises that hire illegal aliens for large-scale projects from claiming certain tax credits related to those projects.

SB 466.summary: This bill would require local boards of education to install key boxes at each school building, with locations chosen in collaboration with local law enforcement and emergency management agencies, if funding is available.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 467.summary: The bill would require procedures to validate the age of certain people using apps.

SB 468.summary: The bill would increase reporting requirements for sexual offenders, including monitoring homeless offenders more closely, requiring them to report international travel, and placing them in risk assessment classifications based on specific crimes.

SB 469.summary: The bill would set term limits for members of the Forsyth County Board of Commissioners.

SB 47.summary: This bill would exempt sales of firearms, ammunition, gun safes, and related accessories from sales and use taxes during an 11-day period each year.

SB 470.summary: The bill would make it illegal to possess, use, operate, manufacture, sell, offer for sale, distribute, or import signal jammers. It also allows the Attorney General to start forfeiture proceedings against those who violate the law.
subjects: MILITARY, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND VETERANS AFFAIRS

SB 471.summary: The bill would remove the automatic repeal provision from an existing law that allows local school boards to require students to wear face masks or face coverings on school property unless parents or guardians can opt their children out of this requirement.

SB 472.summary: The bill would allow for the suspension of members of local boards of education if there are audit findings or findings by the state auditor of financial mismanagement or misconduct.

SB 473.summary: The bill would require people applying for limited driving permits to submit proof that they have completed a certified DUI Alcohol or Drug Use Risk Reduction Program. It also requires completion of such a program for accepting a reduced plea for a DUI charge.

SB 474.summary: This bill would exclude overtime compensation from state income tax. It also requires employers to report this information and allows for rules and regulations to be made for this purpose.

SB 475.summary: The bill would require local boards of education to treat local charter schools no less favorably than other local schools when spending money from a special sales tax for education.

SB 476.summary: The bill would reduce the personal income tax rate in Georgia. It affects people who pay personal income taxes in the state.

SB 477.summary: The bill would reduce the personal income tax rate and the rates of taxation on corporate and partnership income. It would also increase the standard deduction from state taxable income for individuals.

SB 478.summary: The bill would amend the outdoor stewardship laws to include a sunset provision and increase the percentage of money appropriated. It affects the management of outdoor resources.

SB 479.summary: The bill would require local governing bodies for each school system and public school to adopt a policy allowing students at least one excused absence per school year for attending or participating in a civic or political event.
